Because of Tropical Storm Isaias's expected impact on the Gulf Coast, Florida A&M at Alabama State was moved up a day from Saturday, Oct. 10 to Friday, Oct. 9 at noon EDT (11 a.m. CDT). SWAC TV is carrying it.

FAMU comes in at 1-4 (0-1 SWAC). Alabama State is 3-2 (1-1 SWAC) and is playing at home for homecoming. Both teams are starting freshman quarterbacks in place of injured starters: Armond Parker for FAMU and Aaron Frye for Alabama State.

Alabama State lost its last game 16-10 to Bethune-Cookman in a Week 5 SWAC game.
Alabama State's 2026 results: beat Southern 30-17 (8/29), beat Lane 34-0 (9/5), lost at Troy 17-34 (9/12), beat Mississippi Valley State 41-15 (9/26), then lost to Bethune-Cookman 16-10.

Through five games FAMU has run for 242 yards (48.4 per game) and 2 TDs, which ranks 12th and last in the SWAC. Its offensive line is short on depth because of injuries. Alabama State's defense has 42 tackles for loss, 12 sacks and 3 INTs. FAMU has 14 sacks and 30 TFLs.
Last season Alabama State won 42-14 at FAMU on Sept 27, 2025.
In 2024 FAMU won 28-13 at Alabama State's homecoming in Montgomery (Oct 5, 2024). In 2022 FAMU won 21-14 (Nov 12, 2022). FAMU leads the all-time series 19-14-2.

market.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (LOW) $85 in October?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

On Oct 8, WTI futures were up 5% at $92.70 and Brent was up 5.2% at $105.36, after Middle East tensions rose and nine tankers were attacked in and around Hormuz over the past week.

Trading Economics (CFD-based) showed WTI topping $92.6 on Oct 8, its highest in nearly a month, after falling below $89 on Oct 7, its lowest in over a month. It said prices were down about 16% from a September four-month peak as of Oct 7.

The White House reportedly asked the Pentagon for strike options against Iranian targets that could be carried out before the November midterms. The Pentagon reportedly told CENTCOM to finish preparations to resume combat operations in Iran.

Other drivers on Oct 8: tanker attacks in Hormuz last week were the highest weekly level since the war began; about 25% of US Gulf oil output was shut ahead of Tropical Storm Isaias; EIA crude stocks fell by over 3 million barrels; Saudi Arabia cut its official selling prices, and tankers resumed loading in the Gulf.

In September 2026, front-month WTI daily highs ranged widely: 105.63 on Sep 16, 101.69 on Sep 15, 97.22 on Sep 21, 96.78 on Sep 24 and 96.54 on Sep 28. Between Sep 15 and Sep 28, 8 of 10 sessions had highs at or above $95.

WTI closes in 2026 above $100 included Apr 1–2 ($111.54), Apr 29 ($106.88) and Sep 17 ($101.91). Intraday WTI reached nearly $120 in early March. Across the Iran-war period, WTI has repeatedly moved $10+ within a few weeks, e.g. $83.85 on Apr 17 to $106.88 on Apr 29.

Recent swings: WTI jumped 6% to $92.19 on Jul 23 on tanker attacks; it rose from $83.40 (week of Aug 28) to $96.05 on Sep 9 and $101.91 on Sep 17 as US-Iran fighting escalated. Earlier, it fell over 16% in one day on Apr 8 after a ceasefire announcement.

Resolution uses the Pyth 'CLL' feed of the ICE WTI Active Month futures contract, not spot. The EIA Cushing spot series runs well above futures: 97.89 on Oct 2 and 96.24 on Oct 6, against front-month futures closes of 91.11 and 89.44.

recent_facts.fact: After round 1 at Club de Campo Villa de Madrid, Eugenio Chacarra, Connor Syme and Grant Forrest led at 5 under (66). Angel Ayora and Sergio García were tied 4th at 4 under, one shot back.

Ayora shot 67 (−4) in round 1, a card that included two eagles and three bogeys. He was the provisional leader during the morning. Afterward he said that if his driver holds up, he will be near the top.

Round 2 is being played today (2026-10-09). I couldn't find any live or completed round 2 scores: the ESPN, Golf Post and Golf Channel leaderboard pages either returned nothing or blocked access. Ayora's standing after round 2 is not verified.
Co-leader Eugenio Chacarra has a foot injury. He said he did not yet know whether he could play round 2 and left open the possibility of withdrawing.

Ayora tees off at 13:50 Spanish time on Friday 9 October from the 1st tee, playing with Ludvig Åberg and Tyrrell Hatton. In round 1, Åberg shot even par and Hatton +5. The tournament has four rounds, 8–11 October, so it finishes Sunday 11 October.

Before the event, Jon Rahm (world #15) was listed as the highest-ranked player in the field, which also included Justin Rose, Shane Lowry, Ludvig Åberg, Tyrrell Hatton, Patrick Reed and defending champion Marco Penge (#53).
Spanish opening-day reports say Jon Rahm did not play because of the birth of his fourth child. Defending champion Marco Penge and Patrick Reed both opened at +2.

Ayora (born 2004) turned pro in 2023. His only professional win is the 2024 Rosa Challenge Tour event. On the DP World Tour he has no wins; his best finishes include T7 at the 2025 Italian Open (he led outright after 36 holes) and T8 at the 2025 DP World Tour Championship. He had ten top-10s in 2025. A single Challenge Tour win is weak evidence of an ability to close out a win.

In the 2026 season (as of July), Ayora had five DP World Tour top-10s, including T5 at the Qatar Masters, T3 at the KLM Open in June and solo 5th at the Open d'Italia in late June. He missed the cut at the Scottish Open, the PGA Championship and The Open, and was 22nd in the Race to Dubai at the time of The Open.
An undated PGA Tour profile gives Ayora's Official World Golf Ranking as 121. This figure may be out of date.
Ayora finished 9th at the 2025 Open de España at the same venue (Club de Campo Villa de Madrid). He is in his second DP World Tour season and has turned down LIV Golf offers.
The question resolves Yes only if Ayora wins the tournament. If he withdraws or does not tee off, the Tournament Winner market resolves No.

market.question: Will the Democrats win the Ohio Senate race in 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the 2026 Ohio U.S. Senate special election currently scheduled for November 3, inclusive of any run-offs.

A candidate shall be considered to represent a party in the event that he or she is the nominee of the party in question. Candidates other than the Democratic or Republican nominee (e.g., Greens, Libertarian, independent) may be added at a later date.

Candidates who run as independents will not be encompassed by the “Democrat” or “Republican” options regardless of any affiliation they may have with the party.

The candidates may be named in the contract for the convenience of traders. In the event that any named candidate is replaced as the nominee of their respective party prior to election day, the name in the contract will be updated and the market will resolve based on the replacement nominee of the party.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race in this state for the same candidate, this market will resolve based on the official certification.

recent_facts.fact: The RCP polling average for September 1 to October 5, 2026 has Democrat Sherrod Brown at 47.5% and Republican Sen. Jon Husted at 44.0%, which is Brown +3.5.
A CNN poll of 760 registered voters (Sept 29–Oct 5, MoE ±4.5) had Brown at 49% and Husted at 43%.
The Suffolk/USA Today Ohio poll had Brown at 47% and Husted at 44%, with 6% undecided. The ballot also listed Libertarian William Redpath and No Party candidate Greg Levy.

Marist surveyed 1,298 Ohio registered voters (Sept 24–27, MoE ±3.8). Brown led Husted 51% to 43%, and independents favored Brown 58% to 33%. In the governor's race, Democrat Acton led Republican Ramaswamy 50% to 44%.

Some recent polls show a closer race. InsiderAdvantage (Sept 28–29) had Brown 44%, Husted 43%. Quantus Insights (Sept 21–23) had Brown 48%, Husted 47%. Rasmussen (likely voters) had Brown 46%, Husted 43%, with 7% undecided.
A Portage County bellwether poll (MoE ±5.6) had Husted ahead of Brown 48% to 44%, unlike the statewide polls.

In the 2024 Ohio Senate race, Republican Bernie Moreno beat Brown 50.1% to 46.5% (R+3.6). The final RCP average (Oct 23–Nov 4) was Moreno +1.7, so the polls understated the Republican margin by about 1.9 points. A NYT/Siena poll in late September 2024 had Brown +4.

In 2024, Brown led in several mid-campaign polls, and the race moved toward the Republican over the last weeks. Final individual polls ranged from a tie (Trafalgar) to Moreno +3 (Emerson, AtlasIntel).
NPR calls the race a toss-up that could decide Senate control for Trump's last two years in office. Cook Political Report also rates it a Toss-up.

Brown voted in Franklin County on the first day of early voting. He pointed to voter unhappiness over the war with Iran and over food and diesel prices. Husted has said he would back a federal gas tax holiday.
The Hill reported that Donald Trump is scheduled to hold a rally for Jon Husted in Ohio.

Brown's campaign says national Republicans are spending more than $270 million against him; this is the campaign's own figure. Separately, the crypto super PAC Fairshake reportedly plans to spend at least $30 million opposing Brown.
Ohio early voting runs from Oct 6 to Nov 1, 2026, and the voter registration deadline was Oct 5. The special election is Nov 3, 2026. The searches turned up no scheduled Brown–Husted debate.
Brown raised $7.3M in Q4 2025 and had about $9.9M cash on hand. Husted's two committees raised $1.5M in Q4 and $7.3M across all of 2025.

market.question: US-Iran Hormuz Agreement by October 31?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if a diplomatic agreement between the United States and Iran over traffic in the strait of Hormuz is announced by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET.

A diplomatic agreement refers to an official agreement, treaty, deal, or substantially similar diplomatic instrument that establishes agreed actions, policies, obligations, or commitments between the United States and Iran.

A qualifying diplomatic agreement must establish Iranian policies, obligations, or commitments  aimed at permitting, restoring, or increasing vessel or shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

All listed countries must announce their acceptance of the same qualifying diplomatic agreement for the Payout Condition to be met. A joint announcement will qualify, as will separate announcements from each entity of its own acceptance of an agreement which, taken together, directly indicate that all the listed countries accepted the same agreement. Separate announcements of individual policies will not qualify if the policies are not announced as part of a diplomatic agreement.

Each announcement must be a declarative statement that clearly and unambiguously communicates acceptance of an agreement. Statements that reference ongoing negotiations or a prospective agreement, or that allude to or express support for an agreement without confirming acceptance of the agreement, do not qualify. A qualifying announcement need not reference the agreement by name or use specific terminology, provided it clearly communicates acceptance of an agreement.
 
Whether announcements from the listed countries represent a diplomatic agreement and whether such an agreement qualifies will be primarily determined through the announcements themselves. Where an announcement is made by all listed countries but, based on the announcements, it remains ambiguous whether the announcements represent a qualifying diplomatic agreement between the countries, this market will remain open until either i) definitive confirmation that the announcements represent a qualifying diplomatic agreement between the listed entities is achieved through further announcements from the listed countries or a consensus of credible reporting or ii) 14 calendar days (ET) have passed after the date that the last country made their first potentially qualifying announcement. If, at the end of the fourteenth calendar day, no definitive confirmation has been achieved, this market will resolve based on the totality of information available from the resolution sources at that time. No single statement, denial, or presentation of evidence will govern where it is contradicted by the totality of information.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran and a consensus of credible reporting.

Jeremy Hecklinski is taking first-team practice reps, with Jimmy Sullivan as the next backup. Hecklinski's only college stats found were 2-of-2 passing for 8 yards and a 6-yard rushing TD, both in 2025 mop-up duty.

The game is Friday, Oct. 9, 2026, at 9:00 pm ET on FOX, at Alaska Airlines Field at Husky Stadium in Seattle, which is Washington's home field. Iowa is 4-1 and Washington is 3-2 (0-2 Big Ten). One search summary claimed this was Washington's 'third trip to Iowa City'; that conflicts with the venue every source lists.
No. 5 Ohio State beat No. 14 Iowa 31-14 at Kinnick Stadium. Iowa trailed 31-6 before a late touchdown. Julian Sayin threw for 324 yards and 3 TDs, and Brown fumbled on the second play from scrimmage.
Washington lost 25-21 at No. 18 USC on Oct. 3 and 27-24 to Minnesota on Sept. 26. Both conference losses were by 4 points or fewer.

Washington's results: beat Washington State 24-10 (Sept. 6), beat Utah State 16-14 (Sept. 12), beat FCS Eastern Washington 48-16 (Sept. 19), then lost to Minnesota 24-27 and at USC 21-25. The three wins came against non-Big Ten opponents.
Iowa beat Michigan 20-19 the week before the Ohio State game. That is Iowa's only Big Ten win (1-1 in conference).

Iowa's non-conference results: beat Northern Illinois 40-0, beat Iowa State 16-13 on Sept. 12 with a last-second 42-yard field goal, and beat FCS Northern Iowa 55-0 on Sept. 19, when three running backs each ran for 100+ yards.

Washington QB Demond Williams Jr. has 1,327 passing yards and 8 TDs. Iowa's Hank Brown has 832 passing yards and 5 TDs, and Kamari Moulton leads Iowa with 311 rushing yards. Washington is 14th in FBS in turnover margin at +5.

Iowa safety Tyler Brown is 'out for a while' (he has played 2 of 5 games). Backup safety Ty Hudkins is questionable. CB/S Zach Lutmer is good to go, and DB Deshaun Lee expects to play. DB Kyle Gerardy was out against Ohio State, and no update for Washington was found.

This is a Friday night road game at Husky Stadium, kicking off at 6:00 pm PT. Iowa has a bye week afterward, and Washington plays at Purdue on Oct. 16. The Big Ten availability report comes out about two hours before kickoff and will confirm whether Hank Brown plays.

The field has 72 players and there is no 36-hole cut, so every player plays all four rounds. The course is par 71 at Yokohama Country Club.
The event runs October 8–11, 2026, with a $8,000,000 purse, so three rounds remain (Oct 9–11). Homa's Round 2 tee time is 9:07 a.m. local (8:07 p.m. EDT), paired with Steven Fisk and Kurt Kitayama.

market.question: Will Student List – Students Win win the most seats in the 2026 Serbian parliamentary election?
market.rules:
Parliamentary elections to elect the 250 members of the National Assembly of Serbia are scheduled to take place on October 25, 2026.

This market will resolve to the electoral list that wins the greatest number of seats in the National Assembly of Serbia as a result of this election.

Electoral lists will be primarily ranked by the number of seats won in the specified election. If two or more lists are tied on seats, ties will be broken by the total number of valid votes received, with higher vote totals ranking higher. If lists remain tied, ties will be broken by alphabetical order of the listed names. This market will resolve to the list that occupies the highest finishing position after applying this ranking.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the named electoral list, as it appears on the ballot and official proclamations, regardless of which parties make up the list or how its members later organize themselves in the National Assembly.

If the results of the specified election are not definitively known by March 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the results of the elections, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. In the case of ambiguity, this market will resolve solely based on the results as reported by the Republic Electoral Commission of Serbia (https://www.rik.parlament.gov.rs/).

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia – Opinion polling for the 2026 Serbian parliamentary election
recent_facts.fact: Opposition and independent media accuse Ipsos and Faktor Plus of pro-government bias. A Bureau for Social Research study found that most Serbian pollsters do not disclose weighting or funding. CRTA's July poll left out 12.2% undecided, and an April NSPM scenario poll left out 21% undecided.

RIK accepted 18 lists and 1 was withdrawn. List #1 is 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' (SNS, PUPS, SRS, ZS and others; 209,130 signatures). List #3 is 'Student List – Students Are Winning', headed by Ilija Srdanović (69,099 signatures). SPS–JS (Dačić) is running separately as list #2.

Vučić resigned as president on 27 Sep 2026 to lead the SNS list as its prime ministerial candidate. The snap election was announced on 8–9 Sep and set for 25 Oct, more than a year before the regular vote due in late 2027.

Several opposition groups consolidated behind the Student List. The People's Serbia coalition (NPS, NLS, EU) withdrew its list on 22 Sep to back it, after NLS and EU had endorsed it on 15 Sep. PSG left the PES coalition in late September to support the Student List. PES (SSP/SRCE, Tepić/Ponoš) is still running separately as list #9 but has said it will cooperate with the Student List.

In late September, pro-government tabloids ran campaigns against Student List leader Srdanović, which fact-checkers said used AI-manipulated photos. Televised debates are scheduled on RTS, N1, Nova and Radio Belgrade from 29 Sep to 8 Oct.

Vreme reports that polls are dominated by two blocs, 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' and the Student List. A September NSPM survey suggested that Dačić's SPS may struggle to clear the 3% threshold.

The CRTA / Stanford Democracy Action Lab survey (June fieldwork, n=2,324) put the Student List at 44.9% and SNS at 35.7% among decided voters. It was the first published poll to show the Student List ahead.
No Ipsos, CRTA or other poll fielded in October 2026 turned up. The most recent published polls are Faktor Plus (21 Sep) and NSPM (30 Sep, fieldwork early September).

In the December 2023 snap election, preliminary results gave the SNS list 47.95% and Serbia Against Violence 24.32%, with SPS at 6.75%. Ipsos/CeSID exit polls (about 47% vs 23%) were close to the count. Unverified recollection: an SNS-led list has won the most seats in every parliamentary election since 2012 (2012, 2014, 2016, 2020, 2022, 2023), 6 of 6.

All 250 seats are elected by nationwide proportional representation with a 3% threshold. Minority lists, including #4, 5, 6, 10, 14, 15, 17 and 18, are exempt from the threshold. The question resolves on seats won by the ballot-named list, with ties broken by votes.
Election day is 25 Oct 2026, the same day the question closes. RIK (rik.parlament.gov.rs) publishes the preliminary and final results.

market.question: Will BTC trimmed mean be above $87500.00 by 11:59 PM ET on Oct 31, 2026? (Above $87,500.00)
market.rules:
If the price of BTC after issuance and through 11:59 PM ET on Oct 31, 2026 is ever above $
87500.00, then the market resolves to Yes.
At each minute throughout the market duration, a settlement value is calculated using every minute-by-minute CF BRTI price for BTC. For each of these individual minute-by-minute checks, the top 20% and bottom 20% of the cumulative dataset are removed before calculating the average of the remaining values. If the trimmed mean associated with any single minute during the period is above the threshold, the market resolves to Yes. This methodology reduces the impact of extreme price spikes or drops. The measurement period runs from when the market is issued until the specified end time. If CF Benchmarks data is unavailable or incomplete at the expiration time, affected strikes resolve to No. For cryptocurrencies with multiple versions, the Exchange will specify which version or ticker is being tracked.

market.question: Will Flávio Bolsonaro win the second round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election by less than 4%?
market.rules:
The second round of the presidential election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 25, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two candidates in the second round of the next Brazil Presidential Election.

For the purpose of this market, the “margin of victory” is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first- and second-place candidates. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the election.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

If a candidate other than Flávio Bolsonaro or Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva receives the most valid votes in the second round, or if the top two candidates receive exactly the same number of valid votes, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the vote count has been made official.

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

If the result of this election isn't known definitively by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).

recent_facts.fact: Shares for the other first-round candidates: Augusto Cury 2.89%, Renan Santos 2.24%, Ronaldo Caiado 2.18%, Romeu Zema 0.27%, Samara Martins 0.10%. All the others had 0.04% or less, so about 7.8% of valid votes went to eliminated candidates.

AtlasIntel/Bloomberg runoff poll (5,026 interviews, Oct 3–8, MoE ±1 pt, TSE registration BR-03663/2026): Flávio 52.8% vs Lula 47.2% of valid votes, a 5.6-pt margin. On total votes it was Flávio 51.1%, Lula 45.7% and blank/null/undecided 3.2%. AtlasIntel's previous round had Lula 50.1% vs Flávio 49.9%.

Datafolha runoff poll (2,520 interviews, Oct 6–8): Flávio 49% vs Lula 45% of total votes, and Flávio 52% vs Lula 48% of valid votes, a 4-pt margin. Rejection: 46% would not vote for Lula and 43% would not vote for Flávio.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (Opinion polling for the 2026 Brazilian presidential election)
recent_facts.fact: PoderData runoff poll (3,000 interviews, Oct 5–7, MoE ±1.8): Flávio 49% vs Lula 44% of total votes.

The result was Flávio +1.87, so the margin miss was about 3–7 pts toward Flávio. Gerp (Flávio 46 / Lula 44) was close.

Last season Alabama State won 42-14 at FAMU on Sept 27, 2025.

market.rules:

Tournament Winner and End of Round Leader markets will resolve to No
Finishing Position, Make the Cut, Head-to-Head, and 3-Ball markets will resolve to Fair Market Value

recent_facts.fact: After round 1 at Club de Campo Villa de Madrid, Eugenio Chacarra, Connor Syme and Grant Forrest led at 5 under (66). Angel Ayora and Sergio García were tied 4th at 4 under, one shot back.

Ayora shot 67 (−4) in round 1, a card that included two eagles and three bogeys. He was the provisional leader during the morning. Afterward he said that if his driver holds up, he will be near the top.

Round 2 is being played today (2026-10-09). I couldn't find any live or completed round 2 scores: the ESPN, Golf Post and Golf Channel leaderboard pages either returned nothing or blocked access. Ayora's standing after round 2 is not verified.
Co-leader Eugenio Chacarra has a foot injury. He said he did not yet know whether he could play round 2 and left open the possibility of withdrawing.

Ayora tees off at 13:50 Spanish time on Friday 9 October from the 1st tee, playing with Ludvig Åberg and Tyrrell Hatton. In round 1, Åberg shot even par and Hatton +5. The tournament has four rounds, 8–11 October, so it finishes Sunday 11 October.

Before the event, Jon Rahm (world #15) was listed as the highest-ranked player in the field, which also included Justin Rose, Shane Lowry, Ludvig Åberg, Tyrrell Hatton, Patrick Reed and defending champion Marco Penge (#53).
Spanish opening-day reports say Jon Rahm did not play because of the birth of his fourth child. Defending champion Marco Penge and Patrick Reed both opened at +2.

Ayora (born 2004) turned pro in 2023. His only professional win is the 2024 Rosa Challenge Tour event. On the DP World Tour he has no wins; his best finishes include T7 at the 2025 Italian Open (he led outright after 36 holes) and T8 at the 2025 DP World Tour Championship. He had ten top-10s in 2025. A single Challenge Tour win is weak evidence of an ability to close out a win.

In the 2026 season (as of July), Ayora had five DP World Tour top-10s, including T5 at the Qatar Masters, T3 at the KLM Open in June and solo 5th at the Open d'Italia in late June. He missed the cut at the Scottish Open, the PGA Championship and The Open, and was 22nd in the Race to Dubai at the time of The Open.
An undated PGA Tour profile gives Ayora's Official World Golf Ranking as 121. This figure may be out of date.
Ayora finished 9th at the 2025 Open de España at the same venue (Club de Campo Villa de Madrid). He is in his second DP World Tour season and has turned down LIV Golf offers.
The question resolves Yes only if Ayora wins the tournament. If he withdraws or does not tee off, the Tournament Winner market resolves No.

market.question: Next US-Iran senior diplomatic meeting by October 31, 2026? (copy)
market.rules:
On September 22, U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, with President Trump saying another meeting is scheduled in the near future.(see: https://www.israelhayom.com/2026/09/22/witkoff-kushner-attended-us-iran-meeting-another-expected-soon). 

This market will resolve to “Yes” if there is a direct or indirect senior-level diplomatic meeting between the United States and Iran by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A diplomatic meeting occurs when representatives of both listed countries who are acting in an official capacity and are authorized to engage in diplomacy on behalf of their respective governments or governing authorities deliberately meet for the purpose of diplomacy or negotiation. A qualifying meeting need not result in any agreement, joint statement, or further engagement.

A diplomatic meeting is senior-level if each listed entity is represented by a head of state, a head of government, or a vice president; a foreign minister; a minister of cabinet rank; the secretary or head of a national security council; the presiding officer of a national legislature; a special envoy; or another individual designated by the head of state or head of government to conduct diplomatic negotiations on their behalf. Individuals authorized only for technical, implementation, monitoring, staff-level, preparatory, or working-group-level talks will not be considered designated to conduct diplomatic negotiations on behalf of the head of state or head of government. This definition includes, but is not limited to, all of the following individuals: for the United States, Donald Trump, JD Vance, Marco Rubio, Scott Bessent, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner; and for Iran, Mojtaba Khamenei, Masoud Pezeshkian, Abbas Araghchi and Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf. In each case, a qualifying representative must participate in the meeting.

A direct meeting refers to a diplomatic meeting where the representatives of both countries directly interact with each other in person. Meetings conducted through translators qualify, provided direct, face-to-face communication occurs. An indirect meeting refers to a meeting conducted indirectly through designated mediators or facilitators. A qualifying indirect meeting must meet both of the following criteria (i) the designated intermediaries act with the knowledge and authorization of both entities; (ii) representatives of both entities are physically present in the same facility, venue, or city as part of a single organized round of talks convened for the purpose of diplomatic engagement, with the intermediary conveying communications between the representatives or delegations on the same day. “The same day” means the same calendar day local time at the meeting location.

Sessions, proceedings, or convenings of standing international organizations, treaty bodies, or recurring multilateral summits or conferences (e.g., the United Nations General Assembly, G7, and G20 summits) do not qualify, unless a qualifying and deliberate diplomatic meeting between representatives of the listed countries is separately held alongside such a convening.

The following do not qualify as either a direct or indirect diplomatic meeting: chance encounters; standalone exchanges limited to greetings, courtesies, or photo opportunities; meetings conducted remotely, by telephone, or by any other means where the relevant representatives are not physically present at the same facility, venue, or city on the same day; discussions involving persons not authorized to engage in diplomacy or negotiation on behalf of their respective governments.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran and a consensus of credible reporting.

For the purpose of this market, the “margin of victory” is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first- and second-place candidates. The question counts only a PM elected by the National Assembly and formally sworn in as part of a new government, by 2028-06-30. A caretaker PM does not count. The incumbent, Đuro Macut, proposed the dissolution on 2026-09-07 and stays in office until a new government is elected.

recent_facts.fact: After the 2023-12-17 election, the assembly was constituted on 2024-02-06 and approved the Vučević cabinet on 2024-05-02, about 4.5 months after the vote and close to the 90-day post-constitution deadline of May 6.

recent_facts.source: Recall of past Serbian cabinet dates (unverified)
recent_facts.fact: Unverified recalled dates for past election-to-cabinet gaps: 2014 (election Mar 16, Vučić cabinet Apr 27, about 6 weeks); 2016 (Apr 24 to Aug 11, about 3.5 months); 2020 (Jun 21 to Oct 28, about 4 months); 2022 (Apr 3 to Oct 26, about 7 months). In none of these cases was a cabinet elected within days of the vote.
Vučić has called earlier snap elections before (2014, 2016) and his SNS kept its majority each time. In 2016 it won 131 of 250 seats, and Vučić went on to become PM.

There is a 3% threshold for parliamentary seats, and traditional opposition parties risk splitting the vote below it. Several are polling between 1% and 3.6%.

market.question: Will Saudi airspace be closed by October 31?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Saudi Arabian Airspace (The Jeddah Flight Information Region (FIR)/OEJD) is closed between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A qualifying closure occurs when the aviation or governmental authority responsible for overseeing the specified airspace region issues a Notice to Airmen (NOTAM), or other official order under the regulations of the jurisdiction responsible for that airspace region, which generally cancels or suspends commercial aviation across the specified airspace region, and such closure is not excluded under the exclusions provision below. A qualifying closure must apply generally to commercial flights transiting, arriving in, and departing from the specified airspace region. A closure is not disqualified because the order permits limited exceptions, including humanitarian, medical, repatriation, or emergency flights, or select flights authorized by the responsible authority, provided that commercial flights are prohibited by default, rather than permitted subject to conditions or restrictions.

The following are not qualifying closures: (i) closures due to weather, including volcanic and seismic activity; (ii) closures for holidays or religious observances; (iii) closures planned or announced before market creation; (iv) closures occurring on a regular cadence whose occurrence was determined before market creation, even if not announced; (v) closures resulting from the failure or malfunction of air traffic control, navigation, communications, power, or other technical systems; (vi) restrictions applying to aircraft by nationality, state of registry, operator, or ownership rather than to commercial traffic generally; (vii) closures of a subset of the specified airspace region, including geographic sectors and altitude bands; (viii) ground stops, flow restrictions, capacity reductions, or other air traffic management measures that delay or restrict traffic without closing the specified airspace region to commercial aviation; and (ix) warnings, no-fly zones, flight suspensions, or other restrictions imposed by any party other than the aviation or governmental authorities responsible for overseeing the specified airspace region.

A qualifying closure is deemed to occur at the time the closure takes effect, regardless of when the closure is announced or the order is issued. Where no effective time is included in the order, the closure is deemed to take effect at the time the order is issued.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the Saudi Arabian government, including the Ministry of Transport and Logistic Services, the General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA), and Saudi Air Navigation Services (SANS), and a consensus of credible reporting.

recent_facts.fact: As of Oct 9, 2026, no outlet found had reported Other Mommy's Thursday-preview gross or any Friday or weekend figures. The film opened Oct 9, and The Numbers has no actual weekend data yet.

Other Mommy is an R-rated horror film from Blumhouse Atomic Monster and Universal. It was directed by Rob Savage, stars Jessica Chastain and opens in about 3,200 domestic theaters. Its net budget is reported at about $19M; Gold Derby gives $18M.

Universal did not hold standard U.S. critics' screenings for Other Mommy. Previews ran Thursday, Oct 8 (showtimes from 2 p.m.), and early reactions included calling it 'Jessica Chastain's worst movie in a long time'.
Early Rotten Tomatoes reviews were mostly negative: 12 of the first 15 reviews were 'rotten'. Australian outlets scored it 1.5/5 (The Jam Report, Screen Space) and 2/5 (The AU Review).
Hollywood Reporter's roundup of first reviews ran under the headline 'Jessica Chastain's Worst in a Long Time'. Other outlets described the reactions as 'brutal' and 'truly dreadful'.

Industry coverage reports that the Other Mommy trailer went viral in summer 2026, which led to strong pre-release tracking. Box Office Pro wrote that industry tracking had at one point reached as high as $35M, but that was an earlier reading.
Comparable openings: Mama (2013, also based on a horror short and produced by the same team) opened to $28.4M. Verity opened to $32.6M the weekend before (Oct 2–4, 2026) and got a C+ CinemaScore.
Another comparable Blumhouse/Universal R-rated horror title, The Black Phone (2022), opened to $23.6M domestically on its way to $90.1M.
Other wide releases this weekend are The Social Reckoning (new, 59% on Rotten Tomatoes), Verity (second weekend), Resident Evil (fourth weekend), Heart of the Beast and Digger.

market.question: Will Max Verstappen win the 2026 F1 Singapore Grand Prix?
market.rules:
This is a polymarket on the winner of the 2026 F1 Singapore Grand Prix, scheduled for Oct 11, 2026.

If the 2026 F1 Singapore Grand Prix is canceled or rescheduled to a date after Oct 18, 2026, this market will resolve to “Other.”

This market will resolve in favor of the driver who is officially listed in first place in the Final Classification published by the FIA following the conclusion of the race. The Final Classification is typically released 30-60 minutes after the race ends and includes any applied time penalties and official adjustments.

Disqualifications or changes made after the publication of the Final Classification will not affect market resolution. The timing of the podium ceremony does not determine the result for this market — only the FIA's published classification will be used to resolve this market.

The resolution source will be the official Formula 1 website and a consensus of credible sports news reporting.

recent_facts.fact: Verstappen was fastest in Singapore sprint qualifying with 1:31.156. Russell was +0.120s, Leclerc +0.243, Piastri +0.298, Norris +0.431, Hamilton +0.546, championship leader Antonelli 7th at +0.693, and Verstappen's teammate Hadjar 9th at +1.791. This sets the grid for the sprint only. The Grand Prix grid comes from a separate qualifying session.

The FIA stewards are investigating Verstappen for passing Lewis Hamilton under yellow flags at Turn 7 in SQ1, after Perez crashed. A guilty finding could bring a sprint grid penalty. As of the latest reports found, no decision had been published.
Before SQ1, Red Bull changed Verstappen's ERS unit as a precaution over a suspected fault. He was still fastest in all three sprint qualifying segments.

In the only practice session (FP1), Verstappen was 6th, 0.732s behind Russell's 1:32.274, after radio problems and time stuck in the garage. Leclerc was 2nd and Norris 3rd. Reports said his medium-tyre pace was more than half a second faster than anyone else's on mediums.

In the previous round, Verstappen won the rain-delayed Bahrain GP, which was held at Sepang, Malaysia. He started from pole and finished 2.307s ahead of Antonelli, with Hamilton 3rd. It was his first win of 2026.
At the Azerbaijan GP, Verstappen finished 2nd, 0.196s behind winner George Russell, and Hadjar was 3rd. It was Russell's third win of 2026.

In 2026 Verstappen has 8 podiums and 1 win, and is 6th in the standings with 188 points, 132 behind Antonelli. In the 9 races since Austria he has 1 win, six 2nd- or 3rd-place finishes and 2 DNFs, an average finish of 2.14 excluding DNFs.

16 of the 23 rounds of 2026 are complete. Winners found include Antonelli (China, Canada, Belgium), Russell (Austria, Azerbaijan) and Verstappen (Bahrain at Sepang). Mercedes lead the constructors' standings with 538 points after Baku, ahead of Ferrari 378, McLaren 306 and Red Bull 263.
This is Singapore's first sprint weekend. The sprint and Grand Prix qualifying are still to come on Saturday, and the Grand Prix is on Sunday, October 11, 2026.

The Grand Prix pole-sitter has won all but 5 Singapore Grands Prix, roughly 11 of 16 through 2025. Russell won from pole in 2025. The count is inferred from the source's wording, so treat it as unverified.
Verstappen has never won the Singapore GP. Motorsport.com said this sprint qualifying result is his first fastest qualifying time of any kind at Marina Bay.

recent_facts.fact: After round 1 at Club de Campo Villa de Madrid, Eugenio Chacarra, Connor Syme and Grant Forrest led at 5 under (66). Angel Ayora and Sergio García were tied 4th at 4 under, one shot back.

Ayora shot 67 (−4) in round 1, a card that included two eagles and three bogeys. He was the provisional leader during the morning. Afterward he said that if his driver holds up, he will be near the top.

Round 2 is being played today (2026-10-09). I couldn't find any live or completed round 2 scores: the ESPN, Golf Post and Golf Channel leaderboard pages either returned nothing or blocked access. Ayora's standing after round 2 is not verified.
Co-leader Eugenio Chacarra has a foot injury. He said he did not yet know whether he could play round 2 and left open the possibility of withdrawing.

Ayora tees off at 13:50 Spanish time on Friday 9 October from the 1st tee, playing with Ludvig Åberg and Tyrrell Hatton. In round 1, Åberg shot even par and Hatton +5. The tournament has four rounds, 8–11 October, so it finishes Sunday 11 October.

Before the event, Jon Rahm (world #15) was listed as the highest-ranked player in the field, which also included Justin Rose, Shane Lowry, Ludvig Åberg, Tyrrell Hatton, Patrick Reed and defending champion Marco Penge (#53).
Spanish opening-day reports say Jon Rahm did not play because of the birth of his fourth child. Defending champion Marco Penge and Patrick Reed both opened at +2.

Ayora (born 2004) turned pro in 2023. His only professional win is the 2024 Rosa Challenge Tour event. On the DP World Tour he has no wins; his best finishes include T7 at the 2025 Italian Open (he led outright after 36 holes) and T8 at the 2025 DP World Tour Championship. He had ten top-10s in 2025. A single Challenge Tour win is weak evidence of an ability to close out a win.

In the 2026 season (as of July), Ayora had five DP World Tour top-10s, including T5 at the Qatar Masters, T3 at the KLM Open in June and solo 5th at the Open d'Italia in late June. He missed the cut at the Scottish Open, the PGA Championship and The Open, and was 22nd in the Race to Dubai at the time of The Open.
An undated PGA Tour profile gives Ayora's Official World Golf Ranking as 121. This figure may be out of date.
Ayora finished 9th at the 2025 Open de España at the same venue (Club de Campo Villa de Madrid). He is in his second DP World Tour season and has turned down LIV Golf offers.
The question resolves Yes only if Ayora wins the tournament. If he withdraws or does not tee off, the Tournament Winner market resolves No.

market.question: Will Tesla or SpaceX announce a definitive, binding agreement for Tesla to acquire SpaceX, SpaceX to acquire Tesla, or the two entities to merge or combine in any structure that results in a transfer of controlling interest or consolidation of the two entities under common corporate ownership before Nov 1, 2026? (Before Nov 1, 2026)
market.rules:
If Tesla or SpaceX officially announces a definitive, binding agreement for Tesla to acquire SpaceX, SpaceX to acquire Tesla, or the two entities to merge or combine in any structure that results in a transfer of controlling interest or consolidation of the two entities under common corporate ownership before Nov 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
The announcement must be made through official company channels including press releases, SEC filings (8-K, 10-K, 10-Q), earnings calls, investor presentations, verified social media accounts, or official statements to media subsequently confirmed by the company. CEO statements through official channels qualify. Rumors, speculation, unconfirmed reports, leaked information, third-party announcements without company confirmation, and preliminary discussions do not qualify. The announcement must occur after market issuance. Companies are tracked through rebranding and name changes representing the same business entity.

This market resolves Yes regardless of which entity is the acquirer and which is the target. A Tesla acquisition of SpaceX, a SpaceX acquisition of Tesla, a reverse merger, or a stock-for-stock combination all satisfy the Payout Criterion equally, provided a definitive agreement is publicly announced.

A statement by Elon Musk shall only satisfy the Payout Criterion if it constitutes an unambiguous, affirmative confirmation of a definitive signed agreement — not an expression of intent, a hypothetical, a negotiation update, or a speculative comment about a future combination.

recent_facts.fact: As of October 3, 2026, neither board had approved a Tesla–SpaceX merger. No terms or completion date existed, and the article notes that a real proposal would show up in SEC filings.
An analysis dated September 16, 2026 found no definitive Tesla–SpaceX merger agreement, deal valuation, share-exchange ratio or completion date.

On the All-In podcast on September 15, 2026, Musk was asked why Tesla and SpaceX remain separate. He said, "With all this collaboration, on so many levels, who can imagine what action one might take," but did not confirm any deal or talks.

On Tesla's Q2 2026 earnings call on July 22, Musk said "we can't talk about combining companies" and that any such move "has got to be done with the appropriate process." He also cited "more and more overlap, especially with Terafab."

Tesla will release Q3 2026 results after market close on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, with a Q&A webcast at 5:30 p.m. ET. This is the main scheduled official-channel event before the November 1 close.

recent_facts.source: Yahoo Finance (Elon Musk Hints at Tesla-SpaceX Merger)
recent_facts.fact: Searches turned up no report that Tesla's board has formed a special committee or hired advisors to evaluate a SpaceX combination. Recent coverage describes speculation, not reported negotiations.

SpaceX filed its S-1 on May 20, 2026 and began trading on Nasdaq as SPCX on June 12, 2026. Cited market values are about $1.47T for Tesla and about $1.21T for SpaceX, and Tesla shares are down about 17% year to date.

Tesla's stake in SpaceX is under 1%. It comes from Tesla's roughly $2B investment in xAI Series E preferred stock, which converted into SpaceX equity when SpaceX absorbed xAI. Tesla and SpaceX also have a 'framework agreement' on collaboration and the joint Terafab chip project.
On the July 22 call, Tesla's general counsel described "numerous beneficial transactions" with SpaceX, and the CFO said Q2 net income included a $1B mark-to-market gain on Tesla's SpaceX holdings.

More than 900 million SpaceX shares unlocked on August 6, 2026. Third-party trackers (unverified) list further tranches around October 24 and after SpaceX's Q3 report, with full expiry on December 8, 2026. Musk's shares are locked up until one year after the June 2026 IPO.

In late January 2026, Bloomberg and Reuters reported that Musk was weighing a SpaceX–Tesla tie-up, a SpaceX–xAI merger, or a three-way combination. The SpaceX–xAI deal went ahead and Tesla was not combined. (Recalled, unverified here: the SpaceX–xAI merger was announced in early February 2026, within days of the reports.)

Wedbush's Dan Ives frames any combination as coming in 2027, after the SpaceX IPO. Oppenheimer says a deal is 'plausible' but does not see a near-term merger. Morningstar flags Tesla shareholders' concern about SpaceX's valuation as an obstacle.

Precedent: when Musk proposed taking Tesla private in 2018, the board formed a three-member special committee of independent directors and hired outside counsel. The process ended without a deal. A Musk-related-party transaction would likely require a similar committee process before any definitive agreement.

To resolve Yes, a definitive, binding agreement must be announced through official channels before November 1, 2026. Musk hints, intent statements and reports of talks (like the September 15 and July 22 remarks) do not qualify.

market.question: US announces end of Iranian blockade by October 15, 2026?
market.rules:
On July 13, 2026, Trump announced the United States would reinstate its naval blockade of Iran, targeting Iranian ships and customers.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States government, or an authorized representative of the United States government, publicly and officially announces the end, termination, lifting, or suspension of the United States’ naval blockade on Iranian ships and ships of Iranian customers, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An announcement qualifies if it communicates that the United States will generally cease blocking vessel traffic for Iranian ships and customers, including an announcement that the blockade will not take effect at all, even if some restrictions remain (for example, an imposition of fees). An announcement does not qualify if it reflects only a limited or partial change that stops short of a general end or suspension of the blockade, for example, an exemption for a specific vessel, cargo, or port.

A qualifying announcement must be a declarative statement of the United States government’s present termination or suspension of the blockade, previously-unannounced prior termination or suspension of the blockade, or definitive decision to terminate or suspend the blockade.

A qualifying announcement must clearly and unambiguously identify the end or suspension of the blockade. Statements that merely allude to, reference, or describe an end to the blockade, without clearly communicating it, do not qualify. The announcement need not use specific terminology or reference the end of a blockade by name; an announcement of a resumption of prior obligations, the maintenance of a status quo, or a return to a previously agreed baseline qualifies, provided the substantive policy of ending or suspending the blockade is clearly and unambiguously communicated.

A qualifying announcement must be made through official channels, by an individual acting in an official capacity. Statements made incidentally or informally in a context not intended for official communication do not qualify.

The following do not qualify:

Anonymous, unattributed, or leaked statements not confirmed as official;
Statements by persons not authorized to speak for the United States government;
Third-party speculation, analysis, or predictions that the United States government will announce or implement an end to the blockade;
Satirical, fabricated, hacked, or impersonated communications; and
Statements that describe a prospective, contingent, probable, or conditional end to the blockade rather than announcing a present and decided position.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes” regardless of whether it is later reversed, or whether the blockade actually ends in practice.

Resolution will be based on official information from the United States government, including the President, the Department of Defense, the Department of State, and United States Central Command (CENTCOM), or the official representatives of the United States government.

recent_facts.fact: On Truth Social on October 8, Trump said the US would not attack Iran before the November 3 midterms, citing 'productive discussions' with Tehran. Search summaries of the coverage report he also said the blockade 'will remain in full force and effect'; the full articles could not be opened to confirm the exact wording.

On October 5, CENTCOM said it had redirected 130 ships since enforcement resumed on July 14 and had disabled 3 vessels and destroyed 13 over 12 weeks. Vice Adm. Brad Cooper said the mission continues.

Coverage summarized in search results says Treasury sanctioned 17 more vessels and said this effectively neutralizes most of Iran's remaining shadow fleet. A White House official said Trump has all options available. Earlier reports said the White House had told the Pentagon to prepare strikes before the election.

Iran's parliament speaker Ghalibaf said the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until seven conditions based on the Islamabad memorandum are met. The report says the UN-sidelines talks produced no breakthrough, and a Tehran source said Iran's assessment is that the war is resuming.

Trump said he rejected Iran's proposal from indirect talks in New York (Witkoff and Kushner with FM Araghchi, with Qatar mediating). Iran had offered to reopen Hormuz and resume nuclear talks within a week if the US lifted the blockade, removed oil sanctions and restored a region-wide ceasefire.
Trump told Axios he expected more negotiations that week. Gaps remained wide: Iran wants talks focused on Hormuz and the blockade, while the US wants nuclear concessions.

Iranian hardliners filed a request in parliament to impeach FM Araghchi after his New York meetings with Witkoff. They reportedly objected that the talks were not coordinated with the Supreme National Security Council.

The first phase of the blockade ran from April 13 to June 18, 2026, about 9.5 weeks. CENTCOM announced its end on X along with a 60-day US–Iran memorandum of understanding. This is the one previous official lifting.

In early August, Axios reported the US was close to a Hormuz deal (a 60-day Oman–Iran arrangement) and was aiming to announce it that Wednesday. No lifting of the blockade followed; it remained in force through August and September.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (2026 United States naval blockade of Iran)
recent_facts.fact: Trump announced the reinstatement on July 13, and enforcement began July 14. In the timeline through mid-September there was no announcement of lifting. Iran's central bank governor said on August 19 that oil exports had effectively ceased, and redirected vessels passed 100 by September 12.
During the first phase, Trump repeatedly said the blockade would stay until an agreement was signed. In that phase, the lifting came only with a signed MOU, announced by CENTCOM.
The US midterm elections are on November 3, 2026, after both question deadlines (October 15 and October 31). No date has been publicly set for the next US–Iran negotiating round.

market.question: Will the Federal Reserve Hike rates by 0bps at their October 2026 meeting? (Fed maintains rate)
market.rules:
If the Federal Reserve does a Hike of 0bps on October 28, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
The outcomes are mutually exclusive: at most one can resolve to Yes. For example, a 50-basis-point hike resolves “Hike   25 bps” to Yes and “Hike 25 bps” to No.

If the scheduled FOMC meeting is canceled and does not occur on its scheduled date, “Fed maintains rate” resolves to Yes and all other outcomes resolve to No.

recent_facts.fact: At its September 16, 2026 meeting the FOMC voted 12-0 to raise the federal funds target range by 25 bps to 3.75%-4.00%. This was its first hike since 2023.
The next FOMC meeting is October 27–28, 2026, with the decision on October 28. The meeting after that is December 8–9, 2026.

The September minutes, released October 7, said 'most participants assessed that another increase in the target range for the federal funds rate would likely be appropriate by year end.' They gave no timing and said future decisions depend on incoming information.

In an October 1 speech, Vice Chair Jefferson said policymakers 'will need to come to our own judgment, which may take more time' before deciding on another increase. He also said inflation risks are tilted to the upside.

In separate speeches, Jefferson and New York Fed President Williams said the Fed has time to assess the economy before considering another hike. Williams said there was 'no need for urgency' and 'we have time to gather more information.'
On September 24, Williams said it is 'reasonable' to expect another rate hike by the end of the year.
Minneapolis Fed President Kashkari said more hikes lie ahead. Dallas Fed President Logan has said at least two more increases may be needed.
At the July 2026 meeting the Fed held rates, but three FOMC members dissented in favor of a 25 bp hike.

September nonfarm payrolls rose 29,000, against a consensus of about 84,000–90,000. Unemployment rose to 4.2%. July was revised to -10,000 and August to +133,000. Average hourly earnings rose 0.1% in the month and 3.0% over 12 months.

August PCE inflation was 3.4% headline and 3.0% core, both below expectations. August CPI rose 0.4% for the month and 3.4% year over year. Consumers' median 12-month inflation expectation rose to 3.9%.
The September 2026 CPI is due Wednesday, October 14, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. ET, before the October 27–28 meeting. The October CPI is due November 10, after the meeting.
At Jackson Hole, Chair Warsh said inflation is too high and 'we have work to do.' He has said he intends to give less forward guidance.

'Fed maintains rate' resolves Yes if the target range is unchanged on October 28, or if the meeting is canceled. 'Hike 25bps' resolves Yes only for an increase of exactly 25 bps, which would take the range to 4.00%-4.25%.

market.question: Will there be no change in Fed interest rates after the October 2026 meeting?
market.rules:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's October 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for October 27-28, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their October meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

recent_facts.fact: At its September 15–16, 2026 meeting the FOMC voted unanimously, 12-0, to raise the federal funds target range by 25 bps to 3.75%–4.00%. That makes 4.00% the upper bound going into the October meeting, and it was the Fed's first hike since 2023.
The Board raised the interest rate on reserve balances to 3.90%, effective September 17, 2026, and raised the primary credit rate to 4.00%.

In the September dot plot the median participant projected one more 25 bp hike in 2026, ending the year at about 4.1%, then no change in 2027. According to CNBC, 16 of 18 participants projected one more hike this year and 4 projected two. The two meetings left in 2026 are October and December.

The September minutes, released October 7, show officials were worried that inflation pressures could spread. Most participants thought another hike by year-end would likely be appropriate. The minutes did not commit to October specifically.
The September jobs report was weak. Payrolls rose only 29,000, below estimates of more than 80,000, and unemployment edged up to 4.2%. July was revised down by 31,000 jobs and August by 29,000.

The August PCE report showed core prices up 3.0% year over year, below the 3.3% consensus. Inflation was still described as elevated because of energy prices from the Iran war and AI-related price pressures.

On September 29, New York Fed President John Williams said one more rate increase by the end of this year could be appropriate but there was no need to rush. Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said reaching a judgment on further adjustments could take more time.
Chair Kevin Warsh has given little guidance on the next move since the September meeting. At his September press conference he said 'Inflation is too high and has been for too long.'
The September 2026 CPI is scheduled for release on October 14, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. ET, before the FOMC meeting. One low-quality source claims BLS data releases may be disrupted; this is unverified.
The FOMC meets October 27–28, 2026 and the statement is due October 28. The October jobs report will not come out until early November, after the meeting.

The question resolves on the change in the upper bound (currently 4.00%) according to the October 28 FOMC statement. If no statement is released, it resolves to 'No change'. Any non-25 bp move is rounded up to the nearest 25 bp.

recent_facts.fact: Jacksonville won 22-17 at Cincinnati on Oct 4, 2026, which made them 3-1 overall (1-1 away). Trevor Lawrence went 18 of 23 for 227 yards with 1 TD and 0 INT.

The Rams came from 10 points down in the 4th quarter to beat the Eagles 24-20 at Lincoln Financial Field on Oct 4, 2026, dropping Philadelphia to 2-2 (2nd in the NFC East). Jalen Hurts went 12 of 27 for 93 yards with 2 TDs and was sacked 4 times; only one source gave these figures.

Before Week 4, the Eagles lost their Week 3 Monday Night Football game, where the Bears, led by Case Keenum, blew them out. They had beaten the Commanders in Week 1. That means Philadelphia has lost two games in a row going into this one.

In the week of the game, starting RT Lane Johnson retired and starting C Cam Jurgens was traded to the Ravens. LG Landon Dickerson is already on IR. The new starting center, Drew Kendall (knee), did not practice Wednesday.

Eagles who did not practice Wednesday: RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring), WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring), EDGE Jonathan Greenard (ankle), LB Jihaad Campbell (knee), C Drew Kendall (knee), S Marcus Epps (groin) and WR Hollywood Brown (ankle). Limited: CB Quinyon Mitchell (knee), LB Zack Baun (concussion), TE Dallas Goedert (knee) and OT Fred Johnson (knee).

recent_facts.source: Bleeding Green Nation / Philadelphia Inquirer reporting
recent_facts.fact: Barkley is reported as week-to-week, and an NFL source told Jeff McLane he is unlikely to play against Jacksonville. NFL Network's Garafolo reported Smith is 'at very best, questionable' and could miss multiple games. Neither had an official game designation as of Wednesday.

Only one Jaguar missed Wednesday's practice: S Eric Murray (concussion). Limited: DE Josh Hines-Allen (groin), LT Anton Harrison (elbow), OL Cole Van Lanen (knee), and CBs Montaric Brown (hamstring), Jarrian Jones (foot) and Jourdan Lewis (hamstring), plus DT DaVon Hamilton (foot).

SI says cornerback is the Jaguars' biggest injury worry: Montaric Brown missed the Bengals game, three other CBs are on the report, and Ransaw is out for at least a month. Hines-Allen gave no sign he would miss the game.

Eagles at Jaguars is Week 5, Sunday Oct 11, 2026, at 9:30 AM ET at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London, with Jacksonville as the designated home team. Jacksonville then plays a second straight London game, against Houston at Wembley on Oct 18. Philadelphia hosts Carolina on Oct 18.
The Thursday and Friday practice reports, which set final game designations, had not been found as of Oct 8. Official inactive lists come out about 90 minutes before kickoff.
Fox Sports' matchup page shows Philadelphia leading the all-time series about 6-2. That's a small sample spread over many years, and the page's current records (2-1 for both teams) are out of date.

Through 2024, the Jaguars' London record is at least 7-5 in games I could confirm, including Tottenham wins over Buffalo in 2023 and New England (32-16) in 2024. I couldn't verify the 2025 Wembley result against the Rams or one earlier Tottenham game, so treat this count as unverified.

market.question: Will the Democrats win the Michigan Senate race in 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the 2026 midterm Michigan U.S. Senate election, inclusive of any run-offs.

A candidate shall be considered to represent a party in the event that he or she is the nominee of the party in question. Candidates other than the Democratic or Republican nominee (e.g., Greens, Libertarian, independent) may be added at a later date.

Candidates who run as independents will not be encompassed by the “Democrat” or “Republican” options regardless of any affiliation they may have with the party.

The candidates may be named in the contract for the convenience of traders. In the event that any named candidate is replaced as the nominee of their respective party prior to election day, the name in the contract will be updated and the market will resolve based on the replacement nominee of the party.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race in this state for the same candidate, this market will resolve based on the official certification.

recent_facts.fact: RealClearPolling's average of polls from Sept. 15 to Oct. 6 has Democrat Abdul El-Sayed at 48.1% and Republican Mike Rogers at 44.9%, a lead of 3.2 points for El-Sayed. The page may have been cached.
FiftyPlusOne's Michigan Senate polling average as of Oct. 8 has El-Sayed at 48.0% and Rogers at 44.5%.
Quantus Insights polled 744 likely voters on Oct. 5–6 and found El-Sayed at 48% and Rogers at 47%. A YouGov poll fielded Sept. 28–Oct. 5 had El-Sayed at 49% and Rogers at 48%.

A Mitchell Research poll fielded Oct. 1 has El-Sayed at 45.6% and Rogers at 41.4%, with 6% undecided and a 3.8-point margin of error. Four minor-party candidates (Libertarian, Natural Law, U.S. Taxpayers and Green) each got 3% or less, and 11% of respondents had already voted absentee. Mitchell pointed to Republicans gaining in the final weeks of past Michigan Senate races.
In a Fox News poll, El-Sayed led Rogers 50% to 49% among likely voters and 51% to 48% among registered voters. Fox's Aug. 6–10 poll had Rogers ahead 51% to 47% among registered voters.
A Michigan State University IPPSR poll had El-Sayed ahead of Rogers, 48% to 44%. An earlier poll reported in July had El-Sayed trailing Rogers by double digits while Haley Stevens was tied with him.

El-Sayed won the Aug. 4 Democratic primary with about 48.5% to Rep. Haley Stevens' 47.5%, a margin of about 15,000 votes. Stevens conceded and endorsed him. Rogers had no opponent in the Republican primary, and Mallory McMorrow withdrew from the Democratic race in July. The seat is open because Democratic Sen. Gary Peters is retiring.

El-Sayed and Rogers held a very combative first debate in Grand Rapids on Oct. 8, covering gas prices, the war with Iran and tariffs. El-Sayed called Rogers a Trump loyalist, and Rogers called El-Sayed a 'con man'.

El-Sayed is being outspent nearly 2-to-1 on ads. Groups aligned with Republicans had spent nearly $3 million by mid-September on ads tying El-Sayed to the streamer Hasan Piker, according to AdImpact data. Rogers released an ad calling for an end to the tariff war with Canada.
A second debate, hosted by WXYZ-TV, is scheduled for Oct. 21. The general election is Nov. 3, 2026, and absentee voting in Michigan began Sept. 24.

In 2024, Democrat Elissa Slotkin beat Rogers by about 0.3 points (48.6% to 48.3%, roughly 19,000 votes) even though Trump carried Michigan. Late polls had mostly shown Slotkin ahead by a few points, for example 47% to 42% in an EPIC-MRA poll.
The last time a Republican won a U.S. Senate race in Michigan was 1994. Democrats have won every Michigan Senate race since then, including 2024.

recent_facts.fact: The all-items CPI-U rose 3.4% (not seasonally adjusted) in the 12 months ending August 2026, the same rate as for the 12 months ending July. The NSA index level for August 2026 was 334.980 (1982-84=100).

The September 2025 NSA CPI-U index was 324.800, and the August 2025 index was about 323.976. That makes the September 2025 month-over-month NSA change about +0.25%, and this month drops out of the year-over-year base. Arithmetic: a September 2026 rate that rounds to 3.7% or more needs an index of at least about 336.66, which is about +0.50% NSA from August 2026's 334.980. One link in the cited source was described only as a secondary site, so treat the 324.800 figure as unverified against the official BLS table.

The September 2026 CPI is scheduled for release on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET. The question closes at 12:29 UTC that day, which is 8:29 a.m. ET. No 2026 government shutdown affecting the release turned up.

Seasonally adjusted monthly changes in all-items CPI: Feb +0.3%, Mar +0.9%, Apr +0.6%, May +0.5%, Jun -0.4%, Jul +0.1%, Aug +0.4%. Core CPI was up 2.4% year over year in August, down from 2.5% in July.

recent_facts.fact: An average of the last 10 polls, updated 8 Oct 2026, has Likud 23, Yashar (Eisenkot) 22, B'Yachad (Bennett–Lapid) 11 and The Democrats 9. Shas, UTJ, Otzma Yehudit, Yisrael Beiteinu and the Joint List have 8 each, RZP–Zehut 6 and Ra'am 5. Bloc totals: Netanyahu bloc 53, Change bloc 50, Arab parties 13. No bloc reaches the 61 needed for a majority.

Latest individual polls for Likud/Yashar/B'Yachad: Zman Yisrael 8 Oct 20/24/13; Direct Polls/i24 8 Oct 26/20/11; Channel 14 7 Oct 31/23/8; Channel 13 7 Oct 20/20/12; Channel 12 5 Oct 21/23/13; Kan 4 Oct 21/23/12.
A Channel 13 poll put Netanyahu's bloc at 55 seats and Eisenkot's bloc, without the Arab parties, at 50. Neither reaches 61 without the Arab parties.

A Maariv poll gave the Netanyahu bloc 51 seats and the opposition 53. Yashar had 21, Likud 19, Bennett's Together 13 and Otzma Yehudit 9. A Channel 14 poll from early October gave the right-wing bloc 63 seats, with Likud at 32.

The election is on 27 Oct 2026, and official results are due to be confirmed on 4 Nov 2026. The question closes on 28 Oct 2026, so no post-election prime minister can be sworn in before it closes. Netanyahu stays in office as caretaker until a new government is sworn in, and caretaker status does not count for resolution.

After results are certified, the president has 7 days for consultations, then gives one MK 28 days to form a government, extendable by up to 14 days. If that fails, the mandate can go to another MK or to the Knesset (which needs 61 MKs backing one candidate), or new elections are triggered.

Gantz (Blue and White) has ruled out backing a Netanyahu government. Eisenkot said he would work with junior right-wing partners only if Netanyahu is no longer PM. Ra'am says it wants to replace the Netanyahu government, and the Joint List (Hadash, Ta'al, Balad, merged in late August) said it would 'do more than' back an opposition candidate. The threshold is 3.25%, and Netanyahu has warned that small right-wing parties falling below it could cost the right its majority.

Joint tickets: Bennett 2026 and Yesh Atid run as 'Together', headed by Bennett. RZP and Zehut merged, approved 6 Sep. Tropper joined Yashar, and Hendel allied with Zelekha's New Economic Party. The Unity party dropped out on 4 Sep. A Likud–New Hope merger had not been approved by the Knesset House Committee as of July. 38 lists were submitted.

At his May 2026 campaign launch, Avigdor Liberman vowed not to sit in a government with Netanyahu. Bennett has announced a 'no Arab parties' position. I found no explicit pledge from Bennett ruling out Netanyahu (unverified).

Eisenkot challenged Netanyahu to a televised debate, and as of the latest reports Netanyahu had not responded. Likud's campaign attacks Eisenkot's possible reliance on Ra'am's Mansour Abbas, Tibi, Golan and Liberman.
Remaining dates: surplus-vote agreement deadline 16 Oct, voting at diplomatic missions 20 Oct, election 27 Oct, official results confirmed 4 Nov 2026.

In 2022 the final Times of Israel polling average gave Netanyahu's bloc 60.3 seats; it won 64. In the final week it passed 61 in 6 of 15 polls. The extra seats came mostly because Meretz and Balad fell below the threshold, wasting about 290,000 votes, even though the blocs were only about 30,000 votes apart.

Recent gaps between election and swearing-in (from memory, unverified): 2022, election 1 Nov, Netanyahu sworn in 29 Dec, about 58 days. 2021, election 23 Mar, Bennett sworn in 13 Jun, after Netanyahu's mandate expired unused. 2019–2020, three elections with no new government until May 2020.
A late-September poll had Eisenkot's Yashar and Likud tied, with Smotrich's list at a new high. A late-September Kan poll had each bloc at 52 seats, with Yashar 23 and Likud 21.

market.question: Will Aleksandar Vučić be the next Prime Minister of Serbia?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to the next individual who officially assumes the office of Prime Minister of Serbia by June 30, 2028, 11:59 PM ET.

To count for resolution, the individual must be elected by the National Assembly and be formally sworn-in, resulting in the official formation of a new government. Any interim or caretaker Prime Minister who is not elected by the National Assembly will not count toward the resolution of this market.

If no such Prime Minister takes office by June 30, 2028, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

This market will resolve based on a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve solely based on official information from the Serbian government.

recent_facts.fact: Vučić dissolved the National Assembly and called snap parliamentary elections for 25 October 2026. The vote had been due by December 2027. He cited EXPO 2027 in Belgrade as one of his reasons. The question closes on the same day as the election.

Vučić resigned as president on 27 September, cutting his second term short by more than seven months. He is leading SNS in the election. AP reports that if his party wins a majority of seats, parliament is expected to elect him prime minister. He launched his campaign at a packed Belgrade arena on 3 October.

Vučić heads list no. 1, 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' (SNS-led, 209,130 signatures), as SNS's candidate for Prime Minister. All 250 seats are up and 126 are needed for a majority. Seats are allocated by d'Hondt in one nationwide constituency with a 3% threshold, and minority parties are exempt from the threshold.

Faktor Plus poll, 16–20 Sept, n=986: United Serbia 48.6% (+1.4), Student List 37.1% (+5.6), SPS 4.9%, European Serbia 3.6%, NADA 2.8%. Stated willingness to vote was 62%. Faktor Plus is described as pro-government-leaning. I found no October poll or independent poll.
The page says the SNS–Student List race has tightened. Some polls put SNS first and others put the Student List first. It gives no poll figures in its text.

The People's Serbia coalition withdrew its list on 22 September to back the Student List (list no. 3, ballot carrier Ilija Srdanović). Faktor Plus also said the People's Movement of Serbia, Ecological Uprising and New Face of Serbia had withdrawn, which consolidated the opposition vote.

Other lists: 'Factor of Stability!' led by Ivica Dačić (SPS, JS, SDPS, Zeleni), which is the ruling coalition's traditional partner; European Serbia (Tepić/Ponoš, SSP and SRCE); Authentic Right (NADA). Fifteen other lists, including minority lists, were also submitted.

In the 2024 cycle, parliament had one month to constitute itself after final results, then 90 days to form a government. The president nominates the PM-designate, who presents a programme and cabinet for an Assembly vote. If no government is elected in time, parliament is dissolved and new elections are called.

The question closes on 25 October 2026, election day. Any Assembly vote electing a new prime minister would come after the new parliament's constitutive session, about 30 days after final results, so it would fall after the close date. The resolution window runs to 30 June 2028.
In 2022, SNS took about 43% and roughly 120 seats. It stayed the largest party but lost its outright majority (126). It still formed a government with partners.

In 2020, the SNS-led 'For Our Children' coalition won 188 of 250 seats, a two-thirds majority, in a vote boycotted by most opposition parties. In 2016, SNS won 131 seats. SNS-led lists have finished first in every parliamentary election from 2014 to 2023. 2012 is not verified here.

This election follows about two years of student-led protests that began after the November 2024 Novi Sad railway station disaster, with more than 100,000 people protesting at the March 2025 peak. Vučić previously served as Serbia's prime minister from 2014 to 2017, before becoming president.
