market.question: Israel accuses Iran/proxies of plane stabbing incident by Oct 31?
market.rules:
On September 30, 2026, FlyDubai flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv diverted to Saudi Arabia following an incident in the cockpit in which the co-pilot allegedly stabbed the captain. (see: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/diverted-flydubai-flight-israel-was-not-hijacking-incident-israeli-prime-2026-09-30/).

This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Israeli national government, or an authorized representative of the Israeli national government, publicly announces that Iran or its affiliated groups deliberately caused this incident, by October 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A public announcement refers to an on-the-record statement issued by the Israeli national government or by its authorized representatives acting in an official capacity on behalf of the Israeli national government. A statement or press release issued by the Israeli national government or any of its agencies will qualify. A Prime Minister or Cabinet Minister’s public statements will always be considered to be issued on-the-record in a capacity representing the Israeli national government for purposes of this market. A statement from a lawmaker or other government official speaking in their own capacity or on behalf of a party not in government will not alone qualify.

For purposes of this market, an affiliated group of Iran is: any organization directly controlled by Iran, Hezbollah, Hamas, Palestinian Islamic Jihad, Houthis ("Ansar Allah"), Kata'ib Hezbollah, Asa'ib Ahl al-Haq, Badr Organization, and Harakat al-Nujaba. An unlisted group will only qualify if the Israeli claim itself, or accompanying statements or releases, specifies that the group is a proxy of or otherwise is controlled or directed by Iran. A general statement that it was conducted by an Iranian proxy will also qualify, even if no group is named.

Such a statement will be considered to claim that Iran or its affiliated groups deliberately caused the incident if it explicitly claims that Iran or an affiliated group ordered, carried out, planned, or otherwise directly aided or coordinated the incident. Statements that attribute only inspiration or ideological influence (e.g., "this would not have happened if Iran didn't radicalize terrorists," "the co-pilot was influenced by Hamas' ideas") will not qualify.

Once a qualifying announcement has been made, no subsequent walkback or retraction will be relevant for purposes of this market. 

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the Israeli national government; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

recent_facts.fact: Several U.S. officials briefed on the investigation and a former Israeli security official said early signs are that the co-pilot acted alone, not for a larger organization or a foreign government. A senior U.S. official briefed on Israel's investigation said there were no signs that Iran directed or took part in the attack. Officials stressed the investigation is still at an early stage.
Headline: 'Co-pilot accused of trying to hijack Flydubai plane probably acted alone, Israeli sources say.' Only the headline was available to us, not the article text.
Israeli sources told CBS that an early Israeli investigation suggests the co-pilot was probably not directed by a terrorist group or a nation and that this was likely a lone-wolf attack.

recent_facts.source: Al Jazeera / CBS News (via search summary)
recent_facts.fact: In a written statement, Netanyahu said the attacker 'underwent Islamist radicalization' and 'came to crash the plane with its passengers', adding: 'We are investigating whether he was dispatched, and whoever sent him will pay a very heavy price.' The statement did not name Iran. The quote comes from search-result summaries; we could not see which page carried the original text.

Netanyahu said it was too early to say whether Iran was involved and that he did not yet have information to attribute the incident to Tehran. He said Israel would join the probe and that this would be settled 'one way or another in a matter of days'.

On Fox News, Netanyahu said 'We know that he underwent Islamist radical indoctrination', citing personal information gathered during questioning. He also said the co-pilot was suicidal. He did not attribute the attack to Iran.

While admitting it was too early to establish a motive, Netanyahu pointed generally to Iran and its proxies as intent on stepping up attacks on Israelis abroad. Al Jazeera framed this as security messaging ahead of an Israeli election. We did not confirm the election date.

Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz called the incident 'an attempted jihadist terror attack' and called the co-pilot a 'terrorist'. He did not attribute it to Iran or any named group. Our sourcing for this quote is a search summary, so treat the exact page as unconfirmed.

recent_facts.source: South China Morning Post / Outlook India
recent_facts.fact: Asked whether he had been briefed on links between the co-pilot and Tehran, Trump said: 'I would say the answer, based on what I'm hearing, is yes, but we're working on it right now.' He vowed to hit Iran 'very hard' if it was involved. Outlook India later reported he said he 'personally' believed Iran was behind it. VP JD Vance said there was 'nothing conclusive'. These are U.S. statements, not Israeli ones, so they do not count toward resolution.

AP sources named the co-pilot as Omani national Hamam al-Hammami, who had been barred from flying by Omani authorities over extremism concerns. The UAE Attorney General called the attack a 'terrorist act' with a crash axe. Abu Dhabi leads the investigation and has not publicly given a motive or said whether he acted alone.

Reports say a joint UAE-Israel investigation is looking at the co-pilot's radicalisation in Syria and a possible link to an Iranian-backed terrorist group. AP reported that investigators had found no connection to a militant group so far.

Citing Channel 12 and Israel Hayom, NPR and Fox reported that the co-pilot told investigators he meant to crash the plane into Ben Gurion Airport. An Israeli investigative team has joined the UAE investigation.

The investigation is ongoing and final results on whether an organization or state was behind the attack are still pending. The UAE leads the probe, and an Israeli team is taking part. No date for findings has been announced.

market.question: Iran full airspace closure by October 31, 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Iran initiates a general closure of its airspace, that is not solely due to weather conditions, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A “general closure” refers to a cancellation or suspension of aviation which is generally applicable to all commercial flights transiting Iranian airspace (“Tehran FIR”). A qualifying closure must apply generally to all of Iran or the Tehran FIR; limited cancellations, delays, or partial closures will not qualify. A closure which applies generally to commercial aviation across Iranian airspace, with limited exceptions for certain categories of flights, however, will qualify (e.g. exceptions for certain flights pre-approved by the Iranian Civil Aviation Authority may be permitted).

Qualifying previous examples include the February 28, 2026 total closure of Iranian airspace (https://www.iranintl.com/en/202602289115) and the January 2026 total closure of Iranian airspace except to international flights with express governmental permission (https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iran-shuts-airspace-most-flights-flightradar24-says-2026-01-14/). Non-qualifying examples include the January 27, 2026 partial closure of Iranian airspace around the Strait of Hormuz (https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/iran-issues-airspace-notice-for-military-drills-near-strait-of-hormuz/3812508), the April 2024 closure of Iran’s western airspace (https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iranian-airports-cancel-flights-until-monday-morning-2024-04-14/), and the January 25 - April 25, 2026 VFR (Visual Flight Rules) flights suspension which did not broadly close commercial aviation in Iran (https://www.intellinews.com/iran-suspends-general-aviation-and-vfr-flights-in-new-airspace-directive-421997/).

Warnings, No-Fly-Zones, or other flight restrictions imposed by airlines or countries other than Iran will not be sufficient for a “Yes” resolution.

Airspace closures which occur solely due to weather conditions, earthquakes, or volcanic eruptions, will not qualify.

The primary resolution sources for this market will be official information from Iranian aviation authorities and a consensus of credible reporting.

recent_facts.fact: Cleveland beat the White Sox 9-5 in ALDS Game 4 at Rate Field on Oct. 8, 2026. They trailed 2-0 through four innings and scored six runs in the sixth. That tied the best-of-five series 2-2. The Game 5 winner advances to the ALCS against the Tampa Bay Rays.

The winner-take-all ALDS Game 5 is on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, at Progressive Field in Cleveland. MLB.com lists it at 8 p.m. ET on TBS/truTV/UniMas/HBO Max, though MLB's postseason FAQ lists 5 p.m. ET. Friday Oct. 9 is a travel day.
Results so far: Game 1 (Oct. 3, Cleveland): White Sox won 3-0. Game 2 (Oct. 5, Cleveland): White Sox won 4-3. Game 3 (Oct. 7, Chicago): Guardians won 9-3. Game 4 (Oct. 8, Chicago): Guardians won 9-5.

Gavin Williams threw 18 pitches to get the final three outs of Game 4 and is still named as a potential Game 5 starter. In Game 4, starter Parker Messick lasted only 2 1/3 innings. Reliever Grant Taylor, who had a four-inning save in Game 1, got no outs and was charged with four runs.
Williams went 14-8 with a 3.76 ERA in the 2026 regular season. He led the AL with 248 strikeouts in 184 1/3 innings. Neither team had officially named a Game 5 starter in the reports found.

White Sox manager Will Venable would only commit to Sean Burke pitching in some form in Game 5. Burke threw 5 1/3 innings of one-run, one-hit relief with six strikeouts in Game 2. Against Cleveland in the regular season he was 2-0 with a 1.04 ERA in three appearances (two starts).

Cleveland clinched its third straight AL Central title on Sept. 26 at 85-76, two games ahead of the White Sox (83-78), with one game left. Cleveland was the AL's No. 2 seed with a first-round bye. Chicago was the No. 6 seed and came through the Wild Card Series.

After Game 2 the White Sox were 4-0 in the 2026 postseason, all on the road, and went 48-33 at home in the regular season. Chicago is the first team to reach the postseason after three straight 100-loss seasons.
In mid-September, Cleveland (78-75) took two of three from Chicago to move a half-game ahead in the AL Central with nine games left.

market.question: Will the Republican Party control the House after the 2026 Midterm elections?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States House of Representatives in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States House of Representatives if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first elected Speaker of the House of the Congress that convenes after the 2026 midterm election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chamber.

All House elections in the 2026 United States midterm election that elect voting members and determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress are included. Where a seat is decided by a runoff, the runoff result will determine attribution of that seat.

Seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected.

House members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the House elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

recent_facts.fact: FiftyPlusOne's generic ballot average dated October 7, 2026 has Democrats at 51.2% and Republicans at 43.4%, a lead of about D+8.

Cook's House ratings: 185 Solid D, 12 Likely D, 11 Lean D (208 total leaning D), 22 Toss Up, 10 Lean R, 19 Likely R, 176 Solid R (205 total leaning R). Republicans hold 17 of the 22 toss-ups and Democrats hold 5. A majority takes 218 seats. These figures come from a search summary because the page itself returned a 403 error.
Cook's September 25, 2026 update moved 15 House race ratings toward Democrats.

The Iran war began in late February 2026. Net support for it is -27.9 (32.1% support, 60.0% oppose), the worst since it started. AAA regular gasoline averages $4.36 a gallon. The September jobs report showed +29,000 jobs with 60,000 in downward revisions, and unemployment rose to 4.2%.
The analysis says Republican-favoring redistricting means Democrats need to win the national House vote by about 3–4 points to win a House majority.
After ten states redrew their maps for 2026, Cook says the median House seat now has a Cook PVI of R+3. It calls the map more Republican-skewed and less elastic than before. (Date approximate.)

recent_facts.source: AP via Washington Examiner / Jim Ellis (via search summary)
recent_facts.fact: AP estimated Republicans could net about 10 House seats from redistricting if the new maps perform as designed (new maps in TX, MO, NC, OH, FL, TN, LA, AL, offset by Democratic gains in CA and UT). Jim Ellis put the Republican net gain at 8–12 seats after Virginia's Supreme Court struck down the Democratic map, which leaves Virginia's 6D-5R map in place. The date is approximate; I could not confirm the final status of the Florida, Louisiana and Alabama maps.
Olsen's analysis says a D+8.3 generic ballot corresponds to Democrats winning about 225 districts.

NPR reports that Cook lists 43 competitive districts, 22 of them toss-ups. Toss-ups include races in AZ, CA, CO, FL, IA, MI, NY, OH, PA, TX, VA and WI. Axios (September 25) reported House Republicans as 'on track to lose majority.'
Republicans won the House 220–215 in 2024. The current House is reported at 218 Republicans to 214 Democrats.

recent_facts.source: Gallup / secondary commentary (unverified against primary data)
recent_facts.fact: In 18 of the 20 midterms from 1946 to 2022, the president's party lost House seats; the exceptions were 1998 and 2002. When the president's approval was under 50%, his party lost an average of 37 House seats, compared with 14 when approval was over 50%.

Election day is November 3, 2026, and all 435 House seats are on the ballot. Both questions close on 2026-11-04 at 04:59 UTC, which is the night of the election, before many close races will have been called.

recent_facts.fact: After round 1 at Club de Campo Villa de Madrid, Eugenio Chacarra, Connor Syme and Grant Forrest led at 5 under (66). Angel Ayora and Sergio García were tied 4th at 4 under, one shot back.

Ayora shot 67 (−4) in round 1, a card that included two eagles and three bogeys. He was the provisional leader during the morning. Afterward he said that if his driver holds up, he will be near the top.

Round 2 is being played today (2026-10-09). I couldn't find any live or completed round 2 scores: the ESPN, Golf Post and Golf Channel leaderboard pages either returned nothing or blocked access. Ayora's standing after round 2 is not verified.
Co-leader Eugenio Chacarra has a foot injury. He said he did not yet know whether he could play round 2 and left open the possibility of withdrawing.

Ayora tees off at 13:50 Spanish time on Friday 9 October from the 1st tee, playing with Ludvig Åberg and Tyrrell Hatton. In round 1, Åberg shot even par and Hatton +5. The tournament has four rounds, 8–11 October, so it finishes Sunday 11 October.

Before the event, Jon Rahm (world #15) was listed as the highest-ranked player in the field, which also included Justin Rose, Shane Lowry, Ludvig Åberg, Tyrrell Hatton, Patrick Reed and defending champion Marco Penge (#53).
Spanish opening-day reports say Jon Rahm did not play because of the birth of his fourth child. Defending champion Marco Penge and Patrick Reed both opened at +2.

Ayora (born 2004) turned pro in 2023. His only professional win is the 2024 Rosa Challenge Tour event. On the DP World Tour he has no wins; his best finishes include T7 at the 2025 Italian Open (he led outright after 36 holes) and T8 at the 2025 DP World Tour Championship. He had ten top-10s in 2025. A single Challenge Tour win is weak evidence of an ability to close out a win.

In the 2026 season (as of July), Ayora had five DP World Tour top-10s, including T5 at the Qatar Masters, T3 at the KLM Open in June and solo 5th at the Open d'Italia in late June. He missed the cut at the Scottish Open, the PGA Championship and The Open, and was 22nd in the Race to Dubai at the time of The Open.
An undated PGA Tour profile gives Ayora's Official World Golf Ranking as 121. This figure may be out of date.
Ayora finished 9th at the 2025 Open de España at the same venue (Club de Campo Villa de Madrid). He is in his second DP World Tour season and has turned down LIV Golf offers.
The question resolves Yes only if Ayora wins the tournament. If he withdraws or does not tee off, the Tournament Winner market resolves No.

Moore suffered a concussion from a targeting hit in the Sept. 26 game at USC. He has practiced in a helmet and shoulder pads but has not been cleared.
Oregon won 41-27 at then-No. 12 USC on Sept. 26. Dylan Raiola replaced the injured Moore and went 19-of-25 for 289 yards, 2 TDs and no interceptions.
Oregon is 3-1 (1-0 Big Ten) and ranked No. 13 in the AP poll (Wikipedia lists No. 15). Results: beat Boise State 34-27, lost 31-39 at Oklahoma State, beat Portland State 84-0, and won 41-27 at USC.
Oregon was ranked No. 6 when it lost at Oklahoma State, which NBC Sports called the biggest upset of the 2026 season so far.
No. 21 UCLA is 4-0 (2-0 Big Ten) under first-year coach Bob Chesney, who came from James Madison. UCLA averages 44.8 points and 486.5 yards per game. Both teams had a bye last weekend.

UCLA won 54-3 at Maryland on Sept. 26, with four interceptions. Its other wins were 45-24 at Cal (Sept. 5), plus San Diego State and Purdue. Chesney is the first UCLA coach to start 4-0 in his first season since 1949.
UCLA's offense averages 281.5 rushing yards per game and 7.0 yards per carry. Oregon's defense allows opponents to convert 25.58% of third downs.

UCLA QB Nico Iamaleava has been seen grabbing his shoulder over recent weeks, and he left the Cal opener with a calf issue. No official report found lists him out for Oregon, and SI says the Bruins should have few players on the injury report after the bye.
UCLA leads the all-time series 40-33, but Oregon has won the last 5 meetings and 11 of the last 12.

market.question: Will the Democratic Party control the Senate after the 2026 Midterm elections?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States Senate in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States Senate if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the party that wins control of the chamber is the party that wins half of the voting seats and holds the Vice Presidency. If the outcome remains ambiguous after applying the above criteria, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first selected President Pro Tempore of the Congress that convenes after the specified election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chamber.

All regular and special Senate elections that determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress and are scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 are included. Runoffs for qualifying elections will determine attribution of the relevant seat, even if they take place after November 2026. Vacant seats for which no election or special election to fill the seat is scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 will be treated as held by the party affiliation of the most recent member to hold that seat.

For seats contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected.

For seats not contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party that holds the seat as of the date of the election. If a current sitting member of the U.S. Senate who is not up for election changes party affiliation or vacates their seat after the date of the election, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was affiliated at the time of the election.

Senate members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the Senate elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

recent_facts.fact: The Senate is currently 53 Republicans and 47 Democrats (45 Democrats plus 2 independents who caucus with them). 35 seats are up in 2026, including special elections in Florida and Ohio, and 65 are not up.

Republicans hold 23 and Democrats 12 of the 35 seats up in 2026. Democrats need a net gain of 4 seats for a 51-seat majority. Under the resolution rules, a 50-50 split goes to Republicans because the Vice President (JD Vance) is a Republican.

Cook rates 7 Senate races as Toss Up, all of them Republican-held: AK (Sullivan), IA (open), KS (Marshall), ME (Collins), MI (open, Democratic-held), OH (Husted) and TX (open). Note that MI is Democratic-held, so 6 of the 7 are Republican-held. Cook rates NH (open, D) as Lean Democrat and GA (Ossoff) and NC (open, R) as Likely Democrat.

On Oct 6 Cook moved Kansas from Lean Republican to Toss Up, New Hampshire from Toss Up to Lean Democrat and North Carolina from Lean Democrat to Likely Democrat. The analysis is titled 'A Senate Majority is Squarely in Democrats' Sights.'
Inside Elections' Oct 1 changes: Alaska moved from Tilt R to Toss-up, Georgia and North Carolina from Tilt D to Lean D, and Michigan from Toss-up to Tilt R.

RCP polling averages in Republican-held seats: NC Cooper (D) +9.0 over Whatley; ME Jackson (D) +0.7 over Collins; OH Brown (D) +3.2 over Husted; TX Talarico (D) +3.1 over Paxton; IA Turek (D) +0.7 over Hinson; AK Peltola (D) +1.8 over Sullivan.
RCP averages in Democratic-held battlegrounds: MI El-Sayed (D) +3.4 over Rogers; GA Ossoff (D) +7.8 over Mike Collins.

recent_facts.source: Decision Desk HQ / RealClearPolling (via search summary)
recent_facts.fact: Recent individual polls: ME Marist Jackson 51, Collins 47. OH CNN Brown 49, Husted 43, and co/efficient Husted 46, Brown 45. TX UMass Lowell 45-45 and YouGov Talarico 50, Paxton 44. IA CNN Hinson 45, Turek 43, and Suffolk Turek 48, Hinson 44. AK Alaska Survey Research Peltola 51, Sullivan 49 (ranked-choice voting). MI YouGov El-Sayed 49, Rogers 48. NC YouGov/Catawba Cooper 47, Whatley 35.

Kansas polls: Emerson/Nexstar (Sep 15-16) Hamilton (D) 45, Marshall (R) 43, Libertarian 4. co/efficient (Sep 8-10) Marshall 49, Hamilton 44. NYT/Siena Marshall 47, Hamilton 46. GSG (Aug) Hamilton 44, Marshall 43. PPP (Aug) Marshall 46, Hamilton 45. A Democrat has not won a Kansas Senate race since 1932.
Republicans in Kansas Senate races beat their polls in both 2014 and 2020. Trump's approval in Kansas was 40% in the NYT/Siena poll.

In Nebraska, independent Dan Osborn and Sen. Pete Ricketts (R) were tied 47-47 with 5% undecided in an Impact Research poll released by the Osborn campaign (date unverified). The Ricketts campaign said Osborn's internal polls were off by 12 points in 2024. Osborn has not committed to caucusing with Democrats, which matters under the resolution's independent-caucus rule.

In the three cycles before 2022, more than half of late battleground-state polls missed by more than 3 points. In 2016 and 2020 almost all of the error ran toward Democrats (Republicans outperformed their polls). Example: in Maine in 2020, no poll showed Collins leading, and she won by 9 points.

Wang estimated that national Senate polling error in midterm years is about five times larger than in presidential years and can run in either direction. Republicans outperformed their polls in the 1994 and 2002 midterms.
Generic ballot (dated): Data for Progress had Democrats +8 in May 2026. A tracker average from spring 2026 was about D+5. No October 2026 generic-ballot reading was found.

Election Day is November 3, 2026, and the question closes Nov 4 at 04:59 UTC. Alaska's ranked-choice count and any runoffs (such as Georgia's, if no one gets 50%) could settle seats after Election Day, and runoffs count under the rules.

market.question: Will **real GDP** increase by more than 4.0% in Q3 2026? (Above 4.0%)
market.rules:
If real GDP (as measured by the BEA’s seasonally adjusted and annualized Advance Estimate) increases by more than 4.0, then the market resolves to Yes.
The market will close at 8:29 AM on the day of the expected release of the data. The market will expire at the first 10:00 AM following the release of the data for Q3 2026, or 3 months following that expected date of data release. Please note the Expiration Value is the one-decimal value published by the BEA.

recent_facts.fact: BEA plans to release the advance estimate of Q3 2026 GDP on Thursday, October 29, 2026, at 8:30 AM ET. This is the release that settles the market, and the market closes at 8:29 AM that day.

BEA's third estimate put Q2 2026 real GDP growth at a 2.2% annual rate, revised up 0.7 points from the 1.5% second estimate. Higher investment, consumer spending and government spending drove the revision. Q1 2026 was revised to 2.5%.

The August 2026 goods and services trade deficit widened to $105.6 billion, from a revised $92.8 billion in July. That is the largest gap since March 2025, and consensus had been $102.0 billion. Imports rose $17.2 billion to a record $420.8 billion, while exports rose $4.5 billion to $315.2 billion.

Capital goods imports hit a record $146.4 billion in August, up 57.9% from a year earlier, led by semiconductors and aircraft. About two-thirds of the rise in industrial supplies imports came from crude oil and nonmonetary gold. The three-month average deficit through August was $89.9 billion.

August 2026 retail sales rose 1.2% month over month to $773.9 billion, against an expected rise of about 0.8%, and were up 6.0% year over year. Sales excluding autos rose 1.4%. TD estimated real sales rose 0.8% and said real Q3 consumer spending was running at about a 3% annualized pace.

BEA reported that August 2026 personal consumption expenditures rose 0.9% and personal income rose 0.2%. The saving rate was 4.1%, and July PCE was shown at +0.1%. The date is approximate: these are figures from the late-September personal income release.

In 2025, a government shutdown cancelled the scheduled October 30 Q3 advance release. The first Q3 2025 estimate (4.3%) did not come out until December 23, 2025. This shows the release date can slip. As of October 2, 2026, no shutdown delays to federal data releases had been reported.
Recent first prints: Q3 2025 was first reported at 4.3%, later revised to 4.4%. The Q4 2025 advance estimate was 1.4% (second estimate 0.7%). Q1 and Q2 2026 currently stand at 2.5% and 2.2%.

A 2018 commentary counted 6 of 50 quarters from 2005 to 2018 with growth above 4%. recent_facts.fact: The all-items CPI-U rose 3.4% (not seasonally adjusted) in the 12 months ending August 2026, the same rate as for the 12 months ending July. The NSA index level for August 2026 was 334.980 (1982-84=100).

The September 2025 NSA CPI-U index was 324.800, and the August 2025 index was about 323.976. That makes the September 2025 month-over-month NSA change about +0.25%, and this month drops out of the year-over-year base. Arithmetic: a September 2026 rate that rounds to 3.7% or more needs an index of at least about 336.66, which is about +0.50% NSA from August 2026's 334.980. One link in the cited source was described only as a secondary site, so treat the 324.800 figure as unverified against the official BLS table.

The September 2026 CPI is scheduled for release on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET. The question closes at 12:29 UTC that day, which is 8:29 a.m. ET. No 2026 government shutdown affecting the release turned up.

Seasonally adjusted monthly changes in all-items CPI: Feb +0.3%, Mar +0.9%, Apr +0.6%, May +0.5%, Jun -0.4%, Jul +0.1%, Aug +0.4%. Core CPI was up 2.4% year over year in August, down from 2.5% in July.

In August, energy rose 2.1% and gasoline rose 3.9% seasonally adjusted (2.5% NSA). Gasoline made up more than a third of the monthly all-items increase. Energy was up 16.3% and gasoline 27.4% over 12 months.

AAA called September 2026 a record-setting month at the pump, with a monthly average of $4.33 per gallon. The national average was $4.14 on Sep 3, $4.27 on Sep 10, $4.43 on Sep 17, and peaked at $4.48 on Sep 24. By Oct 1 it had fallen to $4.41.
EIA data put the monthly average for regular gasoline at $4.36 in September 2026, compared with $4.06 in August and $3.93 in July. That is roughly a 7% rise from August to September.
AAA linked the September price increases to rising crude oil costs and lingering volatility in the Strait of Hormuz.

The headline 12-month CPI-U change BLS reports is the not-seasonally-adjusted change, rounded to one decimal place. For the question to resolve Yes, the published figure must be 3.7% or higher; a reading of exactly 3.6% resolves No.

market.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (HIGH) $95 in October?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

On Oct 8, WTI futures were up 5% at $92.70 and Brent was up 5.2% at $105.36, after Middle East tensions rose and nine tankers were attacked in and around Hormuz over the past week.

Trading Economics (CFD-based) showed WTI topping $92.6 on Oct 8, its highest in nearly a month, after falling below $89 on Oct 7, its lowest in over a month. It said prices were down about 16% from a September four-month peak as of Oct 7.

The White House reportedly asked the Pentagon for strike options against Iranian targets that could be carried out before the November midterms. The Pentagon reportedly told CENTCOM to finish preparations to resume combat operations in Iran.

Other drivers on Oct 8: tanker attacks in Hormuz last week were the highest weekly level since the war began; about 25% of US Gulf oil output was shut ahead of Tropical Storm Isaias; EIA crude stocks fell by over 3 million barrels; Saudi Arabia cut its official selling prices, and tankers resumed loading in the Gulf.

In September 2026, front-month WTI daily highs ranged widely: 105.63 on Sep 16, 101.69 on Sep 15, 97.22 on Sep 21, 96.78 on Sep 24 and 96.54 on Sep 28. Between Sep 15 and Sep 28, 8 of 10 sessions had highs at or above $95.

WTI closes in 2026 above $100 included Apr 1–2 ($111.54), Apr 29 ($106.88) and Sep 17 ($101.91). Intraday WTI reached nearly $120 in early March. Across the Iran-war period, WTI has repeatedly moved $10+ within a few weeks, e.g. $83.85 on Apr 17 to $106.88 on Apr 29.

Recent swings: WTI jumped 6% to $92.19 on Jul 23 on tanker attacks; it rose from $83.40 (week of Aug 28) to $96.05 on Sep 9 and $101.91 on Sep 17 as US-Iran fighting escalated. Earlier, it fell over 16% in one day on Apr 8 after a ceasefire announcement.

Resolution uses the Pyth 'CLL' feed of the ICE WTI Active Month futures contract, not spot. The EIA Cushing spot series runs well above futures: 97.89 on Oct 2 and 96.24 on Oct 6, against front-month futures closes of 91.11 and 89.44.

Wikipedia lists no independent candidates as having qualified: Tim Rich did not qualify and Phillip Rench withdrew. That suggests a two-candidate ballot, so a ranked-choice runoff is unlikely to matter.

Graham Platner won the June Democratic primary. He withdrew on July 10, 2026, after sexual assault accusations and other controversies. A Democratic nominating convention chose Troy Jackson to replace him on July 25, 2026.
Marist poll, Oct 1–4, 1,505 registered voters (±3.8%): Jackson 51%, Collins 47%, other 1%, undecided 1%.

Late-September polls: Maine People's Resource Center (Sep 25–29): Jackson 49, Collins 47. InsiderAdvantage (R) (Sep 22–23): 46–46. Fabrizio Ward/Impact Research (Sep 20–22): Jackson 50, Collins 47. NYT/Siena (Sep 15–22, 619 LV): Collins 49, Jackson 46. UNH (Sep 17–21, 1,312 LV): Jackson 51, Collins 47.

Polling averages for Sep 20–Oct 4: 270toWin had Jackson 49.1%, Collins 47.6%. The average across aggregators was Jackson 48.8%, Collins 47.2%. RealClearPolling showed a near tie, Jackson 47.6% to Collins 47.5%.

Jackson led or tied Collins in every listed poll from mid-July to mid-September. Examples: UNH Jul 15–20, Jackson 49–46. Hart (D), Jackson 49–45. UMass/YouGov Aug 28–Sep 14, Jackson 48–43. Rasmussen (R), Sep 8–10, Jackson 46–45. Exceptions: the Abacus registered-voter version had Collins 46–45, and Quantus (Sep 14–15) had Collins 48–47.

In 2020, Democrat Sara Gideon led nearly every public poll and finished 6.5 points ahead in the RealClearPolitics average. Collins still won with just under 51% of the vote, a margin of roughly 8–9 points (about 8.6 by recollection, not verified from the sources). That puts the polling miss at about 15 points in Collins's favor.
Unverified recollection: Collins has won all 5 of her Senate general elections (1996, 2002, 2008, 2014, 2020).
Second debate (WMTW, Oct 8) was testy. Jackson accused Collins and her husband of profiting from the Iran war, without offering specific evidence. The two candidates accused each other of corruption.

About a week before Oct 8, ProPublica reported that the FBI sought to investigate bribery claims involving Collins, tied to $150,000 that convicted contractor Martin Kao says he routed to a pro-Collins super PAC. ProPublica says the probe was dropped after Trump returned to office. Collins's campaign calls the allegations recycled and says she was cleared. Jackson called it 'corruption of the highest order.'
As of June 30, 2026, Collins had raised $18.9M and had $11.0M cash on hand. Jackson was not yet a candidate then and shows $0. Trump has not endorsed Collins.
Two more debates are scheduled: Oct 13 (WABI/WAGM) and Oct 15 (News Center Maine/Portland Press Herald/Maine Public). Election day is November 3, 2026.

Maine uses ranked-choice voting for U.S. Senate races. The question resolves once AP, Fox News and NBC all call the race for the same candidate, and otherwise on official certification. Jackson, as the replacement Democratic nominee, counts as the Democrat.

market.question: Will Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia win the most seats in the 2026 Serbian parliamentary election?
market.rules:
Parliamentary elections to elect the 250 members of the National Assembly of Serbia are scheduled to take place on October 25, 2026.

This market will resolve to the electoral list that wins the greatest number of seats in the National Assembly of Serbia as a result of this election.

Electoral lists will be primarily ranked by the number of seats won in the specified election. If two or more lists are tied on seats, ties will be broken by the total number of valid votes received, with higher vote totals ranking higher. If lists remain tied, ties will be broken by alphabetical order of the listed names. This market will resolve to the list that occupies the highest finishing position after applying this ranking.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the named electoral list, as it appears on the ballot and official proclamations, regardless of which parties make up the list or how its members later organize themselves in the National Assembly.

If the results of the specified election are not definitively known by March 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the results of the elections, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. In the case of ambiguity, this market will resolve solely based on the results as reported by the Republic Electoral Commission of Serbia (https://www.rik.parlament.gov.rs/).

recent_facts.fact: In the Faktor Plus poll fielded 16–20 Sep 2026 (n=986), the Vučić-led list was at 48.6% and the Student List at 37.1%, a gain of 5.6 points for the Student List since the previous poll. balk.hu describes Faktor Plus as close to the ruling SNS, and its director denies any manipulation.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia – Opinion polling for the 2026 Serbian parliamentary election
recent_facts.fact: Opposition and independent media accuse Ipsos and Faktor Plus of pro-government bias. A Bureau for Social Research study found that most Serbian pollsters do not disclose weighting or funding. CRTA's July poll left out 12.2% undecided, and an April NSPM scenario poll left out 21% undecided.

RIK accepted 18 lists and 1 was withdrawn. List #1 is 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' (SNS, PUPS, SRS, ZS and others; 209,130 signatures). List #3 is 'Student List – Students Are Winning', headed by Ilija Srdanović (69,099 signatures). SPS–JS (Dačić) is running separately as list #2.

Vučić resigned as president on 27 Sep 2026 to lead the SNS list as its prime ministerial candidate. The snap election was announced on 8–9 Sep and set for 25 Oct, more than a year before the regular vote due in late 2027.

Several opposition groups consolidated behind the Student List. The People's Serbia coalition (NPS, NLS, EU) withdrew its list on 22 Sep to back it, after NLS and EU had endorsed it on 15 Sep. PSG left the PES coalition in late September to support the Student List. PES (SSP/SRCE, Tepić/Ponoš) is still running separately as list #9 but has said it will cooperate with the Student List.

In late September, pro-government tabloids ran campaigns against Student List leader Srdanović, which fact-checkers said used AI-manipulated photos. Televised debates are scheduled on RTS, N1, Nova and Radio Belgrade from 29 Sep to 8 Oct.

Vreme reports that polls are dominated by two blocs, 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' and the Student List. A September NSPM survey suggested that Dačić's SPS may struggle to clear the 3% threshold.

The CRTA / Stanford Democracy Action Lab survey (June fieldwork, n=2,324) put the Student List at 44.9% and SNS at 35.7% among decided voters. It was the first published poll to show the Student List ahead.
No Ipsos, CRTA or other poll fielded in October 2026 turned up. The most recent published polls are Faktor Plus (21 Sep) and NSPM (30 Sep, fieldwork early September).

In the December 2023 snap election, preliminary results gave the SNS list 47.95% and Serbia Against Violence 24.32%, with SPS at 6.75%. Ipsos/CeSID exit polls (about 47% vs 23%) were close to the count. Unverified recollection: an SNS-led list has won the most seats in every parliamentary election since 2012 (2012, 2014, 2016, 2020, 2022, 2023), 6 of 6.

All 250 seats are elected by nationwide proportional representation with a 3% threshold. Minority lists, including #4, 5, 6, 10, 14, 15, 17 and 18, are exempt from the threshold. The question resolves on seats won by the ballot-named list, with ties broken by votes.
Election day is 25 Oct 2026, the same day the question closes. RIK (rik.parlament.gov.rs) publishes the preliminary and final results.

market.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (HIGH) $100 in October?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

On Oct 8, WTI futures were up 5% at $92.70 and Brent was up 5.2% at $105.36, after Middle East tensions rose and nine tankers were attacked in and around Hormuz over the past week.

Trading Economics (CFD-based) showed WTI topping $92.6 on Oct 8, its highest in nearly a month, after falling below $89 on Oct 7, its lowest in over a month. It said prices were down about 16% from a September four-month peak as of Oct 7.

The White House reportedly asked the Pentagon for strike options against Iranian targets that could be carried out before the November midterms. The Pentagon reportedly told CENTCOM to finish preparations to resume combat operations in Iran.

Other drivers on Oct 8: tanker attacks in Hormuz last week were the highest weekly level since the war began; about 25% of US Gulf oil output was shut ahead of Tropical Storm Isaias; EIA crude stocks fell by over 3 million barrels; Saudi Arabia cut its official selling prices, and tankers resumed loading in the Gulf.

In September 2026, front-month WTI daily highs ranged widely: 105.63 on Sep 16, 101.69 on Sep 15, 97.22 on Sep 21, 96.78 on Sep 24 and 96.54 on Sep 28. Between Sep 15 and Sep 28, 8 of 10 sessions had highs at or above $95.

WTI closes in 2026 above $100 included Apr 1–2 ($111.54), Apr 29 ($106.88) and Sep 17 ($101.91). Intraday WTI reached nearly $120 in early March. Across the Iran-war period, WTI has repeatedly moved $10+ within a few weeks, e.g. $83.85 on Apr 17 to $106.88 on Apr 29.

market.question: Baycurrent Classic: Ben Kohles wins
market.rules:
If Ben Kohles wins the Baycurrent Classic, then the market resolves to Yes.
If a golfer forfeits, withdraws, or does not participate prior to teeing off, their contracts will resolve as follows:
Tournament Winner and End of Round Leader markets will resolve to No
Finishing Position, Make the Cut, Head-to-Head, and 3-Ball markets will resolve to Fair Market Value

recent_facts.fact: Standings after 36 holes: Keith Mitchell and Jacob Bridgeman tied for 1st at -11. Max Homa, Zach Bauchou, Ben Kohles and Mac Meissner tied for 3rd at -9. Justin Thomas, Stephan Jaeger and Min Woo Lee tied for 7th at -8. Jordan Smith, Michael Brennan and Ricky Castillo are at -7, and Christiaan Bezuidenhout, Adam Scott and Michael Kim at -6.

Kohles shot 62 in Round 2, the tournament's low round so far, with seven birdies and an eagle on the par-5 6th. Homa shot 68 after an opening 65; he birdied five straight holes (2–6) but made a double bogey on the 14th. Min Woo Lee shot 67-67. Mitchell shot 65 in Round 2, and Bridgeman followed an opening 63 with a 68.

The event has a 72-player field with no cut, played over 72 holes at Yokohama Country Club (par 71, 7,322 yards). The purse is $8 million, with $1.44 million going to the winner. All three named players have teed off, so the withdrawal-before-tee-off clause no longer applies.

Round 3 starts the evening of Oct 9 ET (Oct 10 local time in Japan) and the final round is Oct 11 local time. Mitchell, Bridgeman and Homa play together in the final group at 9:36 p.m. ET. Kohles plays with Bauchou and Meissner.

Kohles has no PGA Tour win in 127 career starts, though he has five Korn Ferry Tour titles, the most recent in June 2026. He is No. 84 in the FedExCup, needs to finish top 100 to keep his card, and skipped the Korn Ferry Tour Championship to play this event. His opening round was even par.

Kohles's recent results: T13 at the Bank of Utah Championship, T15 at the FedExCup Fall event in Asheville, and T27 at the Korn Ferry Tour Finals opener. He leads the PGA Tour in driving accuracy (79.34%) and greens in regulation (74.19%).

Homa has six career PGA Tour wins, but none in 2026 and none since 2023. His best 2026 finish was 2nd at the John Deere Classic in July. He was T26 at the Bank of Utah Championship the week before this event, and he finished T40 (2025) and T27 (2024) at this tournament.
Kohles tied for 3rd at the 2026 John Deere Classic at -18 (65-67-66-68), then tied for 15th at the ISCO Championship at -11.
From 2010 to about 2015–16, PGA Tour 36-hole leaders and co-leaders went on to win about 30.5–31% of the time. This is an older sample, and no figure was found for players two or three shots back.
Since November 2018, 54-hole leaders on the PGA Tour have converted 134 times, a 39.5% win rate.

Other notable names in the field include defending champion Xander Schauffele, Collin Morikawa, Justin Thomas, Jordan Spieth, Hideki Matsuyama, Keegan Bradley and Adam Scott. After 36 holes, Schauffele and Matsuyama are both tied for 30th at -3.

market.rules:
This market will immediately resolve to "Yes" if any Binance 1 minute candle for BTC/USDT during the month specified in the title (from 00:00 AM ET on the first day to 11:59 PM ET on the last), has a final Low price equal to or lower than the price specified in the title. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

The resolution source for this market is Binance, specifically the BTC/USDT Low prices available at https://www.binance.com/en/trade/BTC_USDT, with the chart settings on "1m" for one-minute candles selected on the top bar.

Please note that the outcome of this market depends solely on the price data from the Binance BTC/USDT trading pair. Prices from other exchanges, different trading pairs, or spot markets will not be considered for the resolution of this market.

recent_facts.fact: Same-day Oct 9 snapshots ranged from $81,778 (OKX) and $81,905 (CoinGabbar, down 1.5% over 24h) to $82,577 (CoinGecko) and $82,922 (Analytics Insight, down 1.8% over 24h). The lowest of these is about 5.2% above $77,500.

Early Monday, Oct 5, BTC peaked 'just shy of $86,950', about $1,950 (2.3%) above the $85,000 strike. It then fell to just under $86,000. Whether this counts for the $85K question depends on the market's creation date, which I could not find, because price action before creation is excluded.

CoinDesk reported that BTC was turned back from just above $87,000 on Monday, Oct 5. It said this was the third time since Sept. 23 that the level had capped a rally. The late-September high was about $87,400.

On Oct 2, BTC briefly topped $87,000, then fell below $84,000, with about $570M in liquidations over 24 hours. By Oct 3 it had slipped to about $84,600 after $433M in liquidations, mostly of long positions.
The Oct 7 intraday range was a $86,634 high and a $83,693 low, so BTC again traded above $85,000 on Oct 7. The page did not list any strike as resolved and gave no market creation date.

BTC was $83,448 at 9:30 a.m. ET on Oct 1, 2026, and about $86,682 on the morning of Oct 2. In the reports I found, October's lowest level so far is about $81,700–82,000 on Oct 9, still well above $77,500 and $72,500.

On Thursday, Oct 8, BTC was $82,926, down more than 4% on the week, after closing below $85,000 on Oct 7. The 50-day EMA was about $79,704, the 100-day about $75,857 and the 200-day about $75,242. The earlier horizontal floors were $66,500 and $62,300.
US spot Bitcoin ETFs had $487.07M of net outflows on Wednesday, Oct 7, the largest single day of withdrawals since June 25.

The 10-year Treasury yield hit about 5.30–5.36% intraday on Oct 7, its highest since 2002, and the dollar index reached 102.53 on Monday. Minutes from the Sept 15–16 FOMC meeting showed a unanimous rate hike, with most officials expecting another increase by year-end.

On Oct 8, US government-linked wallets moved about $566M in assets to exchanges, mostly Coinbase Prime, and a dormant whale moved 4,500 BTC. Reports also said the Pentagon had told CENTCOM to prepare to resume major combat operations in Iran.
On Oct 9, total crypto market cap fell 2.5%. Admiral Markets described Thursday, Oct 8, as BTC/USD's fourth straight daily loss.

recent_facts.fact: After round 1 at Club de Campo Villa de Madrid, Eugenio Chacarra, Connor Syme and Grant Forrest led at 5 under (66). Angel Ayora and Sergio García were tied 4th at 4 under, one shot back.

Ayora shot 67 (−4) in round 1, a card that included two eagles and three bogeys. He was the provisional leader during the morning. Afterward he said that if his driver holds up, he will be near the top.

Round 2 is being played today (2026-10-09). I couldn't find any live or completed round 2 scores: the ESPN, Golf Post and Golf Channel leaderboard pages either returned nothing or blocked access. Ayora's standing after round 2 is not verified.
Co-leader Eugenio Chacarra has a foot injury. He said he did not yet know whether he could play round 2 and left open the possibility of withdrawing.

market.question: Will the Democrats win the Texas Senate race in 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the 2026 midterm Texas U.S. Senate election, inclusive of any run-offs.

A candidate shall be considered to represent a party in the event that he or she is the nominee of the party in question. Candidates other than the Democratic or Republican nominee (e.g., Greens, Libertarian, independent) may be added at a later date.

Candidates who run as independents will not be encompassed by the “Democrat” or “Republican” options regardless of any affiliation they may have with the party.

The candidates may be named in the contract for the convenience of traders. In the event that any named candidate is replaced as the nominee of their respective party prior to election day, the name in the contract will be updated and the market will resolve based on the replacement nominee of the party.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race in this state for the same candidate, this market will resolve based on the official certification.

recent_facts.fact: In a poll of 850 likely voters taken Sept. 18–28, 2026 (MoE ±4.5), Talarico and Paxton were tied at 45% each, with Libertarian Ted Brown at 2%, another candidate at 1% and 7% undecided. The same poll had Abbott (R) ahead of Hinojosa (D) 48–44 for governor and Trump's job approval at 47% approve, 53% disapprove.

recent_facts.source: Fox News poll via FOX 7 Austin
recent_facts.fact: A Fox News poll by Beacon Research (D) and Shaw & Company (R) of 881 likely voters, taken Sept. 24–28, had Talarico at 51% and Paxton at 49% (MoE ±3). Talarico's favorability was 52% favorable and 44% unfavorable; Paxton's was 40% and 58%.

A secondhand excerpt of a New York Times/Siena poll taken Sept. 21–30, 2026 reports Talarico ahead of Paxton by 6 points; the full numbers were not verified. The June 19–27 NYT/Siena poll of 656 likely voters had the race tied.

A Siena College/ReconMR poll taken Sept. 8–11 had Talarico at 49% and Paxton at 43%. An Emerson poll taken Sept. 12–14 had Talarico at 47% and Paxton at 46%. A poll sponsored by Paxton's campaign had Paxton at 48% and Talarico at 45%.
The Pollsmax average of 40 polls shows Talarico at 48.4% and Paxton at 44.7%, a 3.7-point Talarico lead. It lists a YouGov poll dated Oct. 5 with Talarico at 50% and Paxton at 44%.

recent_facts.source: Newsweek analysis (polling averages not independently verified)
recent_facts.fact: Final Texas Senate polling averages compared with results: in 2018 polls had Cruz up about 6–7 and he won by 2.6 (polls overstated the Republican). In 2020 RCP had Cornyn up about 7 and he won by 9.6–9.8. In 2024 polls had Cruz up about 4 and he won by 8.5. In 2024, Emerson's final poll had Cruz 48–47.

Democrats have not won a statewide race in Texas in more than 30 years. The last Democratic statewide win was in 1994, and the last Democratic U.S. Senate win in Texas was in 1988. Republicans won all of the roughly 10 Texas Senate elections from 1990 through 2024 (recalled count, unverified).

Texas PAC, a super PAC affiliated with the Senate Leadership Fund, spent $61 million in two days and $131 million in 17 days to boost Paxton and attack Talarico. Talarico's campaign had booked about $35 million in ads for the final two months, putting it on track to be outspent nearly 5 to 1 by pro-Paxton groups.
AdImpact projects total spending on the race will reach about $440 million by Nov. 3, more than double the previous Texas Senate record.

Talarico raised more than three times Paxton's total in Q2 2026 and ended June with $23.3 million on hand, more than triple Paxton's. Since the start of 2025, Talarico's campaign has raised a cumulative $72.0 million to Paxton's $16.8 million.
Talarico agreed to three debates and challenged Paxton to debate. As of that report, Paxton had not committed to any debate.

The general election is Nov. 3, 2026. Texas has no general-election runoff, so a plurality wins. Early voting in Texas usually starts about two weeks before Election Day (around Oct. 19; recalled, not checked).
The question resolves when AP, Fox News and NBC have all called the race for the same candidate, or on official certification if they haven't. The Republican nominee is Paxton.

market.question: Will the Republican Party control the Senate after the 2026 Midterm elections?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States Senate in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States Senate if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the party that wins control of the chamber is the party that wins half of the voting seats and holds the Vice Presidency. If the outcome remains ambiguous after applying the above criteria, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first selected President Pro Tempore of the Congress that convenes after the specified election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chamber.

All regular and special Senate elections that determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress and are scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 are included. Runoffs for qualifying elections will determine attribution of the relevant seat, even if they take place after November 2026. Vacant seats for which no election or special election to fill the seat is scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 will be treated as held by the party affiliation of the most recent member to hold that seat.

For seats contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected.

For seats not contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party that holds the seat as of the date of the election. If a current sitting member of the U.S. Senate who is not up for election changes party affiliation or vacates their seat after the date of the election, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was affiliated at the time of the election.

Senate members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the Senate elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

recent_facts.fact: The Senate is currently 53 Republicans and 47 Democrats (45 Democrats plus 2 independents who caucus with them). 35 seats are up in 2026, including special elections in Florida and Ohio, and 65 are not up.

Republicans hold 23 and Democrats 12 of the 35 seats up in 2026. Democrats need a net gain of 4 seats for a 51-seat majority. Under the resolution rules, a 50-50 split goes to Republicans because the Vice President (JD Vance) is a Republican.

Cook rates 7 Senate races as Toss Up, all of them Republican-held: AK (Sullivan), IA (open), KS (Marshall), ME (Collins), MI (open, Democratic-held), OH (Husted) and TX (open). Note that MI is Democratic-held, so 6 of the 7 are Republican-held. Cook rates NH (open, D) as Lean Democrat and GA (Ossoff) and NC (open, R) as Likely Democrat.

On Oct 6 Cook moved Kansas from Lean Republican to Toss Up, New Hampshire from Toss Up to Lean Democrat and North Carolina from Lean Democrat to Likely Democrat. The analysis is titled 'A Senate Majority is Squarely in Democrats' Sights.'
Inside Elections' Oct 1 changes: Alaska moved from Tilt R to Toss-up, Georgia and North Carolina from Tilt D to Lean D, and Michigan from Toss-up to Tilt R.

RCP polling averages in Republican-held seats: NC Cooper (D) +9.0 over Whatley; ME Jackson (D) +0.7 over Collins; OH Brown (D) +3.2 over Husted; TX Talarico (D) +3.1 over Paxton; IA Turek (D) +0.7 over Hinson; AK Peltola (D) +1.8 over Sullivan.
RCP averages in Democratic-held battlegrounds: MI El-Sayed (D) +3.4 over Rogers; GA Ossoff (D) +7.8 over Mike Collins.

recent_facts.source: Decision Desk HQ / RealClearPolling (via search summary)
recent_facts.fact: Recent individual polls: ME Marist Jackson 51, Collins 47. OH CNN Brown 49, Husted 43, and co/efficient Husted 46, Brown 45. TX UMass Lowell 45-45 and YouGov Talarico 50, Paxton 44. IA CNN Hinson 45, Turek 43, and Suffolk Turek 48, Hinson 44. AK Alaska Survey Research Peltola 51, Sullivan 49 (ranked-choice voting). MI YouGov El-Sayed 49, Rogers 48. NC YouGov/Catawba Cooper 47, Whatley 35.

Kansas polls: Emerson/Nexstar (Sep 15-16) Hamilton (D) 45, Marshall (R) 43, Libertarian 4. co/efficient (Sep 8-10) Marshall 49, Hamilton 44. NYT/Siena Marshall 47, Hamilton 46. GSG (Aug) Hamilton 44, Marshall 43. PPP (Aug) Marshall 46, Hamilton 45. A Democrat has not won a Kansas Senate race since 1932.
Republicans in Kansas Senate races beat their polls in both 2014 and 2020. Trump's approval in Kansas was 40% in the NYT/Siena poll.

In Nebraska, independent Dan Osborn and Sen. Pete Ricketts (R) were tied 47-47 with 5% undecided in an Impact Research poll released by the Osborn campaign (date unverified). The Ricketts campaign said Osborn's internal polls were off by 12 points in 2024. Osborn has not committed to caucusing with Democrats, which matters under the resolution's independent-caucus rule.

In the three cycles before 2022, more than half of late battleground-state polls missed by more than 3 points. In 2016 and 2020 almost all of the error ran toward Democrats (Republicans outperformed their polls). Example: in Maine in 2020, no poll showed Collins leading, and she won by 9 points.

Wang estimated that national Senate polling error in midterm years is about five times larger than in presidential years and can run in either direction. Republicans outperformed their polls in the 1994 and 2002 midterms.
Generic ballot (dated): Data for Progress had Democrats +8 in May 2026. A tracker average from spring 2026 was about D+5. No October 2026 generic-ballot reading was found.

Election Day is November 3, 2026, and the question closes Nov 4 at 04:59 UTC. Alaska's ranked-choice count and any runoffs (such as Georgia's, if no one gets 50%) could settle seats after Election Day, and runoffs count under the rules.

recent_facts.fact: RealClearPolling's average of polls from Sept. 15 to Oct. 6 has Democrat Abdul El-Sayed at 48.1% and Republican Mike Rogers at 44.9%, a lead of 3.2 points for El-Sayed. The page may have been cached.
FiftyPlusOne's Michigan Senate polling average as of Oct. 8 has El-Sayed at 48.0% and Rogers at 44.5%.
Quantus Insights polled 744 likely voters on Oct. 5–6 and found El-Sayed at 48% and Rogers at 47%. A YouGov poll fielded Sept. 28–Oct. 5 had El-Sayed at 49% and Rogers at 48%.

A Mitchell Research poll fielded Oct. 1 has El-Sayed at 45.6% and Rogers at 41.4%, with 6% undecided and a 3.8-point margin of error. Four minor-party candidates (Libertarian, Natural Law, U.S. Taxpayers and Green) each got 3% or less, and 11% of respondents had already voted absentee. Mitchell pointed to Republicans gaining in the final weeks of past Michigan Senate races.
In a Fox News poll, El-Sayed led Rogers 50% to 49% among likely voters and 51% to 48% among registered voters. Fox's Aug. 6–10 poll had Rogers ahead 51% to 47% among registered voters.
A Michigan State University IPPSR poll had El-Sayed ahead of Rogers, 48% to 44%. An earlier poll reported in July had El-Sayed trailing Rogers by double digits while Haley Stevens was tied with him.

El-Sayed won the Aug. 4 Democratic primary with about 48.5% to Rep. Haley Stevens' 47.5%, a margin of about 15,000 votes. Stevens conceded and endorsed him. Rogers had no opponent in the Republican primary, and Mallory McMorrow withdrew from the Democratic race in July. The seat is open because Democratic Sen. Gary Peters is retiring.

El-Sayed and Rogers held a very combative first debate in Grand Rapids on Oct. 8, covering gas prices, the war with Iran and tariffs. El-Sayed called Rogers a Trump loyalist, and Rogers called El-Sayed a 'con man'.

El-Sayed is being outspent nearly 2-to-1 on ads. Groups aligned with Republicans had spent nearly $3 million by mid-September on ads tying El-Sayed to the streamer Hasan Piker, according to AdImpact data. Rogers released an ad calling for an end to the tariff war with Canada.
A second debate, hosted by WXYZ-TV, is scheduled for Oct. 21. The general election is Nov. 3, 2026, and absentee voting in Michigan began Sept. 24.

In 2024, Democrat Elissa Slotkin beat Rogers by about 0.3 points (48.6% to 48.3%, roughly 19,000 votes) even though Trump carried Michigan. Late polls had mostly shown Slotkin ahead by a few points, for example 47% to 42% in an EPIC-MRA poll.
The last time a Republican won a U.S. Senate race in Michigan was 1994. Democrats have won every Michigan Senate race since then, including 2024.

Military contractors will qualify only if confirmed to be operating under the direct command or coordination of the respective state’s armed forces (e.g. the Battle of Khasham would not qualify).

recent_facts.fact: After round 1 at Club de Campo Villa de Madrid, Eugenio Chacarra, Connor Syme and Grant Forrest led at 5 under (66). Angel Ayora and Sergio García were tied 4th at 4 under, one shot back.

Ayora shot 67 (−4) in round 1, a card that included two eagles and three bogeys. He was the provisional leader during the morning. Afterward he said that if his driver holds up, he will be near the top.

Round 2 is being played today (2026-10-09). I couldn't find any live or completed round 2 scores: the ESPN, Golf Post and Golf Channel leaderboard pages either returned nothing or blocked access. Ayora's standing after round 2 is not verified.
Co-leader Eugenio Chacarra has a foot injury. He said he did not yet know whether he could play round 2 and left open the possibility of withdrawing.

Ayora tees off at 13:50 Spanish time on Friday 9 October from the 1st tee, playing with Ludvig Åberg and Tyrrell Hatton. In round 1, Åberg shot even par and Hatton +5. The tournament has four rounds, 8–11 October, so it finishes Sunday 11 October.

Before the event, Jon Rahm (world #15) was listed as the highest-ranked player in the field, which also included Justin Rose, Shane Lowry, Ludvig Åberg, Tyrrell Hatton, Patrick Reed and defending champion Marco Penge (#53).
Spanish opening-day reports say Jon Rahm did not play because of the birth of his fourth child. Defending champion Marco Penge and Patrick Reed both opened at +2.

Ayora (born 2004) turned pro in 2023. His only professional win is the 2024 Rosa Challenge Tour event. On the DP World Tour he has no wins; his best finishes include T7 at the 2025 Italian Open (he led outright after 36 holes) and T8 at the 2025 DP World Tour Championship. He had ten top-10s in 2025. A single Challenge Tour win is weak evidence of an ability to close out a win.

In the 2026 season (as of July), Ayora had five DP World Tour top-10s, including T5 at the Qatar Masters, T3 at the KLM Open in June and solo 5th at the Open d'Italia in late June. He missed the cut at the Scottish Open, the PGA Championship and The Open, and was 22nd in the Race to Dubai at the time of The Open.
An undated PGA Tour profile gives Ayora's Official World Golf Ranking as 121. This figure may be out of date.
Ayora finished 9th at the 2025 Open de España at the same venue (Club de Campo Villa de Madrid). He is in his second DP World Tour season and has turned down LIV Golf offers.
The question resolves Yes only if Ayora wins the tournament. If he withdraws or does not tee off, the Tournament Winner market resolves No.

recent_facts.fact: The ESL Pro League Season 24 playoffs have eight teams: PARIVISION, FURIA, Spirit, Vitality, 1win, Aurora, Falcons and MOUZ. The quarterfinals on Friday, Oct 9 are Vitality vs PARIVISION, 1win vs Aurora, Falcons vs Spirit and FURIA vs MOUZ. No quarterfinal results had been published when these searches ran on Oct 9, and HLTV's event page returned a 403 error, so it could not be checked.
Quarterfinal times on Oct 9, Moscow time: 1win–Aurora 11:30, Vitality–PARIVISION 14:00 (13:00 CET), FURIA–MOUZ 16:30, Falcons–Spirit 19:00. All are single-elimination Bo3 matches.

Bracket halves: the Vitality–PARIVISION winner plays the 1win–Aurora winner in one semifinal, and the FURIA–MOUZ winner plays the Falcons–Spirit winner in the other. Falcons and Vitality are in opposite halves and could only meet in the final. Semifinals are Bo3 on Oct 10, and the grand final is Bo5 on Oct 11 at Spodek, Katowice.

The playoffs are single elimination. To win the title, a team must win the Bo3 quarterfinal, the Bo3 semifinal and the Bo5 grand final, which is three straight series. HLTV is the named resolution source.
Vitality beat Falcons 2-1 in the Swiss 2-0 pool (Anubis 9-13, Dust2 13-4, Mirage 13-8), which HLTV called Vitality's first win over Falcons in a year. Vitality were the second team into the playoffs.

Vitality went 3-0 in the Swiss stage, beating 1win 2-0, NAVI 2-1 and Falcons 2-1. Their quarterfinal opponent PARIVISION went 3-2, eliminating NAVI 2-1 and G2, and is ranked 20th by HLTV and 11th by VRS. The same source lists Vitality 2nd in both HLTV and VRS.

Falcons are the reigning IEM Cologne 2026 Major champions; they beat Spirit in that event's semifinal. Since then Spirit have won the Esports World Cup and BLAST Open Porto, where they beat Falcons in the semifinal. Their map head-to-head is 11-10 in Spirit's favour.

Spirit went 3-2 in the Swiss stage, losing to MOUZ and 1win. MOUZ, a possible Falcons semifinal opponent, beat FURIA and Spirit in the Swiss stage and won BLAST Bounty. FURIA went 3-2, losing to MOUZ and Aurora, and the article describes their roster as fatigued.

Vitality recently won StarSeries, their first title since May, beating Aurora in the Bo5 grand final after losing a Bo3 to Aurora earlier in that event. 1win, the other possible semifinal opponent for Vitality, beat Spirit and G2 in the Swiss stage.
An HLTV preview shows Falcons at #5, but it is not clear which ranking that is, so this is unverified.

market.question: 2026 Balance of Power: R Senate, D House
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States Senate and the party that wins control of the United States House of Representatives in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States Senate if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the party that wins control of the chamber is the party that wins half of the voting seats and holds the Vice Presidency. If the outcome remains ambiguous after applying the above criteria, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first selected President Pro Tempore of the Congress that convenes after the specified election is affiliated.

A party wins control of the United States House of Representatives if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first elected Speaker of the House of the Congress that convenes after the 2026 midterm election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chambers.

For determining Senate control, all regular and special Senate elections that determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress and are scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 are included. Vacant Senate seats for which no election or special election to fill the seat is scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 will be treated as held by the party affiliation of the most recent member to hold that seat. For determining House control, all House elections in the 2026 United States midterm election that elect voting members and determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress are included. Where a Senate or House seat is decided by a runoff, the runoff result will determine attribution of that seat, even if it takes place after November 2026.

For seats contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected. 

For seats not contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party that holds the seat as of the date of the election. If a current sitting member of the U.S. Senate who is not up for election changes party affiliation or vacates their seat after the date of the election, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was affiliated at the time of the election.

Senate and House members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the Senate or House elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.
