market.question: Will Flavio Bolsonaro win the most votes in the second round of the Brazil presidential election from Amazonas?
market.rules:
The second round of the presidential election is scheduled to take place in Amazonas, Brazil on October 25, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the listed candidate who receives the most valid votes in the second round of this election from Amazonas.

Candidates will be primarily ranked by order of valid votes won in Amazonas. If two or more candidates are tied for any position, ties will be broken by alphabetical order of the candidates’ listed full names as they appear in this market. This market will resolve to the candidate that occupies the highest finishing position after applying this ranking.

If the result of this election isn't known definitively by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).

recent_facts.source: Minha Colinha (TSE table, 100% of sections counted)
recent_facts.fact: In Amazonas's first round on Oct 4, 2026, Lula (PT) got 1,046,996 votes (48.23%) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) got 976,764 (45.00%). That is a lead of about 70,200 votes out of 2,170,763 valid votes.

Eliminated candidates in Amazonas together got about 147,000 votes (6.77%): Augusto Cury (Avante) 77,531 (3.57%), Renan Santos (Missão) 35,411 (1.63%), Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) 28,310 (1.30%) and Zema (Novo) 1,781 (0.08%). There were also 24,402 blank votes, 39,384 null votes and 564,062 abstentions.
In the first round, Lula lost the capital, Manaus, with 37% of valid votes to Flávio Bolsonaro's 54%. Lula's statewide lead came from the interior.
Nationally, Flávio Bolsonaro led the first round with 47.03% of valid votes to Lula's 45.16%. The runoff between the two is on Oct 25, 2026.
A national PoderData runoff poll (3,000 interviews, Oct 5–7, 2026, margin of error 1.8 points) showed Flávio Bolsonaro at 53% and Lula at 47%. No Amazonas-specific runoff poll turned up in searches.
Ronaldo Caiado formally backed Flávio Bolsonaro at an event in Goiânia on Oct 6. Zema said he will be against the PT. Renan Santos released his voters without endorsing anyone.
Sources disagree on Augusto Cury, who was third in Amazonas with 3.57%. Some report that he endorsed Flávio Bolsonaro, but not unconditionally. Others report that he endorsed neither candidate.

recent_facts.source: Jornal Opção / Estado de Minas (citing Quaest)
recent_facts.fact: Quaest's national data show Flávio Bolsonaro getting the votes of 60% of Renan Santos voters, 43% of Caiado voters and 34% of Cury voters.

In the 2022 runoff, Lula won Amazonas with about 51.04% to Jair Bolsonaro's 48.96%. This was down from a first-round lead of about 49.4–49.6% to 42.8–43.0% (Money Times / Portal Amazônia). Only one source gives the runoff split, so treat it as unverified.
In Amazonas's 2022 first round, Lula had 49.40%, Bolsonaro 42.95%, Simone Tebet 4.25% and Ciro Gomes 2.18%. Lula's first-round lead of about 6.5 points shrank to about 2 points in the runoff.
In the 2018 runoff, Jair Bolsonaro won Amazonas with 50.27% against the PT candidate (Haddad).
Reports say that since 1989 the national first-round winner has always gone on to become president. This is a national pattern, not one for Amazonas.
The second round is on Oct 25, 2026. Results are counted by the TSE, and in past elections the count was usually complete the same night.

market.question: Will **real GDP** increase by more than 4.0% in Q3 2026? (Above 4.0%)
market.rules:
If real GDP (as measured by the BEA’s seasonally adjusted and annualized Advance Estimate) increases by more than 4.0, then the market resolves to Yes.
The market will close at 8:29 AM on the day of the expected release of the data. The market will expire at the first 10:00 AM following the release of the data for Q3 2026, or 3 months following that expected date of data release. Please note the Expiration Value is the one-decimal value published by the BEA.

recent_facts.fact: BEA's release schedule has the GDP Advance Estimate for Q3 2026 on October 29, 2026 at 8:30 AM EDT. BEA's September 30 GDP release gives the same date as its next release.

The House passed a stopgap funding bill 370-48 on September 1, 2026, after the Senate passed it 90-6 in August. It funds the government through December 11, 2026, which avoids an October 1 shutdown that could have delayed BEA releases. These search results did not confirm the presidential signature.
BEA's third estimate put Q2 2026 real GDP growth at a 2.2% annual rate, revised up 0.7 percentage point from the second estimate (1.5%). Q1 2026 was revised to 2.5%.

Real consumer spending (PCE) rose 0.6% in August 2026 (+$92.8 billion) after rising 0.1% in July. This release included the annual update of the National Economic Accounts, with revisions going back to January 2021.
In August 2026 personal income rose 0.2% and nominal spending rose 0.9%. The saving rate fell to 4.1% from 4.6% in July, and the PCE price index rose 0.3% on the month and 3.4% from a year earlier.

The goods and services trade deficit widened to $105.6 billion in August 2026 from a revised $92.8 billion in July, because imports rose more than exports. The goods deficit was $136.6 billion, up $12.8 billion. A wider deficit subtracts from GDP.
This review says first-half 2026 GDP was held down because strong consumer and capital spending was offset by lower government spending and a sharp rise in the trade deficit.

The September 2026 personal income and outlays data will be released on October 29, 2026, the same day as the Q3 advance GDP estimate. Before then, the September trade, retail sales and inventory data still have to come out.
The question resolves on the one-decimal, seasonally adjusted annualized real GDP growth rate in BEA's advance estimate. A reading of exactly 4.0% would not count as more than 4.0%.

Unverified, recalled count: of the roughly 12 quarterly first estimates from 2023 to 2026, only about 2 were above 4.0%: Q3 2023 at 4.9% and the delayed initial Q3 2025 estimate at about 4.3%. The latest confirmed first-half 2026 figures are 2.5% and 2.2% after revision.

recent_facts.fact: Cleveland beat the White Sox 9-5 in ALDS Game 4 at Rate Field on Oct. 8, 2026. They trailed 2-0 through four innings and scored six runs in the sixth. That tied the best-of-five series 2-2. The Game 5 winner advances to the ALCS against the Tampa Bay Rays.

The winner-take-all ALDS Game 5 is on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, at Progressive Field in Cleveland. MLB.com lists it at 8 p.m. ET on TBS/truTV/UniMas/HBO Max, though MLB's postseason FAQ lists 5 p.m. ET. Friday Oct. 9 is a travel day.
Results so far: Game 1 (Oct. 3, Cleveland): White Sox won 3-0. Game 2 (Oct. 5, Cleveland): White Sox won 4-3. Game 3 (Oct. 7, Chicago): Guardians won 9-3. Game 4 (Oct. 8, Chicago): Guardians won 9-5.

Gavin Williams threw 18 pitches to get the final three outs of Game 4 and is still named as a potential Game 5 starter. In Game 4, starter Parker Messick lasted only 2 1/3 innings. Reliever Grant Taylor, who had a four-inning save in Game 1, got no outs and was charged with four runs.
Williams went 14-8 with a 3.76 ERA in the 2026 regular season. He led the AL with 248 strikeouts in 184 1/3 innings. Neither team had officially named a Game 5 starter in the reports found.

White Sox manager Will Venable would only commit to Sean Burke pitching in some form in Game 5. Burke threw 5 1/3 innings of one-run, one-hit relief with six strikeouts in Game 2. Against Cleveland in the regular season he was 2-0 with a 1.04 ERA in three appearances (two starts).

Cleveland clinched its third straight AL Central title on Sept. 26 at 85-76, two games ahead of the White Sox (83-78), with one game left. Cleveland was the AL's No. 2 seed with a first-round bye. Chicago was the No. 6 seed and came through the Wild Card Series.

After Game 2 the White Sox were 4-0 in the 2026 postseason, all on the road, and went 48-33 at home in the regular season. Chicago is the first team to reach the postseason after three straight 100-loss seasons.

recent_facts.fact: For the week beginning Sep 28, 2026, OpenRouter's Market Share chart showed OpenAI at 18.2% of text requests, up 20% week over week. That is 0.1 percentage points above the 18.1% threshold. This figure comes from a search-result summary; the chart itself could not be loaded directly.
In the same week (beginning Sep 28, 2026), DeepSeek led with 21.8% of requests (up 5%) and Google was second with 21.5% (up 23%). OpenAI, at 18.2%, was third.

According to the page, the Market Share chart by author counts requests, while the model leaderboard ranks models by tokens. Token-share figures from third parties are therefore not directly comparable to the resolution metric.

The rankings page says usage data runs through Oct 9, 2026, so the week of Oct 5 was still partial as of today. The Market Share section's numbers were cut off in the fetched text and could not be read.

For the week of Sep 21, 2026, DeepSeek had 24.4% share (request volume down 2% week over week). OpenAI's request share rose 6% and Google's rose 12%. No absolute OpenAI figure was given for that week.

A snapshot covering usage through Sep 1, 2026 put DeepSeek at 23.0%, Google at 20.7% and OpenAI at 19.6% in OpenRouter's provider market-share view. So OpenAI was above 18.1% in that earlier snapshot too (unverified secondary report).

Among the top 20 models by tokens for Sep 28 to Oct 4, 2026, OpenAI's four models (GPT-6 Luna, GPT-5.6 Luna, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-5.6 Sol) together had about 9.8% of top-20 tokens. GPT-6 Astra rose 36% week over week and GPT-5.6 Luna fell 49%. A stealth model, 'Space Bunny Alpha', had 28.5%, and stealth models had 10.5% of requests.

An Oct 8 report said OpenAI had retaken the weekly spend lead on OpenRouter for the first time in about 2.5 years, after Anthropic held 75–80% of combined OpenAI-plus-Anthropic spend through most of 2024–2025.

recent_facts.source: OpenRouter newsletter 'The Token State of Play'
recent_facts.fact: In the week of Sep 7, 2026, OpenAI models took just over 50% of combined OpenAI-plus-Anthropic spend. In the week of Sep 14, they took 78% of combined OpenAI-plus-Anthropic tokens.
OpenAI's share of coding and work-related usage on OpenRouter was under 25% at the start of 2026 and close to 50% in the latest month covered.

market.question: Will "Other Mommy" Opening Weekend Box Office be between 27m and 30m?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to how much "Other Mommy" Opening Weekend Box Office will gross domestically on its opening weekend. The "Daily Box Office Performance" figures found on the "Box Office" tab on this movie's The Numbers (https://www.the-numbers.com/) page will be used to resolve this market once the values for the 3-day opening weekend (October 9 - 11) are final (i.e., not studio estimates).

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

Please note, this market will resolve according to the The Numbers figures provided under Weekend Box Office Performance for the 3-day weekend (which typically includes Thursday's previews), regardless of whether domestic refers to only the USA, or to USA and Canada, etc.

If there is ambiguity as to whether the resolution source's figures are final, this market will remain open until both https://www.boxofficemojo.com/ and https://www.the-numbers.com/ have confirmed their finalized figures.

If there is no final data available by October 16, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, another credible resolution source will be chosen.

recent_facts.fact: Other Mommy made $3.6M in Thursday previews from about 2,850 screens.
BoxOfficeReport.com projected more than $28.5M for Other Mommy over the Oct. 9–11 weekend.
Before release, Deadline projected a No. 1 opening of about $20M at roughly 3,200 sites.
Boxoffice Pro's pre-release weekend range was $17M–$22M. It noted that industry tracking had run as high as $35M for the opening.

Critics' reviews were described as 'scathing' (Deadline). Variety said the film 'misfires in every direction.' One early report put its Rotten Tomatoes score at about 20%, although Gold Derby reported 59%.
The main new competitor, Sony's The Social Reckoning, is projected at about $6M for the weekend. Verity, last week's No. 1, was projected at about $14M in its second weekend.

Saturday Oct. 10 and Sunday Oct. 11 grosses are still to come. Studio estimates normally come out Sunday Oct. 11, and actuals usually reach The Numbers on Monday Oct. 12. The question closes on 2026-10-11 at 12:00Z.

The question resolves on the final 3-day (Oct. 9–11) figure on The Numbers, which includes Thursday previews. Studio estimates do not count. If the figure lands exactly on a bracket boundary, the higher bracket wins, so $27.0M exactly falls outside the $24M–$27M bracket.

Coverage of horror openings describes the genre's audiences as front-loaded. A $12.3M Friday (with previews) that becomes a $27.5M weekend is about 2.24 times the Friday. Horror films with poor audience grades often finish nearer 2.0–2.2 times Friday, but this range comes from memory and is unverified.

facts_dropped.fact: Deadline's Friday update had Other Mommy at $12.3M for Friday, including Thursday previews, on 3,365 screens. The headline says it is 'on track' for a $27.5M 3-day opening. That is a studio-reported projection, not a final figure.
facts_dropped.reason: makes a prediction

facts_dropped.fact: Audiences gave Other Mommy a D+ CinemaScore. The same article repeats the $27.5M weekend projection on 3,365 screens and an $18M budget.
facts_dropped.reason: makes a prediction

facts_dropped.fact: Pre-release tracking cited here was $17M–$22M, and Gold Derby predicted $21M for the Oct. 9–11 weekend. For comparison, Jessica Chastain's horror film Mama opened to $28.4M in 2013.

recent_facts.fact: The match is Elche vs Celta in LaLiga 2026/27 matchday 8, played Sunday 11 October 2026 at 14:00 Madrid time (12:00 UTC) at Elche's home ground, the Martínez Valero. Celta are the away side, and only a Celta win inside 90 minutes plus stoppage time resolves Yes, so a draw resolves No.
After 7 games, Celta are 15th with 7 points (1 win, 4 draws, 2 losses; goals 8 for, 6 against). Elche are 18th with 5 points (1 win, 2 draws, 4 losses; goals 11 for, 17 against).
Celta's last game was a 5-0 home win over Racing de Santander at Balaídos, their first league win of the season. The scorers were Hugo González, Ilaix Moriba, Miguel Román and Pablo Durán (2).

Elche's last game was a 3-1 win at Espanyol, playing with ten men from the 6th minute (Fer Niño 2, Germán Valera). That win ended a four-match losing run, and Elche have not taken a single point at home this season.

Celta absences: Carl Starfelt (hamstring tear picked up with Sweden, about 6 weeks), Miguel Román and Jones El-Abdellaoui (recovering from knee operations) and Andrés Antañón (ankle sprain) are out. Iago Aspas is likely available but probably on the bench, Sebastián Cáceres is a real doubt with pubalgia, and goalkeeper Ionuț Radu is expected to play despite shoulder discomfort.
In his pre-match press conference, Celta coach Claudio Giráldez said Aspas and Cáceres are back, while Miguel Román, Starfelt and El-Abdellaoui are out.

Elche absences: Federico Redondo is suspended after his red card at Espanyol, Buba Sangaré is doubtful with a muscle problem, and Yago de Santiago is in the last phase of recovery from knee surgery. Roy Revivo is fit.

In last season's (2025-26) LaLiga meeting at the Martínez Valero, on matchday 7, Elche beat Celta 2-1 with an André Silva goal, a Borja Iglesias equaliser and a 68th-minute winner. The date is approximate, and one match is a very small head-to-head sample.

market.rules:
If Joe Dean wins the Open de España presented by Madrid, then the market resolves to Yes.
If a golfer forfeits, withdraws, or does not participate prior to teeing off, their contracts will resolve as follows:
Tournament Winner and End of Round Leader markets will resolve to No
Finishing Position, Make the Cut, Head-to-Head, and 3-Ball markets will resolve to Fair Market Value

recent_facts.fact: After 36 holes, Grant Forrest (SCO) led at -9 (66-67). Connor Syme (SCO) and Joel Girrbach (SUI) were tied 2nd at -8, one shot back. Eugenio Chacarra and Joe Dean were tied 4th at -7. Jacob Skov Olesen, Jeff Winther, Martin Couvra, Victor Perez and Daniel Hillier were tied 6th at -6.
Syme opened with rounds of 66 and 68 (-8). Girrbach went 68-66, and his Friday round included five straight birdies from the 4th to the 8th.

Forrest has finished tied 3rd at this event twice (2021, 2024) and has never missed the cut in six previous appearances. Chacarra is playing with a fractured toe. Patrick Reed, who has led the Race to Dubai since February, missed the cut. Sky's text lists Chacarra and Dean at -8, while the DP World Tour lists them at -7.
Syme shot a first-round 66 (-5) to share the early lead with Grant Forrest. Eugenio Lopez-Chacarra also shot 66 on day one.

The tournament runs 8–11 October 2026 at Club de Campo Villa de Madrid (par 71). Round 3 is on Saturday 10 October and the final round on Sunday 11 October. No round-3 scores could be found at research time.
The cut fell at +1. Justin Rose, Patrick Reed and Rafa Cabrera Bello missed it at +2 (per Golf Magic).

The field was headlined by Jon Rahm, Justin Rose and Shane Lowry, and defending champion Marco Penge also entered. Rahm's and Lowry's 36-hole positions were not in the reports found, and neither was among the top 10 named at -6 or better.
Syme's only DP World Tour title is the 2025 KLM Open, which he won by two shots over Joakim Lagergren in his 182nd start. That one win is weak evidence on how he converts from contention.

recent_facts.source: PGA Tour / DP World Tour profiles
recent_facts.fact: Syme's rankings are undated and the two profiles disagree. The PGA Tour profile lists his OWGR as 376 with 0 wins in 2026. The DP World Tour profile lists him 184th on its ranking with 80.97 Race to Dubai points.
In July 2026, Syme described being in a rough patch that included a spell out injured. He called it 'a bit of a storm'.

market.question: Will Ilija Srdanović be the next prime minister of Serbia?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to the next individual who officially assumes the office of Prime Minister of Serbia by June 30, 2028, 11:59 PM ET.

To count for resolution, the individual must be elected by the National Assembly and be formally sworn-in, resulting in the official formation of a new government. Any interim or caretaker Prime Minister who is not elected by the National Assembly will not count toward the resolution of this market.

If no such Prime Minister takes office by June 30, 2028, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

This market will resolve based on a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve solely based on official information from the Serbian government.

recent_facts.fact: Vučić dissolved the National Assembly and called snap parliamentary elections for 25 October 2026. The vote had been due by December 2027. He cited EXPO 2027 in Belgrade as one of his reasons. The question closes on the same day as the election.

Vučić resigned as president on 27 September, cutting his second term short by more than seven months. He is leading SNS in the election. AP reports that if his party wins a majority of seats, parliament is expected to elect him prime minister. He launched his campaign at a packed Belgrade arena on 3 October.

Vučić heads list no. 1, 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' (SNS-led, 209,130 signatures), as SNS's candidate for Prime Minister. All 250 seats are up and 126 are needed for a majority. Seats are allocated by d'Hondt in one nationwide constituency with a 3% threshold, and minority parties are exempt from the threshold.

Faktor Plus poll, 16–20 Sept, n=986: United Serbia 48.6% (+1.4), Student List 37.1% (+5.6), SPS 4.9%, European Serbia 3.6%, NADA 2.8%. Stated willingness to vote was 62%. Faktor Plus is described as pro-government-leaning. I found no October poll or independent poll.
The page says the SNS–Student List race has tightened. Some polls put SNS first and others put the Student List first. It gives no poll figures in its text.

The People's Serbia coalition withdrew its list on 22 September to back the Student List (list no. 3, ballot carrier Ilija Srdanović). Faktor Plus also said the People's Movement of Serbia, Ecological Uprising and New Face of Serbia had withdrawn, which consolidated the opposition vote.

Other lists: 'Factor of Stability!' led by Ivica Dačić (SPS, JS, SDPS, Zeleni), which is the ruling coalition's traditional partner; European Serbia (Tepić/Ponoš, SSP and SRCE); Authentic Right (NADA). Fifteen other lists, including minority lists, were also submitted.

In the 2024 cycle, parliament had one month to constitute itself after final results, then 90 days to form a government. The president nominates the PM-designate, who presents a programme and cabinet for an Assembly vote. If no government is elected in time, parliament is dissolved and new elections are called.

The question closes on 25 October 2026, election day. Any Assembly vote electing a new prime minister would come after the new parliament's constitutive session, about 30 days after final results, so it would fall after the close date. The resolution window runs to 30 June 2028.
In 2022, SNS took about 43% and roughly 120 seats. It stayed the largest party but lost its outright majority (126). It still formed a government with partners.

In 2020, the SNS-led 'For Our Children' coalition won 188 of 250 seats, a two-thirds majority, in a vote boycotted by most opposition parties. In 2016, SNS won 131 seats. SNS-led lists have finished first in every parliamentary election from 2014 to 2023. 2012 is not verified here.

This election follows about two years of student-led protests that began after the November 2024 Novi Sad railway station disaster, with more than 100,000 people protesting at the March 2025 peak. Vučić previously served as Serbia's prime minister from 2014 to 2017, before becoming president.

recent_facts.fact: At lunch on day 2 of the 1st Test at Kingsmead, Durban, Australia were 277/8 in their first innings after 96 overs, with Matt Renshaw 102* (218 balls) and Nathan Lyon 7*. South Africa had not yet batted. I could not find a day-2 stumps score.

In the second session of day 2, Australia were still batting on 277/8 after 96 overs. On day 2, Wiaan Mulder dismissed Pat Cummins (43) and bowled Mitchell Starc (6). The blog reported no weather interruptions on day 2 up to that point.

Bad light caused an early close on day 1, so only 65.2 of the scheduled overs were bowled. Australia, who chose to bat, finished day 1 on 187/6 after being 124/6. Jansen, Mulder and Nortje took two wickets each.
The 1st Test at Kingsmead, Durban is scheduled for five days, October 9–13, 2026, so days 3, 4 and 5 (Oct 11–13) are still to come.
In 2024, only 3 of 53 Tests ended in draws (5.66%), and 2 of those 3 were affected by weather. That is the lowest draw rate of any year with at least 20 Tests.
In the 2023–25 WTC cycle (2022 to 2024-25), 11 of 120 Tests ended in draws, compared with 26 draws in the 2013 to 2015-16 window. Only about one in three recent Tests reached a fifth day.
As of 2009, Durban was the venue where South Africa had drawn the most Tests since readmission, with 6 draws. This is old data and does not cover the last decade.

Rain often disrupts Kingsmead Tests. On day 1 of the November 2024 South Africa v Sri Lanka Test in Durban, persistent rain limited play to 20.4 overs. Climate sources disagree on Durban's October rainfall, putting it at roughly 96–129 mm a month.

recent_facts.fact: Cleveland beat the White Sox 9-5 in ALDS Game 4 at Rate Field on Oct 8, 2026, tying the best-of-five series 2-2. José Ramírez homered and drove in three runs. That sets up a winner-take-all Game 5 on Saturday, Oct 10.
ALDS Game 5 is Saturday, Oct 10 at 8 p.m. ET at Progressive Field in Cleveland, so Cleveland is the home team. The winner advances to the ALCS against the Tampa Bay Rays.

Series results so far: Game 1 (Oct 3, at CLE) White Sox 3-0; Game 2 (Oct 5, at CLE) White Sox 4-3; Game 3 (Oct 7, at CHW) Guardians 9-3; Game 4 (Oct 8, at CHW) Guardians 9-5. Each team won both games in the other's park, and Cleveland scored 18 runs across Games 3 and 4.

Neither team has officially named a Game 5 starter. Cleveland's likely pitcher is Gavin Williams, who led the AL with 248 regular-season strikeouts and struck out 11 in 5 innings in Game 2 (a 4-3 loss), but he also threw about 18-19 pitches in relief in Game 4. Parker Messick is the other option after pitching only 2 1/3 innings in Game 4.

Chicago is expected to use Sean Burke in some role, though manager Will Venable has not committed to one. Burke allowed 1 hit and 1 run in 5 1/3 innings of bulk relief in Game 2 and went 2-0 with a 1.04 ERA in three regular-season appearances (two starts) against Cleveland.

Bullpens: Cleveland used seven pitchers in Game 4, and manager Stephen Vogt said it would be 'all hands on deck' after the off-day. The White Sox bullpen is described as taxed after Grant Taylor struggled in Game 4, and Chicago will use whoever is available, including starters. Neither team reported injuries.
In Game 4, Cleveland scored 6 runs in the 6th inning, mostly against the White Sox bullpen, to win 9-5. Patrick Bailey hit a pinch-hit home run with 2 RBIs.
Series hitting leaders: José Ramírez is 4-for-9 with a double, triple, home run and 5 RBIs. Chicago's Miguel Vargas has reached base 12 times in the series.

Cleveland finished the regular season 85-77 and won its third straight AL Central title, clinching on Sept 26, as the AL's No. 2 seed with a first-round bye. Chicago finished 84-78, one game back, as the No. 6 seed. Cleveland went 24-10 over its last 34 games to pass Chicago.
In the 2026 regular season the White Sox won the 13-game series against Cleveland 7-6. Seven of the 13 games were decided by one run, and four ended in walk-offs.
The White Sox swept the Houston Astros (81-81) in the AL Wild Card Series, winning the clincher 7-3 on Sept 30. It was Chicago's first playoff series win since 2005.
There have been 40 winner-take-all Division Series Game 5s since 1995. Home teams won both 2025 Game 5s (Mariners over Tigers, Brewers over Cubs). The article gives no full home/road split.

An older MLB.com piece said road teams had won 11 of 15 decisive Division Series Game 5s from 2002 on. A 2019 MLB.com figure put home teams at 56-58 in all postseason winner-take-all games. Both counts are out of date and are not single-game evidence.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). market.question: Iran-Oman Hormuz Agreement by October 31?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if a diplomatic agreement between Oman and Iran over traffic in the strait of Hormuz is announced by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET.

A diplomatic agreement refers to an official agreement, treaty, deal, or substantially similar diplomatic instrument that establishes agreed actions, policies, obligations, or commitments between Oman and Iran.

A qualifying diplomatic agreement must establish Iranian or Omani policies, obligations, or commitments aimed at managing, permitting, restoring, or increasing vessel or shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, including agreements defining vessel traffic corridors, fee collection policies, or other management policies.

All listed countries must announce their acceptance of the same qualifying diplomatic agreement for the Payout Condition to be met. A joint announcement will qualify, as will separate announcements from each entity of its own acceptance of an agreement which, taken together, directly indicate that all the listed countries accepted the same agreement. Separate announcements of individual policies will not qualify if the policies are not announced as part of a diplomatic agreement.

Each announcement must be a declarative statement that clearly and unambiguously communicates acceptance of an agreement. Statements that reference ongoing negotiations or a prospective agreement, or that allude to or express support for an agreement without confirming acceptance of the agreement, do not qualify. A qualifying announcement need not reference the agreement by name or use specific terminology, provided it clearly communicates acceptance of an agreement.
 
Whether announcements from the listed countries represent a diplomatic agreement and whether such an agreement qualifies will be primarily determined through the announcements themselves. Where an announcement is made by all listed countries but, based on the announcements, it remains ambiguous whether the announcements represent a qualifying diplomatic agreement between the countries, this market will remain open until either i) definitive confirmation that the announcements represent a qualifying diplomatic agreement between the listed entities is achieved through further announcements from the listed countries or a consensus of credible reporting or ii) 14 calendar days (ET) have passed after the date that the last country made their first potentially qualifying announcement. If, at the end of the fourteenth calendar day, no definitive confirmation has been achieved, this market will resolve based on the totality of information available from the resolution sources at that time. No single statement, denial, or presentation of evidence will govern where it is contradicted by the totality of information.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of Oman and Iran and a consensus of credible reporting.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if Iran initiates a general closure of its airspace, that is not solely due to weather conditions, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A “general closure” refers to a cancellation or suspension of aviation which is generally applicable to all commercial flights transiting Iranian airspace (“Tehran FIR”). A qualifying closure must apply generally to all of Iran or the Tehran FIR; limited cancellations, delays, or partial closures will not qualify. A closure which applies generally to commercial aviation across Iranian airspace, with limited exceptions for certain categories of flights, however, will qualify (e.g. exceptions for certain flights pre-approved by the Iranian Civil Aviation Authority may be permitted).

Qualifying previous examples include the February 28, 2026 total closure of Iranian airspace (https://www.iranintl.com/en/202602289115) and the January 2026 total closure of Iranian airspace except to international flights with express governmental permission (https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iran-shuts-airspace-most-flights-flightradar24-says-2026-01-14/). Non-qualifying examples include the January 27, 2026 partial closure of Iranian airspace around the Strait of Hormuz (https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/iran-issues-airspace-notice-for-military-drills-near-strait-of-hormuz/3812508), the April 2024 closure of Iran’s western airspace (https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iranian-airports-cancel-flights-until-monday-morning-2024-04-14/), and the January 25 - April 25, 2026 VFR (Visual Flight Rules) flights suspension which did not broadly close commercial aviation in Iran (https://www.intellinews.com/iran-suspends-general-aviation-and-vfr-flights-in-new-airspace-directive-421997/).

Warnings, No-Fly-Zones, or other flight restrictions imposed by airlines or countries other than Iran will not be sufficient for a “Yes” resolution.

Airspace closures which occur solely due to weather conditions, earthquakes, or volcanic eruptions, will not qualify.

The primary resolution sources for this market will be official information from Iranian aviation authorities and a consensus of credible reporting.

recent_facts.fact: At lunch on day 2 of the 1st Test at Kingsmead, Durban, Australia were 277/8 in their first innings after 96 overs, with Matt Renshaw 102* (218 balls) and Nathan Lyon 7*. South Africa had not yet batted. I could not find a day-2 stumps score.

In the second session of day 2, Australia were still batting on 277/8 after 96 overs. On day 2, Wiaan Mulder dismissed Pat Cummins (43) and bowled Mitchell Starc (6). The blog reported no weather interruptions on day 2 up to that point.

Bad light caused an early close on day 1, so only 65.2 of the scheduled overs were bowled. Australia, who chose to bat, finished day 1 on 187/6 after being 124/6. Jansen, Mulder and Nortje took two wickets each.
The 1st Test at Kingsmead, Durban is scheduled for five days, October 9–13, 2026, so days 3, 4 and 5 (Oct 11–13) are still to come.
In 2024, only 3 of 53 Tests ended in draws (5.66%), and 2 of those 3 were affected by weather. That is the lowest draw rate of any year with at least 20 Tests.
In the 2023–25 WTC cycle (2022 to 2024-25), 11 of 120 Tests ended in draws, compared with 26 draws in the 2013 to 2015-16 window. Only about one in three recent Tests reached a fifth day.
As of 2009, Durban was the venue where South Africa had drawn the most Tests since readmission, with 6 draws. This is old data and does not cover the last decade.
South Africa's all-time Test record is 191 wins, 162 losses and 126 draws from 479 Tests (about 26% drawn), covering all eras and venues.

Rain often disrupts Kingsmead Tests. On day 1 of the November 2024 South Africa v Sri Lanka Test in Durban, persistent rain limited play to 20.4 overs. Climate sources disagree on Durban's October rainfall, putting it at roughly 96–129 mm a month.

market.question: Will the Republican Party control the House after the 2026 Midterm elections?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States House of Representatives in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States House of Representatives if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first elected Speaker of the House of the Congress that convenes after the 2026 midterm election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chamber.

All House elections in the 2026 United States midterm election that elect voting members and determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress are included. Where a seat is decided by a runoff, the runoff result will determine attribution of that seat.

Seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected.

House members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the House elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: US announces end of Iranian blockade by October 15, 2026?
market.rules:
On July 13, 2026, Trump announced the United States would reinstate its naval blockade of Iran, targeting Iranian ships and customers.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States government, or an authorized representative of the United States government, publicly and officially announces the end, termination, lifting, or suspension of the United States’ naval blockade on Iranian ships and ships of Iranian customers, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An announcement qualifies if it communicates that the United States will generally cease blocking vessel traffic for Iranian ships and customers, including an announcement that the blockade will not take effect at all, even if some restrictions remain (for example, an imposition of fees). An announcement does not qualify if it reflects only a limited or partial change that stops short of a general end or suspension of the blockade, for example, an exemption for a specific vessel, cargo, or port.

A qualifying announcement must be a declarative statement of the United States government’s present termination or suspension of the blockade, previously-unannounced prior termination or suspension of the blockade, or definitive decision to terminate or suspend the blockade.

A qualifying announcement must clearly and unambiguously identify the end or suspension of the blockade. Statements that merely allude to, reference, or describe an end to the blockade, without clearly communicating it, do not qualify. The announcement need not use specific terminology or reference the end of a blockade by name; an announcement of a resumption of prior obligations, the maintenance of a status quo, or a return to a previously agreed baseline qualifies, provided the substantive policy of ending or suspending the blockade is clearly and unambiguously communicated.

A qualifying announcement must be made through official channels, by an individual acting in an official capacity. Statements made incidentally or informally in a context not intended for official communication do not qualify.

The following do not qualify:

Anonymous, unattributed, or leaked statements not confirmed as official;
Statements by persons not authorized to speak for the United States government;
Third-party speculation, analysis, or predictions that the United States government will announce or implement an end to the blockade;
Satirical, fabricated, hacked, or impersonated communications; and
Statements that describe a prospective, contingent, probable, or conditional end to the blockade rather than announcing a present and decided position.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes” regardless of whether it is later reversed, or whether the blockade actually ends in practice.

Resolution will be based on official information from the United States government, including the President, the Department of Defense, the Department of State, and United States Central Command (CENTCOM), or the official representatives of the United States government.

recent_facts.source: CNN / Times of Israel / India TV (reporting Trump Truth Social post)
recent_facts.fact: On October 8, 2026, Trump posted on Truth Social that the US will not attack Iran before the November 3 midterms. In the same post he said the naval blockade of Iranian ports 'will remain in full force and effect.' He said Steve Witkoff is 'doing very well' in negotiations with Iran.

Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi said on October 8 that Tehran is 'reviewing the views of the Americans' and will reply to the latest US proposal 'within the next few days.' Messages are passing through mediators. He pointed again to Iran's 'Seven-Day Plan,' under which Hormuz would reopen once US conditions, including lifting the blockade, are met.
CENTCOM said on October 5 that it had redirected its 130th commercial vessel since the blockade resumed on July 14. Over the past 12 weeks it has disabled 3 ships and destroyed 13.

The US blockade of Iranian ports is still in place, and Iranian leaders admit it is crippling the economy. Iran's oil exports remain blocked, and Oil Minister Paknejad resigned as oil available for export ran out. Trump said 'either Iran signs the deal, or it won't exist any longer,' and senior officials met at Camp David the previous Friday.

Before Trump's October 8 post, Axios reported that the Pentagon had been told to prepare possible fresh strikes on Iran, with no set date. Trump had not made a final decision on resuming major combat operations.

Trump called 'unacceptable' Iran's seven-day proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume nuclear talks if the US lifted the naval blockade and waived oil sanctions. Mediators kept working after the rejection.

Axios reported that Trump was willing to ease sanctions and unfreeze Iranian assets in return for concrete Iranian nuclear steps. A US official said there would be no deal 'unless the nuclear issues are addressed' and that the sides remained apart on sequencing. Trump had said he was willing to keep the blockade in place to pressure Tehran toward a nuclear agreement.

The USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier group is expected to arrive by the end of October, bringing US carrier groups in the region to three. The US midterm elections are on November 3. No formal talks or negotiating deadline was reported. Iran's reply to the US proposal is due 'within days' of October 8.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (2026 United States naval blockade of Iran)
recent_facts.fact: Precedent from the first blockade (April 13 to June 18, 2026): Trump and Iran announced a deal on June 14, and Trump said he authorized lifting the blockade. CENTCOM said the blockade stayed in effect until signing. The MOU was signed June 17, and CENTCOM announced the lifting on June 18. The first blockade lasted about 9 weeks, from failed talks to an announced end.

The June interim MOU, which set a 60-day negotiating window, collapsed after the IRGC resumed attacks on commercial ships. Trump declared the MOU 'over,' announced the blockade's reinstatement on July 13, and it took effect July 14. The current blockade has run about 12.5 weeks as of October 10.

In June the lifting was communicated through several official channels: Trump's statement that he ordered or authorized a stop to the blockade (June 14), then a formal CENTCOM announcement (June 18). The June 14 announcement made the end conditional on the deal being signed.

market.question: Will there be no change in Fed interest rates after the October 2026 meeting?
market.rules:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's October 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for October 27-28, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their October meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

market.question: 2026 Balance of Power: R Senate, R House
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States Senate and the party that wins control of the United States House of Representatives in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States Senate if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the party that wins control of the chamber is the party that wins half of the voting seats and holds the Vice Presidency. If the outcome remains ambiguous after applying the above criteria, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first selected President Pro Tempore of the Congress that convenes after the specified election is affiliated.

A party wins control of the United States House of Representatives if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first elected Speaker of the House of the Congress that convenes after the 2026 midterm election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chambers.

For determining Senate control, all regular and special Senate elections that determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress and are scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 are included. Vacant Senate seats for which no election or special election to fill the seat is scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 will be treated as held by the party affiliation of the most recent member to hold that seat. For determining House control, all House elections in the 2026 United States midterm election that elect voting members and determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress are included. Where a Senate or House seat is decided by a runoff, the runoff result will determine attribution of that seat, even if it takes place after November 2026.

For seats contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected. 

For seats not contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party that holds the seat as of the date of the election. If a current sitting member of the U.S. Senate who is not up for election changes party affiliation or vacates their seat after the date of the election, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was affiliated at the time of the election.

Senate and House members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the Senate or House elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Israel accuses Iran/proxies of plane stabbing incident by Oct 31?
market.rules:
On September 30, 2026, FlyDubai flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv diverted to Saudi Arabia following an incident in the cockpit in which the co-pilot allegedly stabbed the captain. (see: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/diverted-flydubai-flight-israel-was-not-hijacking-incident-israeli-prime-2026-09-30/).

This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Israeli national government, or an authorized representative of the Israeli national government, publicly announces that Iran or its affiliated groups deliberately caused this incident, by October 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A public announcement refers to an on-the-record statement issued by the Israeli national government or by its authorized representatives acting in an official capacity on behalf of the Israeli national government. A statement or press release issued by the Israeli national government or any of its agencies will qualify. A Prime Minister or Cabinet Minister’s public statements will always be considered to be issued on-the-record in a capacity representing the Israeli national government for purposes of this market. A statement from a lawmaker or other government official speaking in their own capacity or on behalf of a party not in government will not alone qualify.

For purposes of this market, an affiliated group of Iran is: any organization directly controlled by Iran, Hezbollah, Hamas, Palestinian Islamic Jihad, Houthis ("Ansar Allah"), Kata'ib Hezbollah, Asa'ib Ahl al-Haq, Badr Organization, and Harakat al-Nujaba. An unlisted group will only qualify if the Israeli claim itself, or accompanying statements or releases, specifies that the group is a proxy of or otherwise is controlled or directed by Iran. A general statement that it was conducted by an Iranian proxy will also qualify, even if no group is named.

The newest listed poll is from co/efficient, a Republican-aligned pollster, taken Sep 30–Oct 1 among 837 likely voters (MoE ±3.37). It shows Honeycutt (R) at 46% and Lacore (D) at 40%.

A Democratic-sponsored Public Policy Polling survey taken Sep 9–10 among 536 registered voters (MoE ±4.2) shows Honeycutt at 41% and Lacore at 40%. An earlier poll from GQR, a Democratic-aligned pollster, dated Jul 22 among 400 likely voters, shows Honeycutt at 50% and Lacore at 48%.

The Cook Political Report rates SC-01 as R+6 on its partisan lean index and calls it a solidly Republican House seat. The seat is open because incumbent Republican Nancy Mace ran for governor; she lost the June 9 GOP gubernatorial primary.

Honeycutt and Lacore met on Oct 7 in their first general-election debate, hosted by WCBD and WSAV. They clashed over Iran, experience and inflation. Honeycutt blamed debt and spending; Lacore blamed tariffs and the Iran war.

recent_facts.fact: All-items CPI-U rose 3.4% (not seasonally adjusted) over the 12 months to August 2026, the same as the 12 months to July. The seasonally adjusted monthly change was +0.4% in August, after +0.1% in July.

The NSA CPI-U index for August 2026 was 334.980 (1982-84=100). Energy rose 2.1% SA in August and 16.3% year over year. Gasoline rose 3.9% SA (2.5% NSA) in August and 27.4% year over year. Core CPI was up 2.4% year over year, down from 2.5% in July.

The September 2025 NSA CPI-U index was 324.800, a 3.0% year-over-year rise. Only one secondary source confirmed this figure. Desk arithmetic: for the reported rate to round to 3.6% or more, the September 2026 index must reach about 336.33, which is an NSA rise of about 0.40% from August's 334.980. An index of about 336.01 (+0.31% NSA) would round to 3.5%, which does not count as above 3.5%.
BLS will release September 2026 CPI on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET (12:30 UTC). The question closes at 12:29 UTC that day.

Headline CPI inflation was 3.4% in August 2026, mainly because of rising gasoline prices.

market.question: Will the Democratic Party control the Senate after the 2026 Midterm elections?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States Senate in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States Senate if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the party that wins control of the chamber is the party that wins half of the voting seats and holds the Vice Presidency. If the outcome remains ambiguous after applying the above criteria, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first selected President Pro Tempore of the Congress that convenes after the specified election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chamber.

All regular and special Senate elections that determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress and are scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 are included. Runoffs for qualifying elections will determine attribution of the relevant seat, even if they take place after November 2026. Vacant seats for which no election or special election to fill the seat is scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 will be treated as held by the party affiliation of the most recent member to hold that seat.

For seats contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected.

For seats not contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party that holds the seat as of the date of the election. If a current sitting member of the U.S. Senate who is not up for election changes party affiliation or vacates their seat after the date of the election, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was affiliated at the time of the election.

Senate members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the Senate elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Will Aleksandar Vučić be the next Prime Minister of Serbia?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to the next individual who officially assumes the office of Prime Minister of Serbia by June 30, 2028, 11:59 PM ET.

To count for resolution, the individual must be elected by the National Assembly and be formally sworn-in, resulting in the official formation of a new government. Any interim or caretaker Prime Minister who is not elected by the National Assembly will not count toward the resolution of this market.

If no such Prime Minister takes office by June 30, 2028, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

This market will resolve based on a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve solely based on official information from the Serbian government.

recent_facts.fact: Vučić dissolved the National Assembly and called snap parliamentary elections for 25 October 2026. The vote had been due by December 2027. He cited EXPO 2027 in Belgrade as one of his reasons. The question closes on the same day as the election.

Vučić resigned as president on 27 September, cutting his second term short by more than seven months. He is leading SNS in the election. AP reports that if his party wins a majority of seats, parliament is expected to elect him prime minister. He launched his campaign at a packed Belgrade arena on 3 October.

Vučić heads list no. 1, 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' (SNS-led, 209,130 signatures), as SNS's candidate for Prime Minister. All 250 seats are up and 126 are needed for a majority. Seats are allocated by d'Hondt in one nationwide constituency with a 3% threshold, and minority parties are exempt from the threshold.

Faktor Plus poll, 16–20 Sept, n=986: United Serbia 48.6% (+1.4), Student List 37.1% (+5.6), SPS 4.9%, European Serbia 3.6%, NADA 2.8%. Stated willingness to vote was 62%. Faktor Plus is described as pro-government-leaning. I found no October poll or independent poll.
The page says the SNS–Student List race has tightened. Some polls put SNS first and others put the Student List first. It gives no poll figures in its text.

The People's Serbia coalition withdrew its list on 22 September to back the Student List (list no. 3, ballot carrier Ilija Srdanović). Faktor Plus also said the People's Movement of Serbia, Ecological Uprising and New Face of Serbia had withdrawn, which consolidated the opposition vote.

Other lists: 'Factor of Stability!' led by Ivica Dačić (SPS, JS, SDPS, Zeleni), which is the ruling coalition's traditional partner; European Serbia (Tepić/Ponoš, SSP and SRCE); Authentic Right (NADA). Fifteen other lists, including minority lists, were also submitted.

In the 2024 cycle, parliament had one month to constitute itself after final results, then 90 days to form a government. The president nominates the PM-designate, who presents a programme and cabinet for an Assembly vote. If no government is elected in time, parliament is dissolved and new elections are called.

The question closes on 25 October 2026, election day. Any Assembly vote electing a new prime minister would come after the new parliament's constitutive session, about 30 days after final results, so it would fall after the close date. The resolution window runs to 30 June 2028.
In 2022, SNS took about 43% and roughly 120 seats. It stayed the largest party but lost its outright majority (126). It still formed a government with partners.

In 2020, the SNS-led 'For Our Children' coalition won 188 of 250 seats, a two-thirds majority, in a vote boycotted by most opposition parties. In 2016, SNS won 131 seats. SNS-led lists have finished first in every parliamentary election from 2014 to 2023. 2012 is not verified here.

This election follows about two years of student-led protests that began after the November 2024 Novi Sad railway station disaster, with more than 100,000 people protesting at the March 2025 peak. Vučić previously served as Serbia's prime minister from 2014 to 2017, before becoming president.

market.question: Will the Democrats win the South Carolina Senate race in 2026?
market.rules:

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (2026 United States Senate election in South Carolina)
recent_facts.fact: Lindsey Graham won the June 9 GOP primary but died on July 11, 2026. Gov. McMaster appointed his sister Darline Graham on July 13, with backing from Trump and Thune. She was sworn in July 14 and is now the Republican nominee. Democrat Annie Andrews won her primary with 61.5% over Brandon Brown.
The Aug 11 special GOP primary produced no majority winner. In the Aug 25 runoff, Darline Graham beat Rep. Ralph Norman with 52.5% of the vote.

Recent polls: InsiderAdvantage (Sept 28–29, 1,200 likely voters, ±2.83) Graham 46%, Andrews 45%; Trafalgar (Sept 23–25, 1,087 LV, ±2.9) Graham 43%, Andrews 42%, with about 8.5% undecided; InsiderAdvantage (Sept 8–9) Graham 45%, Andrews 43%.
A Rasmussen poll from about mid-September (exact date unverified) had Graham 48%, Andrews 43% among likely voters, with 9% not sure.

In 2020, final polls showed Lindsey Graham ahead of Jaime Harrison by 2–3 points (Data for Progress 49–46; Morning Consult 46–44), but Graham won by about 10. The polls understated the Republican margin by about 7–8 points.

The last Democrat elected to the US Senate from South Carolina was Ernest Hollings in 1998, and the last Democrat to carry the state for president was Carter in 1976. Republican presidential margins were Trump +18 (2024), about +12 (2020), +14 (2016), Romney +10 (2012) and McCain +9 (2008).

recent_facts.source: Daily Beast / Newsweek reporting on Cook Political Report
recent_facts.fact: Cook Political Report moved the race from Solid Republican to Likely Republican on Sept 23, 2026, according to these reports. Sabato's Crystal Ball also shifted its rating.
An SCETV debate in Columbia is set for Sunday, Oct 11, 2026, between Graham, Andrews and Libertarian Kasie Whitener. The general election is Nov 3, 2026.

October quarterly FEC reports covering spending through Sept 30 are due Oct 15. Through June 30, Andrews had spent over $1.6 million on media and ads. The Democratic super PAC Fresh Start SC started a $2.5 million ad campaign on Sept 16.
Trump aimed a slur at Andrews. Graham responded that his remarks were 'probably not something I would have said.'

The question resolves when AP, Fox News and NBC all call the race for the same candidate, otherwise by official certification. Darline Graham is the Republican nominee, and a Libertarian (Kasie Whitener) is also on the ballot.

market.question: Will Ken Sim win the 2026 Vancouver mayoral election?
market.rules:
The 2026 Vancouver mayoral election is currently scheduled to be held on October 17, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who becomes the next mayor of Vancouver as a result of this election.

Temporary, interim, or placeholder mayors appointed before the election will not be considered.

If the result of this election isn't known by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting; however, if there is any ambiguity in the results, this market will resolve according to official information from Vancouver.

recent_facts.source: CityHallWatch (analysis of Canada Pulse Insights/OMNI TV poll)
recent_facts.fact: The newest published poll, from Canada Pulse Insights for Rogers OMNI TV, came out October 9. Among decided voters (n=427) it had Pete Fry (Green) at 28%, Ken Sim (ABC) at 27%, Kareem Allam at 19%, Colleen Hardwick at 13% and Rebecca Bligh at 7%. CPI quotes a margin of error of ±4.4 points, but this was an online opt-in panel. The analysis calls the race a statistical tie between Fry and Sim.
In the CPI poll, 18% were undecided at first. That fell to 10% after respondents were asked which candidate they leaned toward. The poll had no non-English language option and no ethnic weighting.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (2026 Vancouver municipal election, poll table)
recent_facts.fact: Justason Market Intelligence polled August 31 to September 11, right after the left consolidated. Its decided-voter results were Fry 45%, Sim 30%, Hardwick 11%, Allam 10% and Bligh 5%. The research desk did not check this against Justason's own release.

Research Co. surveyed 401 likely voters (±4.9 points) before the left-wing withdrawals. Among decided voters it had Sim at 30%, Allam and Fry at 19% each, and Hardwick at 14%. Among all likely voters it was Sim 22%, Allam 14%, Fry 14% and Hardwick 10%, with 26% undecided.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (2026 Vancouver municipal election, poll table)
recent_facts.fact: Pallas Data polled July 20–24 for the Vancouver Conservatives, with a margin of error of ±5.5 points. It had Fry at 18.1%, Sim 13.8%, Allam 11.5%, Hardwick 10.5%, COPE's Allen 6% and OneCity's Azaroff 3.5%, with about 34% undecided. In Mainstreet polls from 2025, before candidates had declared, Sim placed between 11% and 15%.

OneCity's William Azaroff left the mayoral race on September 8, saying the need was to get Ken Sim out, and spoke in favour of Pete Fry. COPE's Stephanie Allen had withdrawn six days earlier. That leaves Fry as the only left-of-centre mayoral candidate.

The Tyee reports that Azaroff and Allen did not explicitly endorse Fry, citing uncertainty over Elections BC rules on endorsing another party's candidate. Daily Hive described Azaroff's statement as an endorsement. OneCity's council, school board and park board candidates stay on the ballot.

Eight candidates are on the mayoral ballot: Ken Sim (ABC), Pete Fry (Green), Kareem Allam (Vancouver Liberals, Sim's former chief of staff), Colleen Hardwick (TEAM), Rebecca Bligh (Vote Vancouver), Muhammad Ahmad (Bright Future), and independents Amauri Caliman and Scott Gilbert. Several right-of-centre candidates are splitting the non-left vote: Sim, Allam, Hardwick and Bligh.
Vancouver elects its mayor by first-past-the-post with no runoff, so a plurality wins. Research Co. noted that about one-third of the vote could be enough to win.

Sim, Allam, Bligh, Fry and Hardwick took part in a five-candidate mayoral debate around October 8. Sim had skipped the first debate in September. ABC's platform includes a ban on open-air hard drug use, a 0% property tax increase for 2027, and a rebuilt Vancouver Aquatic Centre.
Advance voting is on October 10 and October 13, and general voting day is Saturday, October 17, 2026.
In 2022, Sim unseated incumbent mayor Kennedy Stewart with 51% of the vote, and ABC won majorities on council, park board and school board. In his first run, in 2018, Sim lost narrowly to Stewart.

This record is recalled, not checked against a source. Since 2008, Vancouver's incumbent mayors who sought re-election went 2 for 3: Gregor Robertson won in 2011 and 2014, and Kennedy Stewart lost in 2022.

A Léger Metro Vancouver poll reportedly had Fry at 23% and Sim at 19% in Vancouver, with 36% undecided, and found 21% saying Sim should be re-elected against 49% saying he should be replaced. The research desk could not confirm the date or these figures.

market.question: 2026 Balance of Power: R Senate, D House
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States Senate and the party that wins control of the United States House of Representatives in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States Senate if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the party that wins control of the chamber is the party that wins half of the voting seats and holds the Vice Presidency. If the outcome remains ambiguous after applying the above criteria, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first selected President Pro Tempore of the Congress that convenes after the specified election is affiliated.

A party wins control of the United States House of Representatives if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first elected Speaker of the House of the Congress that convenes after the 2026 midterm election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chambers.

For determining Senate control, all regular and special Senate elections that determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress and are scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 are included. Vacant Senate seats for which no election or special election to fill the seat is scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 will be treated as held by the party affiliation of the most recent member to hold that seat. For determining House control, all House elections in the 2026 United States midterm election that elect voting members and determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress are included. Where a Senate or House seat is decided by a runoff, the runoff result will determine attribution of that seat, even if it takes place after November 2026.

For seats contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected. 

For seats not contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party that holds the seat as of the date of the election. If a current sitting member of the U.S. Senate who is not up for election changes party affiliation or vacates their seat after the date of the election, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was affiliated at the time of the election.

Senate and House members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the Senate or House elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: NATO x Russia military clash by October 31, 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a military encounter between the military forces of a NATO country and Russia between market creation and October 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "military encounter" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between NATO and Russian military forces. Non-violent actions, such as airspace violations, firing of warning shots (such as the June, 2021 Black Sea Confrontations between Russian forces and HMS Defender), or cyberattacks will not qualify.

Interception of missiles or other one-way attack or loitering munitions (e.g. Shahed drones) which are targeting a 3rd party other than the listed countries or their respective forces will not alone qualify. Shooting down UAVs which are not munitions (e.g. MQ-9, Orlan 10, Orion, Bayraktar TB2, etc.) will qualify.

Intentional physical collisions, including aerial interceptions and naval ramming without the direct use of weaponry, such as the 2023 Black Sea incident—where a Russian Su-27 damaged a U.S. MQ-9 Reaper drone's propeller, leading to its crash— will not qualify regardless of damage.

Military contractors will qualify only if confirmed to be operating under the direct command or coordination of the respective state’s armed forces (e.g. the Battle of Khasham would not qualify).

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Will the Republicans win the Michigan Senate race in 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the 2026 midterm Michigan U.S. Senate election, inclusive of any run-offs.

A candidate shall be considered to represent a party in the event that he or she is the nominee of the party in question. Candidates other than the Democratic or Republican nominee (e.g., Greens, Libertarian, independent) may be added at a later date.

Candidates who run as independents will not be encompassed by the “Democrat” or “Republican” options regardless of any affiliation they may have with the party.

The candidates may be named in the contract for the convenience of traders. In the event that any named candidate is replaced as the nominee of their respective party prior to election day, the name in the contract will be updated and the market will resolve based on the replacement nominee of the party.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race in this state for the same candidate, this market will resolve based on the official certification.

recent_facts.fact: RealClearPolling's average of polls from Sept. 15 to Oct. 6 has Democrat Abdul El-Sayed at 48.1% and Republican Mike Rogers at 44.9%, a lead of 3.2 points for El-Sayed. The page may have been cached.
FiftyPlusOne's Michigan Senate polling average as of Oct. 8 has El-Sayed at 48.0% and Rogers at 44.5%.
Quantus Insights polled 744 likely voters on Oct. 5–6 and found El-Sayed at 48% and Rogers at 47%. A YouGov poll fielded Sept. 28–Oct. 5 had El-Sayed at 49% and Rogers at 48%.

A Mitchell Research poll fielded Oct. 1 has El-Sayed at 45.6% and Rogers at 41.4%, with 6% undecided and a 3.8-point margin of error. Four minor-party candidates (Libertarian, Natural Law, U.S. Taxpayers and Green) each got 3% or less, and 11% of respondents had already voted absentee. Mitchell pointed to Republicans gaining in the final weeks of past Michigan Senate races.
In a Fox News poll, El-Sayed led Rogers 50% to 49% among likely voters and 51% to 48% among registered voters. Fox's Aug. 6–10 poll had Rogers ahead 51% to 47% among registered voters.
A Michigan State University IPPSR poll had El-Sayed ahead of Rogers, 48% to 44%. An earlier poll reported in July had El-Sayed trailing Rogers by double digits while Haley Stevens was tied with him.

El-Sayed won the Aug. 4 Democratic primary with about 48.5% to Rep. Haley Stevens' 47.5%, a margin of about 15,000 votes. Stevens conceded and endorsed him. Rogers had no opponent in the Republican primary, and Mallory McMorrow withdrew from the Democratic race in July. The seat is open because Democratic Sen. Gary Peters is retiring.

El-Sayed and Rogers held a very combative first debate in Grand Rapids on Oct. 8, covering gas prices, the war with Iran and tariffs. El-Sayed called Rogers a Trump loyalist, and Rogers called El-Sayed a 'con man'.

El-Sayed is being outspent nearly 2-to-1 on ads. Groups aligned with Republicans had spent nearly $3 million by mid-September on ads tying El-Sayed to the streamer Hasan Piker, according to AdImpact data. Rogers released an ad calling for an end to the tariff war with Canada.
A second debate, hosted by WXYZ-TV, is scheduled for Oct. 21. The general election is Nov. 3, 2026, and absentee voting in Michigan began Sept. 24.

In 2024, Democrat Elissa Slotkin beat Rogers by about 0.3 points (48.6% to 48.3%, roughly 19,000 votes) even though Trump carried Michigan. Late polls had mostly shown Slotkin ahead by a few points, for example 47% to 42% in an EPIC-MRA poll.
The last time a Republican won a U.S. Senate race in Michigan was 1994. Democrats have won every Michigan Senate race since then, including 2024.

market.question: Will the Republican Party control the Senate after the 2026 Midterm elections?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States Senate in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States Senate if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the party that wins control of the chamber is the party that wins half of the voting seats and holds the Vice Presidency. If the outcome remains ambiguous after applying the above criteria, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first selected President Pro Tempore of the Congress that convenes after the specified election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chamber.

All regular and special Senate elections that determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress and are scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 are included. Runoffs for qualifying elections will determine attribution of the relevant seat, even if they take place after November 2026. Vacant seats for which no election or special election to fill the seat is scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 will be treated as held by the party affiliation of the most recent member to hold that seat.

For seats contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected.

For seats not contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party that holds the seat as of the date of the election. If a current sitting member of the U.S. Senate who is not up for election changes party affiliation or vacates their seat after the date of the election, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was affiliated at the time of the election.

Senate members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the Senate elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.
