market.question: Will Lula win the most votes in the second round of the Brazil presidential election from Amazonas?
market.rules:
The second round of the presidential election is scheduled to take place in Amazonas, Brazil on October 25, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the listed candidate who receives the most valid votes in the second round of this election from Amazonas.

Candidates will be primarily ranked by order of valid votes won in Amazonas. If two or more candidates are tied for any position, ties will be broken by alphabetical order of the candidates’ listed full names as they appear in this market. This market will resolve to the candidate that occupies the highest finishing position after applying this ranking.

If the result of this election isn't known definitively by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).

market.question: Eritrea invades Ethiopia by October 31?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Eritrean military forces enter Ethiopia by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET in a military operation that establishes control over any portion of Ethiopian territory. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Any Eritrean military operation which remains on the ground inside the territory of Ethiopia for less than 48 hours will not qualify.

Mere presence of Eritrean military forces within Ethiopia will not alone qualify, even if for longer than 48 hours. A consensus of credible reporting must demonstrate that such presence is or was part of a military operation which established control over a portion of Ethiopia.

Only the entry of Eritrean military forces into the territory of Ethiopia must occur by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Where Eritrean military forces enter the territory of Ethiopia by the listed date, but on the listed date, at 11:59 PM ET, control has not yet been confirmed by a consensus of credible reporting, this market will remain open for 7 additional full calendar days (ET) to allow for confirmation. If, at the end of the seventh calendar day, no consensus of credible reporting indicates that the operation has established or did establish control over part of Ethiopia, this market will resolve to "No." No single statement, denial, or presentation of evidence will govern where it is contradicted by a consensus of credible reporting.

Hybrid or "grey zone" operations conducted by unmarked personnel will qualify if they are confirmed to be acting under the direct control of the Eritrean state and establish de facto control over territory.

For purposes of this market, Ethiopia will be considered to be territory claimed by Ethiopia and not controlled by another state at the time of market creation. Territory claimed by Ethiopia but held by Eritrea or another state will not be relevant for purposes of this market.  

Search and rescue or hostage rescue operations, operations intended solely to capture specific individuals, operations solely intended to evacuate personnel or to extract or destroy equipment or infrastructure, and intelligence, reconnaissance, or surveillance operations, whether overt or covert, will not qualify unless clearly demonstrated by a consensus of credible reporting to have satisfied this market’s criteria for a “Yes” resolution. Operations conducted with the consent or at the invitation of the government of Ethiopia and strikes by air, missile, drone, or naval forces unaccompanied by ground forces will not qualify.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Will Student List – Students Win win the most seats in the 2026 Serbian parliamentary election?
market.rules:
Parliamentary elections to elect the 250 members of the National Assembly of Serbia are scheduled to take place on October 25, 2026.

This market will resolve to the electoral list that wins the greatest number of seats in the National Assembly of Serbia as a result of this election.

Electoral lists will be primarily ranked by the number of seats won in the specified election. If two or more lists are tied on seats, ties will be broken by the total number of valid votes received, with higher vote totals ranking higher. If lists remain tied, ties will be broken by alphabetical order of the listed names. This market will resolve to the list that occupies the highest finishing position after applying this ranking.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the named electoral list, as it appears on the ballot and official proclamations, regardless of which parties make up the list or how its members later organize themselves in the National Assembly.

If the results of the specified election are not definitively known by March 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the results of the elections, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. In the case of ambiguity, this market will resolve solely based on the results as reported by the Republic Electoral Commission of Serbia (https://www.rik.parlament.gov.rs/).

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia, Opinion polling for the 2026 Serbian parliamentary election
recent_facts.fact: An earlier Faktor Plus poll (about 4 Sept 2026, n=1,200) had the SNS-led list at 47.2% and the Student List at 31.5%. About one in three voters was undecided. Opposition and independent media accuse Faktor Plus and Ipsos of pro-government bias.

recent_facts.source: bne IntelliNews (CRTA / Stanford Democracy Action Lab)
recent_facts.fact: A CRTA/Stanford DAL poll (June 2026 fieldwork) found 44.9% of decided voters backing the Student List versus 35.7% for SNS. It was reported as the first regular national poll since July 2010 to place a party other than SNS first.

Searches as of early October 2026 found no poll with October fieldwork. The latest published figures are still the late-September Faktor Plus and NSPM releases, and Vukadinović said a new NSPM poll could come out in early or mid-October.

All 250 seats are elected by closed-list PR in a single nationwide constituency using D'Hondt. The threshold is 3% of votes cast, and minority lists are exempt. On the ballot, list 1 is 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' (SNS, PUPS, SPS-excluded allies, SRS and others) and list 3 is 'Student List – Students Are Winning'. SPS runs separately as list 2 ('Ivica Dačić – Factor of Stability!').

DS, the Green–Left Front, PSG (which left European Serbia), POKS, SPO, Kreni-Promeni, SDS, LSV, Dveri and Enough is Enough are not running their own lists and are backing the Student List. The People's Serbia coalition (NPS, NLS, EU) withdrew its list on 22 Sept to back the Student List.

The opposition vote is still split among several separate lists: European Serbia (SSP, SRCE, Solidarity), Authentic Right/NADA (NDSS, Monarchists), and Alternative for Serbia. NADA said NDSS would join a Student List-led government if it crosses the threshold.

Vučić dissolved the Assembly on 9 Sept 2026 and resigned the presidency on 27 Sept to head the SNS list as its prime ministerial candidate. The Student List is led by Ilija Srdanović, a Novi Sad cardiologist.

The list 'Izbor naroda' withdrew after endorsing the Student List. Vreme reported that Nestorović's list, which Vukadinović said could have passed the threshold, also exited. RIK had to publish the final summary list by 9 October.

Election day is 25 Oct 2026, with polls open 07:00–20:00 and campaign silence starting two days before. Televised debates ran from 24 Sept to 9 Oct. The Student List has called on citizens to take to the streets after polls close.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia, Opinion polling for the 2023 Serbian parliamentary election
recent_facts.fact: In the December 2023 election, the SNS list got about 46.7–48.0% (129 seats) and the opposition SPN got about 23.6–24.3% (65 seats). The final NSPM poll (12 Dec, 39.8 vs 25.6) and OFID poll (38.7 vs 27.1) underestimated SNS by roughly 8–9 points. Ipsos (44.6 vs 23.6) was closest.

SNS-led lists have won the most seats in every Serbian parliamentary election since 2012: 2012, 2014, 2016, 2020, 2022 and 2023, which is 6 of 6 (count recalled, unverified per election). The 2023 vote was marred by monitor-reported irregularities.

Observers describe Serbian elections as run under unfair conditions, including media dominance by the ruling party. Separately, pro-government tabloids have run campaigns against Srdanović using AI-manipulated photos, according to fact-checkers.
An earlier CRTA telephone poll (13–27 Sept 2025, n=2,020) found 44% support for a student list versus 32% for Vučić's bloc. This is older trend context from before the 2026 lists were formed.

market.question: Will CPI rise more than 0.5% in September 2026? (Above 0.5%)
market.rules:
If the Consumer Price Index (CPI) increases by more than 0.5% (single-decimal) in September 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
The market will always close at 8:25 AM ET on the scheduled day of the data release (October 14, 2026). Please note: the Expiration Value is the single-decimal value published at the Source Agency. In the case of a delay in data caused by a federal government shutdown impacting the reliability of the Source Agency, the market’s latest Expiration Date will be extended to the sooner of the release of the Underlying or six months after the end of the government shutdown.

recent_facts.fact: Seasonally adjusted CPI-U rose 0.4% in August 2026, after 0.1% in July. Before seasonal adjustment it was up 3.4% over 12 months. Core CPI rose 0.3% on the month and 2.4% on the year.
Recent seasonally adjusted monthly headline CPI changes were: Mar 2026 +0.9%, Apr +0.6%, May +0.5%, Jun -0.4%, Jul +0.1%, Aug +0.4%. Two of the last six months were above 0.5%.

In August 2026 the gasoline index rose 3.9% (after -2.9% in July), making up over a third of the all-items increase. Energy rose 2.1%, shelter 0.3% and food 0.1%. Energy was up 16.3% and gasoline 27.4% over 12 months.

EIA data put the September 2026 average US gasoline price at $4.36 a gallon, up from $4.06 in August and $3.93 in July. That is roughly a 7.3–7.4% rise from August to September before seasonal adjustment ($4.355 vs $4.058 per EIA weekly survey averages).
EIA weekly US regular gasoline retail prices were $4.478 on 2026-09-21, $4.465 on 2026-09-28 and $4.354 on 2026-10-05.

The AAA national average rose from $4.14 (Sept 3) to $4.27 (Sept 10), $4.43 (Sept 17) and a peak of $4.48. AAA's September 2026 monthly average was $4.33, 50 cents above the previous September record of $3.83 (2023). By Oct 1 the average had fallen to $4.41.
AAA said crude oil ran near $100 a barrel earlier in September before dipping back into the $90s, and named volatility in the Strait of Hormuz as a key factor.

September seasonal factors assume pump prices normally ease that month. So a rise in unadjusted gasoline prices in September becomes a larger rise once seasonally adjusted, and the adjusted CPI is the figure the question uses.

The September 2026 CPI is scheduled for Wednesday, October 14, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. ET. The question closes at 8:25 a.m. ET that day and resolves on the published single-decimal seasonally adjusted monthly change, so 0.6% or higher means Yes.
BLS headline monthly CPI-U changes are seasonally adjusted and rounded to one decimal. A published 0.5% does not count as 'more than 0.5%'.
In September 2025 the gasoline index rose 4.1% and was the largest factor in the monthly increase, but headline seasonally adjusted CPI rose only 0.3%.

market.rules:
This is a polymarket on the winner of the 2026 F1 Singapore Grand Prix, scheduled for Oct 11, 2026.

If the 2026 F1 Singapore Grand Prix is canceled or rescheduled to a date after Oct 18, 2026, this market will resolve to “Other.”

This market will resolve in favor of the driver who is officially listed in first place in the Final Classification published by the FIA following the conclusion of the race. The Final Classification is typically released 30-60 minutes after the race ends and includes any applied time penalties and official adjustments.

Disqualifications or changes made after the publication of the Final Classification will not affect market resolution. The timing of the podium ceremony does not determine the result for this market — only the FIA's published classification will be used to resolve this market.

The resolution source will be the official Formula 1 website and a consensus of credible sports news reporting.

recent_facts.fact: Verstappen was fastest in Singapore sprint qualifying with 1:31.156. Russell was +0.120s, Leclerc +0.243, Piastri +0.298, Norris +0.431, Hamilton +0.546, championship leader Antonelli 7th at +0.693, and Verstappen's teammate Hadjar 9th at +1.791. This sets the grid for the sprint only. The Grand Prix grid comes from a separate qualifying session.

The FIA stewards are investigating Verstappen for passing Lewis Hamilton under yellow flags at Turn 7 in SQ1, after Perez crashed. A guilty finding could bring a sprint grid penalty. As of the latest reports found, no decision had been published.
Before SQ1, Red Bull changed Verstappen's ERS unit as a precaution over a suspected fault. He was still fastest in all three sprint qualifying segments.

In the only practice session (FP1), Verstappen was 6th, 0.732s behind Russell's 1:32.274, after radio problems and time stuck in the garage. Leclerc was 2nd and Norris 3rd. Reports said his medium-tyre pace was more than half a second faster than anyone else's on mediums.

In the previous round, Verstappen won the rain-delayed Bahrain GP, which was held at Sepang, Malaysia. He started from pole and finished 2.307s ahead of Antonelli, with Hamilton 3rd. It was his first win of 2026.
At the Azerbaijan GP, Verstappen finished 2nd, 0.196s behind winner George Russell, and Hadjar was 3rd. It was Russell's third win of 2026.

In 2026 Verstappen has 8 podiums and 1 win, and is 6th in the standings with 188 points, 132 behind Antonelli. In the 9 races since Austria he has 1 win, six 2nd- or 3rd-place finishes and 2 DNFs, an average finish of 2.14 excluding DNFs.

16 of the 23 rounds of 2026 are complete. Winners found include Antonelli (China, Canada, Belgium), Russell (Austria, Azerbaijan) and Verstappen (Bahrain at Sepang). Mercedes lead the constructors' standings with 538 points after Baku, ahead of Ferrari 378, McLaren 306 and Red Bull 263.
This is Singapore's first sprint weekend. The sprint and Grand Prix qualifying are still to come on Saturday, and the Grand Prix is on Sunday, October 11, 2026.

The Grand Prix pole-sitter has won all but 5 Singapore Grands Prix, roughly 11 of 16 through 2025. Russell won from pole in 2025. The count is inferred from the source's wording, so treat it as unverified.
Verstappen has never won the Singapore GP. Motorsport.com said this sprint qualifying result is his first fastest qualifying time of any kind at Marina Bay.

market.rules:

This market will resolve to the next individual who is officially appointed and sworn in as Prime Minister of Israel following the 2026 parliamentary election. If no such Prime Minister is sworn in by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the Government of Israel; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

recent_facts.fact: Election day is 27 October 2026, official results are due to be confirmed on 4 November 2026, and 61 of 120 seats is a majority. The question closes 2026-10-28, which is before results are certified and before any new government could be sworn in.

recent_facts.source: Recalled historical record (unverified; not from a source fetched this session)
recent_facts.fact: In recent Israeli elections the government was sworn in weeks or months after the vote: 2022 election on Nov 1, Netanyahu sworn in Dec 29 (about 58 days); 2021 election on Mar 23, Bennett–Lapid sworn in Jun 13; 2020 election on Mar 2, government sworn in May 17. The April and September 2019 elections produced no government and led to new elections. None of the 5 elections from 2019 to 2022 produced a sworn-in PM within days.

Poll taken Oct 7–8 (n=700, ±3.7): Yashar (Eisenkot) 21, Likud 20, B'yachad (Bennett) 13, Democrats 9, Yisrael Beytenu 9, Otzma Yehudit 8, Joint Arab List 7, UTJ 7, Shas 7, RZP 6, Ra'am 5, Amcha Yisrael 4, Reservists/Economic 4. Coalition and opposition tied at 52 seats each, with Arab parties at 12.

recent_facts.source: Maariv analysis, as summarized in search results (via Jerusalem Post election coverage)
recent_facts.fact: Across polls, Likud is at about 20–22 seats (it won 32 in 2022) and Netanyahu's coalition at 50–54, short of 61. The opposition also falls short of 61 without the Arab parties, which are projected at 12–14 seats combined. Pollsters' figures vary widely.

The polling average puts Likud at about 22.3 seats, Yashar at 21.8, and Netanyahu's outgoing coalition at 51.6. Yashar places first in most tracked polls (Channel 13, Channel 12, Kan, Maariv), while Channel 14 polls have shown the Netanyahu coalition at 63 seats.

recent_facts.source: Channel 12 polls via Israel National News / JPost search snippets
recent_facts.fact: Recent Channel 12 polls varied: one had Yashar 24 and Likud 22; others had the blocs tied at 52–52, or the opposition at 58–59 vs the coalition at 51–52. Gantz's Blue and White polled below the 3.25% threshold (2.5% and 1.1%). Exact dates of these polls were not confirmed.
An earlier Maariv poll, taken before candidate lists were final, had an Eisenkot-led bloc reaching 61 seats without Arab parties if the Hendel–Zelekha slate joined, with Netanyahu's coalition at 47.

Avigdor Liberman (Yisrael Beytenu, about 9 seats in polls) pledged his party will not join any Netanyahu-led government: 'Hell will freeze over before we sit with him.' No similar direct pledge from Eisenkot or Bennett turned up in these searches.

In late September, Eisenkot, Bennett, Lapid, Golan and Liberman agreed not to attack each other until a government is formed. Who would lead remains unsettled: Eisenkot says the largest party should form the government, and he has ruled out Ra'am joining a government he leads.

Ben-Gvir is campaigning for right-wing voters and has claimed Netanyahu plans to form a government without him. Netanyahu privately reassured him that any government he forms would rest on the current coalition. Likud MK Tally Gotliv left for a senior spot in Otzma Yehudit.

The Supreme Court overturned the Central Elections Committee's Sept 23–24 disqualification of Ra'am, the Joint List and Ofer Cassif, so both Arab lists are running, separately. On Sept 8, Haaretz reported allegations that Netanyahu had advance warning of the Oct 7 attacks, which he denied.

Lists and alliances: Bennett heads 'Together' (Bennett 2026 merged with Lapid's Yesh Atid); Likud plans to merge with New Hope; RZP runs jointly with Feiglin's Zehut; Hili Tropper joined Yashar. Surplus-vote pairs: Together–Yisrael Beiteinu, Yashar–Democrats, Joint List–Ra'am, Likud–RZP. 38 lists were submitted.

Remaining dates: surplus-vote agreement deadline Oct 16, diplomatic-mission voting Oct 20, election Oct 27, official results Nov 4. Government formation (President's consultations, the mandate, a Knesset confidence vote) would follow after that.

market.rules:
The second round of the presidential election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 25, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two candidates in the second round of the next Brazil Presidential Election.

For the purpose of this market, the “margin of victory” is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first- and second-place candidates. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the election.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

If a candidate other than Flávio Bolsonaro or Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva receives the most valid votes in the second round, or if the top two candidates receive exactly the same number of valid votes, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the vote count has been made official.

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

If the result of this election isn't known definitively by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).

The second round of the presidential election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 25, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two candidates in the second round of the next Brazil Presidential Election.

For the purpose of this market, the “margin of victory” is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first- and second-place candidates. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the election.

​A candidate's party will be determined by their ballot-listed or otherwise identifiable affiliation with that party at the time all of the 2026 House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources. recent_facts.fact: A Siena poll of 496 likely NY-21 voters, taken Sept 30 to Oct 6, 2026 with a ±4.6 margin of error, had Democrat Blake Gendebien at 46%, Republican Anthony Constantino at 42%, independent Christopher Schmidt at 5% and 8% undecided. Constantino's favorability was 39-52 and Gendebien's was 46-29.

In the same poll, Republicans outnumbered Democrats 49% to 28% among likely voters. Constantino led Republicans only 65-21, while Gendebien led independents 51-30. In the district, Republican Bruce Blakeman led Hochul 55-40 for governor, and voters preferred Republican control of Congress 50-45.
Cook Political Report moved its rating for NY-21 from 'Solid Republican' to 'Likely Republican'.

Other NY-21 polls in 2026: a Public Policy Polling survey completed Sept 10 had Constantino 48%, Gendebien 43%. A mid-August J.L. Partners poll of 500 likely voters had Constantino 50%, Gendebien 40%. A WNYT/SurveyUSA poll of 800 adults, taken Aug 4-8, had Gendebien 43%, Constantino 39%. A June Gendebien internal poll had Constantino 45%, Gendebien 44%. Constantino's campaign called the Siena poll a 'scam poll'.
Reporting that the NY-21 race is tight, WWNY said Constantino was scheduled to appear with President Trump in Syracuse.

In the June 23, 2026 primaries, NBC projected Sticker Mule CEO Anthony Constantino as the Republican winner, ahead of Assemblyman Robert Smullen, and dairy farmer Blake Gendebien as the Democratic winner, ahead of Stuart Armoriell. The seat is open because Elise Stefanik is not seeking reelection.
Trump carried NY-21 by 16 points in 2024. In May 2026, Cook rated the seat safe Republican, and the DCCC had added it to its 'Districts in Play' list.

Unverified recall: Republican Elise Stefanik held this North Country seat in every election from 2014 through 2024, winning 6 of 6. Her 2024 margin was roughly 24 points. Democrat Bill Owens held the predecessor NY-23 from 2009 to 2015.
The general election is November 3, 2026. Ballotpedia also lists Christopher Schmidt (Independent) and Michael Metzgier (American Independent Party) on the general election ballot.

market.question: Will the rate of core CPI inflation be above 2.4% for the year ending in September 2026? (Above 2.4%)
market.rules:
If the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for All Urban Consumers: All Items less Food and Energy increases by more than 2.4% in the twelve months ending September 2026 (as represented by the one-decimal place value reported by the Bureau of Labor Statistics), then the market resolves to Yes.
In the case of a delay in data caused by a federal government shutdown impacting the reliability of the Source Agency, the market’s latest Expiration Date will be extended to the sooner of the release of the Underlying or six months after the end of the government shutdown.

recent_facts.fact: BLS's unadjusted core CPI index (all items less food and energy) was 338.041 in August 2026 and 329.970 in August 2025. BLS reported the 12-month change as 2.4%. Computed from these index levels, the unrounded change is about 2.445%, just under the 2.45% that would round to 2.5%.
Core CPI rose 0.3% in August 2026 (seasonally adjusted), and its 12-month rate was 2.4%, down from 2.5% in July. It was the lowest core rate since March 2021. Headline CPI was 3.4% year over year.

Seasonally adjusted monthly core CPI changes in 2026: Feb 0.2%, Mar 0.2%, Apr 0.4%, May 0.2%, Jun 0.0%, Jul 0.2%, Aug 0.3%. Shelter rose 0.3% in August after two months of 0.1%, and shelter's 12-month rate was 3.0%, down from 3.2% in July.

recent_facts.source: Ball State CBER (BLS data); BLS September 2025 CPI release
recent_facts.fact: The base month dropping out of the comparison is September 2025, when the unadjusted core index was 330.54 (two decimals; the three-decimal value 330.542 is unverified). Core rose 0.2% m/m seasonally adjusted that month and 3.0% year over year. Computed: the unadjusted index rose about 0.17% from August to September 2025.

For the published one-decimal 12-month rate to be 2.5% or higher, the unadjusted September 2026 core index needs to reach about 338.64 (330.54 × 1.0245). That is a rise of about 0.18% or more from August's 338.041. If the rise matches September 2025's roughly 0.17%, the rate stays near 2.44–2.45%.
BLS is scheduled to release the September 2026 CPI on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET. The question closes at 12:25 UTC that day.
August 2026 core CPI came in 0.1 percentage point above the consensus on a monthly basis (0.3% vs 0.2%). The annual rate of 2.4% matched the consensus. Gasoline was up 27.4% year over year.
In September 2025, core CPI rose 0.2% m/m seasonally adjusted, after 0.3% in both July and August 2025. Shelter rose 0.2% m/m, and owners' equivalent rent rose 0.13% (Goldman Sachs breakdown).

recent_facts.fact: In Gallup International's poll (fieldwork Sep 26–Oct 6, 987 interviews), Yotova–Valchev led with 44.9% and Gyurov–Kandev were second with 24.8%. The first round is on October 25, 2026, and a runoff between the top two would be held on November 1 if no candidate wins 50% or more. The campaign ends at midnight on October 23 and October 24 is a day of silence. 27 candidate tickets are registered, and Gyurov is No. 4 on the ballot.

A first-round win requires an absolute majority with turnout above 50%. Otherwise the top two go to a runoff. No Bulgarian presidential candidate has ever won in the first round. 'None of the above' has been on the ballot since 2016.

Incumbent President Iliana Iotova (Yotova), who was vice president from 2017 to 2026 and is now president, is running for a full term. She is backed by Radev's Progressive Bulgaria, BSP–United Left, Stand Up.BG and VMRO-BND. Gyurov, an independent and former caretaker PM, is backed by PP–DB. DPS has nominated no candidate.

GERB is fielding no presidential candidate. Borisov said he will not give 'unsolicited' support to Gyurov, but also that he cannot campaign for Yotova because she is his ideological opponent. Gyurov refused to ask GERB's leadership for support and said he expects backing from GERB voters.
Analyst Boyko Stankushev said at least two-thirds of GERB's electorate would vote for Gyurov in a runoff against Yotova. This is a commentator's estimate, not poll data.
Trend's Dimitar Ganev said runoff turnout could fall below 2 million voters. In Trend's poll, 20% of respondents were still unsure whether they will vote.

Gyurov and running mate Georgi Kandev announced their candidacy on September 1, 2026, nominated by an initiative committee. PP and DSB backed the ticket. Gyurov was caretaker prime minister from February 19 to May 8, 2026, appointed by Yotova.

Unverified, recalled from past results: since 1992, the first-round leader went on to win the runoff in most Bulgarian presidential elections, including 2006, 2011, 2016 and 2021. In 2001, incumbent Stoyanov lost the runoff to Parvanov. Incumbents running again won in 2006 and 2021 and lost in 2001.

Verstappen has never won the Singapore GP. Motorsport.com said this sprint qualifying result is his first fastest qualifying time of any kind at Marina Bay.

recent_facts.fact: At lunch on day 2 of the 1st Test at Kingsmead, Durban, Australia were 277/8 in their first innings after 96 overs, with Matt Renshaw 102* (218 balls) and Nathan Lyon 7*. South Africa had not yet batted. I could not find a day-2 stumps score.

In the second session of day 2, Australia were still batting on 277/8 after 96 overs. On day 2, Wiaan Mulder dismissed Pat Cummins (43) and bowled Mitchell Starc (6). The blog reported no weather interruptions on day 2 up to that point.

Bad light caused an early close on day 1, so only 65.2 of the scheduled overs were bowled. Australia, who chose to bat, finished day 1 on 187/6 after being 124/6. Jansen, Mulder and Nortje took two wickets each.
The 1st Test at Kingsmead, Durban is scheduled for five days, October 9–13, 2026, so days 3, 4 and 5 (Oct 11–13) are still to come.
In 2024, only 3 of 53 Tests ended in draws (5.66%), and 2 of those 3 were affected by weather. That is the lowest draw rate of any year with at least 20 Tests.
In the 2023–25 WTC cycle (2022 to 2024-25), 11 of 120 Tests ended in draws, compared with 26 draws in the 2013 to 2015-16 window. Only about one in three recent Tests reached a fifth day.
As of 2009, Durban was the venue where South Africa had drawn the most Tests since readmission, with 6 draws. This is old data and does not cover the last decade.
South Africa's all-time Test record is 191 wins, 162 losses and 126 draws from 479 Tests (about 26% drawn), covering all eras and venues.

Rain often disrupts Kingsmead Tests. On day 1 of the November 2024 South Africa v Sri Lanka Test in Durban, persistent rain limited play to 20.4 overs. Climate sources disagree on Durban's October rainfall, putting it at roughly 96–129 mm a month.

The average fell $0.0049 from Oct 9 to Oct 10. Over the past week it fell $0.0138 ($4.3807 to $4.3669), about $0.002 per day. To finish at or below $4.3600 on Oct 12, it would need to fall more than $0.0069 in two days.

AAA's Oct 8 weekly release said the national average 'dropped 5 cents this past week to $4.36' and gave a figure of $4.3612, compared with $4.4137 a week earlier. On Oct 1, AAA reported the national average down nearly 7 cents week over week to about $4.41. September 2026 averaged $4.33, a record for the month and 50 cents above the previous September record of $3.83 set in 2023.

In early trading on Oct 9, Brent fell 1.3% to $102.91 and WTI fell 1.2% to $90.40 after Trump said the US would not attack Iran before the November 3 midterms. In the previous session Brent had settled about 4% higher.

EIA's weekly US regular retail gasoline price for Oct 5, 2026 was $4.354 per gallon, as reported in a search summary. EIA uses a different method from AAA.

market.question: Will Flavio Bolsonaro win the most votes in the second round of the Brazil presidential election from Amazonas?
market.rules:
The second round of the presidential election is scheduled to take place in Amazonas, Brazil on October 25, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the listed candidate who receives the most valid votes in the second round of this election from Amazonas.

Candidates will be primarily ranked by order of valid votes won in Amazonas. If two or more candidates are tied for any position, ties will be broken by alphabetical order of the candidates’ listed full names as they appear in this market. This market will resolve to the candidate that occupies the highest finishing position after applying this ranking.

If the result of this election isn't known definitively by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).

recent_facts.source: Minha Colinha (TSE table, 100% of sections counted)
recent_facts.fact: In Amazonas's first round on Oct 4, 2026, Lula (PT) got 1,046,996 votes (48.23%) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) got 976,764 (45.00%). That is a lead of about 70,200 votes out of 2,170,763 valid votes.

Eliminated candidates in Amazonas together got about 147,000 votes (6.77%): Augusto Cury (Avante) 77,531 (3.57%), Renan Santos (Missão) 35,411 (1.63%), Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) 28,310 (1.30%) and Zema (Novo) 1,781 (0.08%). There were also 24,402 blank votes, 39,384 null votes and 564,062 abstentions.
Nationally, Flávio Bolsonaro led the first round with 47.03% of valid votes to Lula's 45.16%. The runoff between the two is on Oct 25, 2026.
A national PoderData runoff poll (3,000 interviews, Oct 5–7, 2026, margin of error 1.8 points) showed Flávio Bolsonaro at 53% and Lula at 47%. No Amazonas-specific runoff poll turned up in searches.
Ronaldo Caiado formally backed Flávio Bolsonaro at an event in Goiânia on Oct 6. Zema said he will be against the PT. Renan Santos released his voters without endorsing anyone.
Sources disagree on Augusto Cury, who was third in Amazonas with 3.57%. Some report that he endorsed Flávio Bolsonaro, but not unconditionally. Others report that he endorsed neither candidate.

In the 2022 runoff, Lula won Amazonas with about 51.04% to Jair Bolsonaro's 48.96%. This was down from a first-round lead of about 49.4–49.6% to 42.8–43.0% (Money Times / Portal Amazônia). Only one source gives the runoff split, so treat it as unverified.
In Amazonas's 2022 first round, Lula had 49.40%, Bolsonaro 42.95%, Simone Tebet 4.25% and Ciro Gomes 2.18%. Lula's first-round lead of about 6.5 points shrank to about 2 points in the runoff.
In the 2018 runoff, Jair Bolsonaro won Amazonas with 50.27% against the PT candidate (Haddad).
Reports say that since 1989 the national first-round winner has always gone on to become president. This is a national pattern, not one for Amazonas.
The second round is on Oct 25, 2026. Results are counted by the TSE, and in past elections the count was usually complete the same night.

facts_dropped.fact: In the first round, Lula lost the capital, Manaus, with 37% of valid votes to Flávio Bolsonaro's 54%. Lula's statewide lead came from the interior.

The "Daily Box Office Performance" figures found on the "Box Office" tab on this movie's The Numbers (https://www.the-numbers.com/) page will be used to resolve this market once the values for the 3-day opening weekend (October 9 - 11) are final (i.e., not studio estimates).

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

Please note, this market will resolve according to the The Numbers figures provided under Weekend Box Office Performance for the 3-day weekend (which typically includes Thursday's previews), regardless of whether domestic refers to only the USA, or to USA and Canada, etc.

If there is ambiguity as to whether the resolution source's figures are final, this market will remain open until both https://www.boxofficemojo.com/ and https://www.the-numbers.com/ have confirmed their finalized figures.

If there is no final data available by October 16, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, another credible resolution source will be chosen.

recent_facts.fact: Other Mommy made $3.6M in Thursday previews from about 2,850 screens.
BoxOfficeReport.com projected more than $28.5M for Other Mommy over the Oct. 9–11 weekend.
Before release, Deadline projected a No. 1 opening of about $20M at roughly 3,200 sites.
Boxoffice Pro's pre-release weekend range was $17M–$22M. It noted that industry tracking had run as high as $35M for the opening.
The main new competitor, Sony's The Social Reckoning, is projected at about $6M for the weekend. Verity, last week's No. 1, was projected at about $14M in its second weekend.

Saturday Oct. 10 and Sunday Oct. 11 grosses are still to come. Studio estimates normally come out Sunday Oct. 11, and actuals usually reach The Numbers on Monday Oct. 12. The question closes on 2026-10-11 at 12:00Z.

The question resolves on the final 3-day (Oct. 9–11) figure on The Numbers, which includes Thursday previews. Studio estimates do not count. If the figure lands exactly on a bracket boundary, the higher bracket wins, so $27.0M exactly falls outside the $24M–$27M bracket.

Coverage of horror openings describes the genre's audiences as front-loaded. A $12.3M Friday (with previews) that becomes a $27.5M weekend is about 2.24 times the Friday. Horror films with poor audience grades often finish nearer 2.0–2.2 times Friday, but this range comes from memory and is unverified.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if Eritrean military forces enter Ethiopia by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET in a military operation that establishes control over any portion of Ethiopian territory. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Any Eritrean military operation which remains on the ground inside the territory of Ethiopia for less than 48 hours will not qualify.

Mere presence of Eritrean military forces within Ethiopia will not alone qualify, even if for longer than 48 hours. A consensus of credible reporting must demonstrate that such presence is or was part of a military operation which established control over a portion of Ethiopia.

Hybrid or "grey zone" operations conducted by unmarked personnel will qualify if they are confirmed to be acting under the direct control of the Eritrean state and establish de facto control over territory.

For purposes of this market, Ethiopia will be considered to be territory claimed by Ethiopia and not controlled by another state at the time of market creation. Territory claimed by Ethiopia but held by Eritrea or another state will not be relevant for purposes of this market.  

Search and rescue or hostage rescue operations, operations intended solely to capture specific individuals, operations solely intended to evacuate personnel or to extract or destroy equipment or infrastructure, and intelligence, reconnaissance, or surveillance operations, whether overt or covert, will not qualify unless clearly demonstrated by a consensus of credible reporting to have satisfied this market’s criteria for a “Yes” resolution. Disqualifications or changes made after the publication of the Final Classification will not affect market resolution. The timing of the podium ceremony does not determine the result for this market — only the FIA's published classification will be used to resolve this market.

recent_facts.fact: A partial results page for 2026 Singapore GP qualifying (main race grid), published 10 Oct 2026, showed the order before Q3 was complete: Hamilton (Ferrari) 1st on 1:31.529, Verstappen 2nd on 1:31.639, Norris 3rd on 1:31.895, Leclerc 4th on 1:31.953, then Antonelli, Russell and Piastri. The live blog stops with Q3 under way. Hamilton led at the last timed update, with Verstappen 0.110s behind. Leclerc was briefly 2nd during the session and 4th at 15:05. Verstappen took sprint pole on 1:31.156, 0.120s ahead of Russell. Leclerc was 3rd (+0.243s) after holding provisional pole following his first SQ3 lap, and Hamilton was 6th. Formula1.com said Ferrari had looked like the team to beat going into SQ3.
After the sprint, Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes) leads the drivers' championship by 89 points over George Russell.

Standings after the Azerbaijan GP: Antonelli 302 pts, Russell 236, Hamilton 199, Norris 186, Leclerc 179 (5th), Verstappen 163. Russell won in Baku, and Leclerc finished 4th after starting on the front row.
Leclerc's only 2026 win so far is the British Grand Prix at Silverstone. That gives him 9 career GP wins. Sources disagree on his podium total (53 vs 54) and report about 27 career poles.
Verstappen came to Singapore after taking his first victory of the 2026 season at a recent race.

Leclerc took pole in Singapore in 2019 and 2022 but has never won the Singapore GP. Vettel won it for Ferrari in 2019. Marina Bay is a street circuit where track position from qualifying weighs heavily.
The Singapore GP runs 9–11 Oct 2026 at Marina Bay. The Grand Prix is on Sunday 11 Oct. The weekend uses the sprint format, and rain affected Saturday's sprint.

market.question: Will "Other Mommy" Opening Weekend Box Office be between 27m and 30m?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to how much "Other Mommy" Opening Weekend Box Office will gross domestically on its opening weekend. The "Daily Box Office Performance" figures found on the "Box Office" tab on this movie's The Numbers (https://www.the-numbers.com/) page will be used to resolve this market once the values for the 3-day opening weekend (October 9 - 11) are final (i.e., not studio estimates).

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

Please note, this market will resolve according to the The Numbers figures provided under Weekend Box Office Performance for the 3-day weekend (which typically includes Thursday's previews), regardless of whether domestic refers to only the USA, or to USA and Canada, etc.

If there is ambiguity as to whether the resolution source's figures are final, this market will remain open until both https://www.boxofficemojo.com/ and https://www.the-numbers.com/ have confirmed their finalized figures.

If there is no final data available by October 16, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, another credible resolution source will be chosen.

recent_facts.fact: Deadline's Friday update put Universal's Other Mommy on track for a $27.5M 3-day domestic opening at No. 1, playing on 3,365 screens. The Social Reckoning was No. 5 with about $6M.

Other Mommy made $3.6M in Thursday previews and another $8M+ on Friday, for a first day (previews included) of more than $12M, reported as about $12.3M. A $27.5M weekend would mean about $15.2M from Saturday and Sunday combined. Saturday and Sunday figures had not been reported yet.
Other Mommy earned $3.6M from Thursday previews on 2,850 domestic screens. Variety reported its budget as about $18M.
Other Mommy reported $3.5M+ in Thursday previews despite a Rotten Tomatoes critics score of about 17% (other outlets cite 18%). The studio reportedly held no press screenings.
Koimoi reported that Other Mommy's previews beat Scream 5's preview number.
Some outlets that reported the $3.6M previews gave a 3-day weekend range of $25M–$30M.
Before release, Deadline projected a No. 1 debut of about $20M at roughly 3,200 locations. Boxoffice Pro's preview range was $17M–$22M, though it noted some tracking had reached as high as $35M.

The market resolves on The Numbers' final (not estimated) 3-day figures for Oct 9–11, with Thursday previews included in that 3-day total. A value exactly on a bracket boundary, such as $27.0M, counts toward the higher bracket ($27M–$30M). Sunday studio estimates typically come out Sunday morning and final actuals on Monday.

facts_dropped.fact: Saturday Oct 10 grosses and the Sunday estimate are still to come, and the questions close Oct 11 at 12:00 UTC, likely before the official Sunday studio estimates are published. Front-loaded horror openings with poor reviews often decline on Saturday from a Friday that includes previews, and the trade projections shift as Saturday numbers arrive.

market.question: Will average **gas prices** be above $4.3600? (Above 4.3600)
market.rules: If average regular gas prices for United States are strictly greater than $4.3600 on Oct 12, 2026 according to AAA, then the market resolves to Yes.

recent_facts.fact: AAA's national average for regular gas was $4.3669 on 10/10/26. That is $0.0069 above the $4.3600 threshold. AAA's ticker showed $4.3718 yesterday (Oct 9), $4.3807 a week ago and $4.2770 a month ago.

The average fell $0.0049 from Oct 9 to Oct 10. Over the past week it fell $0.0138 ($4.3807 to $4.3669), about $0.002 per day. To finish at or below $4.3600 on Oct 12, it would need to fall more than $0.0069 in two days.

AAA's Oct 8 weekly release said the national average 'dropped 5 cents this past week to $4.36' and gave a figure of $4.3612, compared with $4.4137 a week earlier. The release called these the highest pump prices ever recorded for autumn. That $4.3612 is below the Oct 9 ticker reading of $4.3718, so the daily figures may have moved up and down within the week.

The Oct 8 release cited EIA data showing gasoline demand rising from 8.68 to 8.76 million b/d and gasoline production falling from 9.46 to 9.34 million b/d. Total gasoline stocks rose from 204.4 to 204.7 million barrels. WTI settled at $88.28 that Wednesday, down $1.16.

On Oct 1, AAA reported the national average down nearly 7 cents week over week to about $4.41. September 2026 averaged $4.33, a record for the month and 50 cents above the previous September record of $3.83 set in 2023.

In early trading on Oct 9, Brent fell 1.3% to $102.91 and WTI fell 1.2% to $90.40 after Trump said the US would not attack Iran before the November 3 midterms. In the previous session Brent had settled about 4% higher.

market.question: Will Lula win the most votes in the second round of the Brazil presidential election from Pará?
market.rules:
The second round of the presidential election is scheduled to take place in Pará, Brazil on October 25, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the listed candidate who receives the most valid votes in the second round of this election from Pará.

Candidates will be primarily ranked by order of valid votes won in Pará. If two or more candidates are tied for any position, ties will be broken by alphabetical order of the candidates’ listed full names as they appear in this market. This market will resolve to the candidate that occupies the highest finishing position after applying this ranking.

If the result of this election isn't known definitively by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).

recent_facts.source: O Tempo (TSE data, 100% of sections counted)
recent_facts.fact: First-round presidential result in Pará, with all 20,827 sections counted: Lula (PT) 2,427,237 votes (49.91% of valid votes), Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) 2,163,957 (44.50%). Lula's margin was 263,280 votes, about 5.4 points.

Other first-round votes in Pará: Augusto Cury (Avante) 125,172 (2.57%), Renan Santos (Missão) 84,165 (1.73%), Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) 51,991 (1.07%), Zema (Novo) 3,064 (0.06%). Minor left candidates (UP, PSTU, PCB, PCO) together had about 5,850. All non-runoff candidates combined had about 276,000 votes, more than Lula's 263,280-vote lead.

Compared with the 2022 first round in Pará, Lula fell from 52.22% (2,443,730 votes) to 49.91%. The Bolsonaro candidate rose from 40.27% (1,884,673; Jair) to 44.50% (Flávio), a gain of about 279,000 votes.

In the 2022 runoff Lula won Pará with 54.75% to Bolsonaro's 45.25%, after leading the first round there 52.22% to 40.27%. His share rose about 2.5 points between rounds. Unverified (from memory): Haddad also won Pará in the 2018 runoff, and PT won Pará in the 2014 runoff.
Nationally, Flávio Bolsonaro led the first round with 47.03% of valid votes (56,104,503) to Lula's 45.16% (53,879,538). Lula outperformed his national share in Pará by about 4.8 points.

National runoff poll, fieldwork Oct 5–7, 3,000 interviews, margin of error 1.8 points: Flávio 53%, Lula 47% of valid votes, with Lula down 3 points in a week. Regional figures were published only for Flavio: Centro-Oeste 54%, Sudeste 51%, Sul 58%. No Norte breakdown was reported.

Datafolha national runoff poll, Oct 6–7, 2,520 interviews: Flávio 52%, Lula 48% of valid votes. Total votes: 49% to 45%, with 5% blank/null and 1% undecided. Datafolha's final pre-first-round poll (Oct 3) had Lula ahead 45% to 42% in valid votes, but Flávio won the first round 47.03% to 45.16%.

Other national runoff polls: AtlasIntel/Bloomberg Flávio 52.8%, Lula 47.2% of valid votes; Veritá Flávio 51.56%, Lula 48.44%; Vox Lula 44.2%, Flávio 42.7% of total votes. No Pará-specific runoff poll was found.

Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) declared full support for Flávio Bolsonaro in the runoff, and the União Brasil-PP federation also backed Flávio. Reports differ on Romeu Zema (Novo): Diário do Nordeste says he endorsed Flávio, while Tribuna do Planalto says he avoided a formal endorsement. Together Caiado and Zema had about 55,000 votes in Pará.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

recent_facts.fact: Deadline's Saturday update on Friday grosses put Other Mommy at $12.3M for Friday, Thursday previews included, and on track for a $27.5M 3-day opening on 3,365 screens. These are studio and industry estimates, not final figures.
TheWrap, at 8:08 AM on Oct 10, reported a $13M opening day from 3,365 screens and a $28M opening weekend estimate.
This site reported about $3.6M in Thursday previews plus about $8M+ on Friday, for a total over $12M, and a '$27+ million opening weekend'.

Audiences gave Other Mommy a D+ CinemaScore. That is the lowest grade CinemaScore has given any film since Megalopolis got a D+ in September 2024. The film's Rotten Tomatoes scores are 20% from critics and 47% from audiences.
Thursday previews for Other Mommy brought in $3.6M from 2,850 screens, which beat expectations. JoBlo's headline gave a slightly different figure of $3.9M.
Universal released Other Mommy, which is based on a Josh Malerman novel, directed by Rob Savage and made on a reported $19M budget.

Before release, Boxoffice Pro said industry tracking ran as high as $35M for the opening weekend. Its preview compared the film to January's Send Help, a female-led original horror film that opened to $19.1M and finished at $64.7M domestic.

Horror films usually do most of their business early because young audiences turn out on opening weekend. This article covers whole-run multiples (total gross divided by opening weekend), not Friday-to-weekend ratios. Its unverified context is that 11 September horror releases with $18M+ openings averaged about a 2.3x run multiple.
Horror films tend to get low CinemaScores. 12 of the 13 recent films that had received an F at the time were horror. CinemaScore polls only opening-night audiences. Hereditary got a D+.

Saturday (Oct 10) and Sunday (Oct 11) grosses are still to come. Studios release Sunday weekend estimates on Oct 11, and final actuals typically follow on Monday, Oct 12. The question closes Oct 11 at 12:00 UTC, before any Sunday estimates come out.

market.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (HIGH) $100 in October?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

recent_facts.fact: WTI front-month futures daily highs in October 2026: Oct 1 93.68, Oct 2 93.51, Oct 5 91.88, Oct 6 90.05, Oct 7 90.98, Oct 8 93.20, Oct 9 92.16. The highest October high so far is 93.68, below $95. This is NYMEX-style data, not the Pyth CLL feed.
WTI closed at 91.20 on Oct 9, 2026 after a 92.16–90.08 range that day. It closed at 91.49 on Oct 8, up from 88.28 on Oct 7.
Late-September daily highs were Sep 28 96.54, Sep 24 96.78, Sep 21 97.22, Sep 18 98.01 and Sep 16 105.63. Prices fell from a 102.43 close on Sep 16 to around 89–92 by early October.
WTI (CFD) was about $91.3/bbl on Oct 9, 2026, down about 10.9% over the past month and up about 55% year over year. Investing.com lists a 52-week range of 54.98–117.63.

WTI settled at $91.49 on Oct 8, up 3.6%, and Brent closed at $104.28. Iran stepped up attacks on tankers in Hormuz, and Kpler data show Hormuz flows about 30% below prewar levels. Prices came off session highs after Trump said the US would not attack Iran before the Nov 3 midterms.

Oil rose as much as 5.6% intraday on Oct 8. Upside drivers listed: record tanker freight costs, attacks on vessels in Hormuz (nine targeted in the prior week), a US naval blockade of Iranian ports, reports of US plans for three days of strikes, and Hurricane Isaias shutting in about 1.3 million bpd (over 60%) of Gulf of Mexico crude output.

Downside drivers on Oct 9: Trump described 'productive discussions' with Iran, and Iran is reportedly reviewing a US response to a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days. China is also set to resume refined fuel exports in October.

WTI traded near $90.65 early on Oct 9, roughly flat. Axios reported the Pentagon is preparing for possible renewed strikes on Iran with no date set, and Saudi exports are recovering after the East-West pipeline restarted.
A record 10 tankers were struck in the week to Oct 4, and Houthi missile activity was also reported.

The Cushing WTI spot price was 99.77 on Oct 1, 97.89 on Oct 2, 96.13 on Oct 5 and 96.24 on Oct 6, 2026. This spot series is not the futures contract used for resolution and runs several dollars above front-month futures.

Still due before the Oct 31 close: Iran's reply on the Hormuz reopening proposal, Hurricane Isaias impacts on Gulf output, and the US midterms on Nov 3, after the window closes. Trump has said there will be no strikes on Iran before then. About 16 trading sessions remain in October after Oct 9.
On Sep 23, oil snapped a five-day losing streak after Iran vowed it would not surrender. This came during the drop from above $100 in mid-September.

recent_facts.fact: Falcons play Spirit today, October 9, 2026, at 18:00 CEST in a best-of-three, single-elimination quarterfinal at Spodek Arena in Katowice. No final result was available. BLAST.tv showed the series at 0–0, with a 'LIVE' tag that conflicted with its own 'yet to start' label.

The playoffs run October 9–11 in Katowice with 8 teams. The quarterfinals are 1win vs Aurora, PARIVISION vs Vitality, FURIA vs MOUZ and Falcons vs Spirit. To win the title, Falcons need wins in a Bo3 quarterfinal, a Bo3 semifinal (against the FURIA–MOUZ winner) and a Bo5 grand final on October 11.

BLAST.tv lists Falcons at VRS #6 and Spirit at VRS #1. The rosters are Falcons: karrigan, kyousuke, m0NESY, NiKo, TeSeS; Spirit: donk, magixx, sh1ro, tN1R, zont1x. HLTV's match page lists Spirit as #1 and Falcons as #5 in the HLTV ranking.
Falcons secured a playoff spot by beating NAVI 2-1, finishing on Mirage 13-8, and ended the Swiss stage 3-1. They also swept Aurora 2-0.
Vitality beat Falcons 2-1 in the Swiss stage on October 5. With three straight wins, Vitality were one of the first two teams to qualify for the playoffs. This was Falcons' only Swiss-stage loss.

Spirit went 3-2 in the Swiss stage. They beat ShindeN and PARIVISION 2-1, lost 0-2 to both MOUZ and 1win (ending a 13-match win streak), then qualified from the 2-2 pool. Before EPL, Spirit had won the Esports World Cup 2026 and BLAST Open Porto.

HLTV's all-time head-to-head is Falcons 10 wins, Spirit 11. Another source lists 5–7 over the last 12 meetings. The most recent meeting, on September 5, 2026 (a BLAST Open Porto semifinal), was a 2-0 Spirit win. Falcons beat Spirit in the IEM Cologne 2026 Major semifinal on the way to that title.
Previews note that Falcons had not built on their IEM Cologne 2026 Major win before EPL S24, while MOUZ won BLAST Bounty, the first event of the season.
The question resolves by the HLTV event winner of ESL Pro League Season 24, scheduled October 3–11, 2026. The grand final is a best-of-five on October 11 (HLTV match ID 2398757).

market.question: Perim Island no longer under Houthi control by October 15?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Perim Island is no longer under Houthi control by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

“The Houthis” refers to the Houthi movement (Ansar Allah), including its governing institutions and any armed force operating under its direction or on its behalf. “Perim Island” refers to Perim (Mayyun) Island in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, Yemen.

“No longer under the control of the Houthis” means that the Houthis no longer exercise primary military control over Perim Island, and another state, occupying force, the internationally recognized government of Yemen, or an internationally backed authority has established control over the island.

Temporary raids, isolated landings, special operations, bombardment, sabotage, naval presence offshore, or temporary disruption of Houthi activity will not qualify on their own.

An announcement, threat, or claim that the Houthis have lost control will not qualify without actual control being established.

If control changes pursuant to a negotiated settlement, ceasefire term, surrender, or transfer agreement, this will qualify only once actual control has been established on the island.

If control over Perim Island is contested, unclear, disputed, or not sufficiently established by the resolution date, this will not qualify, and the market will resolve to “No”.

The primary resolution source will be official statements from the relevant governments and militaries, along with a consensus of credible reporting.

recent_facts.fact: Variety reported that The Social Reckoning opened to $2.15 million on Friday from 2,606 North American theaters, which put it in fourth place for the day.

TheWrap reported Friday at $2.1 million from 2,606 locations and an opening weekend of about $6 million. That is less than a third of the original The Social Network's $22.4M opening in 2010. The film's net production cost is $30M, co-financed by Alcon.

ScreenRant said Sony projected a $6 million 3-day opening as of Saturday morning. It reported a B- CinemaScore (the original Social Network got a B+). ComicBookMovie reported a B+ CinemaScore instead, so the grade is disputed.
Sony's film made $650K in Thursday previews, starting at 4 p.m., from 2,368 locations. It opened Friday in 2,606 North American theaters.
ComicBookMovie reported the film at No. 5 for the weekend, behind Heart of the Beast, with a 55% Rotten Tomatoes score and a $30M budget.

Friday is about $2.1-2.3M including the $650K in previews, so the $6M weekend estimate assumes about $3.7-3.9M from Saturday and Sunday combined. The Numbers' final 3-day figure usually comes out on Monday, Oct 12. Finals can come in above or below Sunday's studio estimate.
For comparison, Tom Cruise's Digger, called 2026's biggest bomb, opened to about $8M domestically, slightly above The Social Reckoning's projected $6M.
